en.title: Malabar Beach
en.summary: Observe the boat ramp and coastline within Long Bay, then enjoy a coffee after a short walk through the park.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Located on the inner side of Long Bay, Malabar Beach is distinct from the open, expansive stretch of nearby Maroubra Beach, thanks to the unique shape of the bay and its surrounding high cliffs. On the northern side, you’ll find a boat ramp and maritime rescue facilities, while the southern shoreline features rock pools and a coastal landscape that runs beneath a golf course. For a casual visit, you can simply stick to the beach and public rest areas without needing to venture onto the longer trails along the headlands.

The surrounding neighborhood blends residential life with maritime activity; there are no large-scale commercial tourist developments here. The real appeal lies in the shifting scale: up close, you have a small sandy shore and a space for boat operations, while in the distance, you can take in the opening of Long Bay framed by high ground on either side. By observing the boat ramp, the beach, and the public green space as distinct elements, you can better appreciate how this area serves both as a recreational bay for local residents and as a functional hub for maritime services.
## How to explore
1. Start at the public area near the beach off Fishermans Road, and take note of the layout of the boat ramp in relation to the sandy shore. Choose a walking path that doesn’t obstruct boats, vehicles, or rescue operations; identify your return route before heading onto the dry sand.
2. Take a leisurely walk along the beach and the public path behind it, observing how the bay transitions from the shallow inner shore toward its open mouth. Turn back when you reach the rocky coastline or where the path narrows. When taking photos, avoid standing in the middle of the boat ramp, and do not scramble over the reefs in search of a better vantage point. 3. Return to the public seating areas or green spaces to rest, then take a short stroll along the footpaths near Bay Parade to grab a coffee. If you wish to see the rock pools on the southern side, please use the designated land-based paths and view them from accessible public vantage points. This route does not connect to the longer Malabar Headland trail, nor should the golf course be used as a public shortcut.
## Timing
Allow 45 minutes for taking in the bay views and a short walk; extend this to 90 minutes if you’d like to stop for a coffee or explore the official paths on the southern side. The beach is small, making it better suited for relaxation. Please note that the extra walking required for navigating slopes or reaching the rock pools cannot be accommodated within a brief, quick visit. After dark this is a shore-side walk and a chance to sit and listen to the water. Stay on visible public paths close to the approach; do not swim, enter rock platforms or continue onto unlit cliffs or bush tracks. Lifeguard patrols, bathing facilities, toilets and car parks have separate hours; public shore access does not imply a patrolled swim or an open car park.
## Getting there and costs
Navigate to "Malabar Beach, Fishermans Road." If arriving by public transport, walk from the nearest stop. If driving, please use only legal parking spaces; ensure that boat ramps, emergency access points, and residential driveways remain clear. Access to the beach is free and requires no booking; costs for food, drinks, parking, and transport are separate.
## Nearby food
You can find coffee and light meals around Bay Parade; if you plan to have a picnic, please bring your own water and snacks. Dining options are more limited here than at larger, more popular beaches, so it is best not to hunt for a specific menu—simply check which establishments are open and what they offer before deciding whether to dine in or take your food to go.
en.tips: There are no lifeguards on duty here; please enjoy the view from the shore. Be mindful of boat traffic and emergency vehicles, and do not cross any safety barriers or fencing. Wear shoes with good grip, and bring water and sun protection. If you choose to walk toward the rock pools, avoid slippery edges and do not enter the golf course grounds.

items.summary: 在皮尔蒙特的社区公园短暂停留，沿公共步道散步。
items.guide:
## 简介
Cadi Park是Pyrmont Bowman Street附近朝向港湾的社区绿地，由Place Management NSW管理。它所处的Pyrmont曾长期以码头、工厂、木材与仓储等滨水行业为背景，后来逐渐转为住宅、办公与公共步行空间；今天坐在草地看港湾，也是在看这片工业岸线向日常生活空间的变化。

这里没有大型纪念建筑或复杂游乐线路，重点是草地、座位与海港之间的距离感。公寓楼构成背后的城市边界，水面和船只则让视野打开，适合把一段忙碌街区里的散步收在这里。看风景、读几页书或短坐，都比刻意寻找“必玩设施”更符合这块小绿地的尺度。
## 这样逛
1. 到74 Bowman Street附近的公共绿地，先认清 Cadi Park 的场地边界，再从开放步道进入；周边住宅庭院和门禁区域不属于公园。
2. 沿草地外侧走一段，在朝向港湾的位置停下，比较水面、船只与 Pyrmont 城市建筑的层次；想拍照可以先绕半圈找角度，不必直接走到水边。
3. 找一处空座位坐十分钟，听水边与街区声音；休息后按来路或仍开放的公共路径返回，让这次出门成为一段容易完成的散步，而不是赶景点。
## 时间怎么用
20分钟走一圈、看看港景；60分钟可带一本书或饮水，慢坐并观察光线变化。公园体量不大，不必安排满一小时连续步行。 夜间也可沿可通行的公共步道或建筑外侧散步，挑能看清台阶与路面的路线往返；室内、泳池、活动区域和园内设施按各自开放安排。
## 怎么去与花费
地址74 Bowman Street, Pyrmont；可按地图选择附近轻轨或公交后步行。进园后按公共步道指示选择路线。
## 附近餐饮
可回Bowman Street、Harris Street方向寻找咖啡与简餐，按自己的返程路线选一段即可。公园适合带水短坐，想吃正餐则先完成滨水散步再回街区。
items.tips: 官方列出的主要设施是座椅和港景，带好水，不攀越岸边限制设施；管理方为Place Management NSW，现场施工和活动提示优先。

en.title: Cadi Park
en.summary: Make a short stop at this community park in Pyrmont and take a walk along the public footpath.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Cadi Park is a community green space overlooking the harbor near Bowman Street in Pyrmont; it is managed by Place Management NSW. Pyrmont, the area where this site is located, was once defined by waterfront industries—docks, factories, timber yards, and warehouses—before gradually transforming into a space for residences, offices, and public pedestrian pathways. Today, as you sit on the grass overlooking the harbor, you are witnessing the evolution of this former industrial shoreline into a setting for everyday life.

There are no grand monuments or elaborate recreational attractions here; the focus lies in the interplay between the lawns, the seating, and the harbor. Apartment buildings form an urban backdrop, while the expanse of water and the passing boats open up the view—an ideal destination to conclude a stroll through the bustling city streets. Whether you’re taking in the scenery, reading a few pages of a book, or simply resting for a while, these activities suit the scale of this small green space far better than the pursuit of "must-see" attractions.
## How to explore
1. Upon arriving at the public green space near 74 Bowman Street, identify the boundaries of Cadi Park and enter via the accessible public pathways. Please note that the private courtyards and gated residential areas nearby are not part of the park.
2. Walk along the edge of the lawn and pause at a spot facing the harbor. Observe the layers formed by the water, the boats, and the urban architecture of Pyrmont. If you wish to take photos, explore the perimeter to find the best angle—there is no need to walk all the way to the water’s edge.
3. Find an available seat and linger for ten minutes, listening to the sounds of the waterfront and the surrounding neighborhood. When you’re ready, head back the way you came—or via another open public path—ensuring your outing remains a relaxed, manageable walk rather than a rushed sightseeing mission.
## Timing
A full loop takes about 20 minutes, offering plenty of harbor views. For a longer visit—perhaps an hour—bring a book or a drink, sit back, and watch the shifting light. As the park is quite compact, there is no need to plan for a full hour of continuous walking. Evening visits use public paths and building exteriors where you can see the surface and steps clearly. Interiors, pools, event zones and other facilities retain their own access arrangements.
## Getting there and costs
Address: 74 Bowman Street, Pyrmont. You can reach the area by light rail or bus, followed by a short walk. Once inside, follow the signs for the public pedestrian paths.
## Nearby food
For coffee or a light meal, head back toward Bowman Street or Harris Street; you can easily find options along your return route. The park is a suitable spot for a brief rest—bring some water along. If you’re looking for a full meal, it’s best to complete your waterfront stroll first and then head back into the city blocks.
en.tips: The primary features officially listed are seating and harbor views. Please bring your own water, and do not climb over any barriers along the waterfront. The site is managed by Place Management NSW; please prioritize any notices regarding on-site construction or events.

items.guide:
## 简介
Woolloomooloo的Finger Wharf于1910年代建成，长条建筑从岸边伸入海湾，形状让它得到“手指码头”的俗称。大型木结构、重复的仓储开口和很长的侧立面，源自货物装卸与港口管理需要，而非最初就为了酒店和餐饮设计。码头曾经参与羊毛出口、航运和旅客活动，后来在港口功能迁移中逐渐转向新的使用。站在岸边看其尺度，比只在餐厅门口拍照更能理解旧港口设施占据城市空间的方式。

今天建筑内结合酒店、餐饮和私人住宅，是典型的适应性再利用案例。遗产外壳保留下来，内部功能却已不是可以任意穿行的公共仓库；游客能走的主要是岸边公共路段和明确允许的外侧步道。这里与CBD仅隔着Domain一带的高差和绿地，海湾却较安静，适合比较现代城市、山坡道路与旧码头的关系。本条不要求进入酒店或消费，也不会把私人住宅端点、停船区域和服务通道算作免费必看内容。
## 这样逛
1. 从Cowper Wharf Road岸边开始，先站远一点看Finger Wharf的完整长度、屋顶和门洞重复节奏；留意公共通道与酒店、餐厅入口的区别。
2. 沿允许开放的外侧步道走一段，观察木结构、泊船与海湾景色，遇私人区域或服务标识便折返，不为走到“最尖端”穿越住户通道。
3. 回到岸边公共路段看码头侧面与周围坡地，再找座位或咖啡休息。若继续到美术馆，按公共街道和台阶指示上坡，另留体力与时间。
## 时间怎么用
60分钟看整体、走开放侧边并休息；90分钟适合摄影和一杯咖啡。路线轻松但与Domain之间有坡度或台阶，不把“地图看着近”当作完全平坦的连接。 夜间也可沿可通行的公共步道或建筑外侧散步，挑能看清台阶与路面的路线往返；室内、泳池、活动区域和园内设施按各自开放安排。
## 怎么去与花费
地址6 Cowper Wharf Roadway一带。从Kings Cross或St James步行接入，路线有高差；自驾停车按周边时限和收费。公共岸边免费，餐厅、酒店和停车另付。
## 附近餐饮
码头餐厅以坐下用餐为主，可先看菜单；想轻便一点在Cowper Wharf Road和周边街道选择咖啡、简餐，消费不是步行条件。
items.tips: 公共岸边与私人码头分开，近水看好儿童；勿进入系泊区、居民门和酒店客房通道。

en.title: Woolloomooloo Finger Wharf
en.summary: From the public waterfront, observe the scale of the long timber pier, and take in the views of the bay and the hillside streetscape as you walk along.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Built in the 1910s, the Finger Wharf in Woolloomooloo—a long structure extending from the shore into the bay—earns its name from its shape. Its massive timber framework, repetitive warehouse openings, and elongated side facades were originally designed for cargo handling and port operations, rather than for hospitality or dining. Once a hub for wool exports, shipping, and passenger travel, the wharf transitioned to new uses as port functions relocated elsewhere. Viewing its scale from the shore offers a much better understanding of how these historic port facilities occupy urban space than simply snapping a photo in front of a restaurant entrance.

Today, the structure houses a mix of hotels, restaurants, and private residences—a classic example of adaptive reuse. While the historic shell remains, the interior is no longer a public warehouse open to free movement; visitors are generally restricted to the public path along the shoreline and designated walkways on the outer edges. Separated from the CBD by the elevation changes and green space of The Domain, this bay area remains relatively quiet—an ideal vantage point to observe the interplay between the modern city, hillside streets, and the old wharf. This entry does not require you to enter the hotel or make a purchase; furthermore, private residential areas, boat mooring zones, and service corridors are not considered part of the accessible public experience.
## How to explore
1. Starting from the shore along Cowper Wharf Road, take a step back to appreciate the full length of the Finger Wharf, its roofline, and the rhythmic repetition of its doorways. Pay attention to the distinction between the public thoroughfares and the entrances to the hotels and restaurants. 2. Follow the accessible outer walkway to take in the timber structures, moored boats, and bay views. Turn back if you encounter signs marking private areas or service zones; do not cross into residential pathways in an attempt to reach the "very tip" of the pier.
3. Return to the public waterfront area to view the side of the pier and the surrounding slopes, then find a seat or a café to take a break. If you plan to continue on to the art gallery, follow the signs along the public streets and stairs—just be sure to set aside enough time and energy for the uphill walk.
## Timing
Allow 60 minutes for a general overview, a walk along the accessible side, and a short break; 90 minutes is ideal if you want to take photos and enjoy a coffee. While the route is leisurely, there are slopes and stairs connecting it to The Domain—don’t assume that a short distance on the map implies a completely flat path. Evening visits use public paths and building exteriors where you can see the surface and steps clearly. Interiors, pools, event zones and other facilities retain their own access arrangements.
## Getting there and costs
Located in the vicinity of 6 Cowper Wharf Roadway. You can reach it on foot from Kings Cross or St James, though the route involves changes in elevation. If driving, be mindful of local parking time limits and fees. The public waterfront is free to access, but restaurants, hotels, and parking facilities require payment.
## Nearby food
The restaurants on the pier are primarily for sit-down dining—feel free to check the menus first. For a more casual experience, explore the cafés and light-meal options along Cowper Wharf Road and the surrounding streets; purchasing food or drink is not a requirement for walking through the area.
en.tips: The public waterfront is separate from the private piers. Keep a close eye on children near the water, and avoid entering mooring zones, private residential entrances, or hotel guest areas.

items.title: 牛奶海滩
items.summary: 在历史庄园下方的小海湾看城市轮廓，沿公共路径短走后返回。
items.guide:
## 简介
Milk Beach位于Vaucluse的Hermitage Foreshore一带，海湾上方是Strickland Estate。沙岸面积不大，但隔着海港能看到城市和海港大桥方向的轮廓；草坡、砂岩与水面把这里组织成几个不同高度，适合坐下看景，而不是把每一片相邻海湾都赶完。

庄园中的Carrara别墅建于1856年，后来以Strickland House为人熟知，曾承担不同的公共用途。今天海湾、开放庄园公共区域与海滨步道构成连续的风景，建筑背景让单纯看海多了一层历史感。房屋内部与专门导览并非普通岸边散步内容，游览以实际开放的公共路径和草坡为范围。
## 这样逛
1. 从Vaucluse Road一侧按Strickland Estate与Milk Beach的公共标识接近，先在上方看海湾和返回方向。沿明确开放路径下行，不穿相邻私人花园；带野餐物品时先考虑回程上坡。
2. 到沙岸或允许休息的公共草坡看海港，留意城市轮廓、近处水面与两端砂岩的层次。小海湾空间有限，选一处不挡通行的位置停留即可，不在潮湿岩面找更低机位，也不攀爬历史建筑。
3. 沿正式海滨步道向一侧走到第一个合适观景位置后折返，再从原公共路径返回上方。想更轻松可省去这段，把时间留给坐着看船；Nielsen Park和整条Hermitage Foreshore应另留路程，不自动当成返回捷径。
## 时间怎么用
45分钟看海湾和草坡；90分钟可增加一个步道观景点、休息与建筑外观。沙岸宽度会随水位变化，留在开放陆路也能看景。返程上坡和走回公交站的时间另留。
## 怎么去与花费
导航Milk Beach, Strickland Estate, Vaucluse，公交至附近道路后沿公共连接步行。街边停车有限，依时限和标识使用合法车位，不占住宅车道。个人公共岸边到访无需预约，交通、停车、餐饮及专门导览另计。
## 附近餐饮
海滩没有集中餐饮设施，先准备水与简单点心较方便；结束后按回程方向在Vaucluse或Rose Bay用餐。不要为找餐馆临时把整条海滨步道走完，也不把庄园内部当成必然开放的咖啡空间。
items.tips: 公共路径有坡道与台阶，穿抓地鞋、轻装步行。国家公园遵守禁烟及宠物限制；海湾小，拍照和野餐给其他人留空间，所有包装随身带走。

en.title: Milk Beach
en.summary: Enjoy views of the city skyline from the small cove below the historic estate, then return via the public footpath.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Milk Beach is located along the Hermitage Foreshore in Vaucluse, with the Strickland Estate situated above the bay. While the sandy beach itself is small, it offers views across the harbor toward the city skyline and the Harbour Bridge. With its grassy slopes, sandstone formations, and water, the area is structured across several levels—perfect for sitting back and taking in the scenery, rather than rushing to visit every single bay in the vicinity. Built in 1856, the Carrara villa—later better known as Strickland House—has served various public functions over the years. Today, the cove, the open grounds, and the coastal walking path form a continuous landscape, where the architectural backdrop adds a layer of historical depth to the simple act of gazing out at the sea. Please note that the building’s interior and specialized guided tours are not part of a standard casual visit; access is limited to the designated public paths and grassy slopes.
## How to explore
1. Approach via Vaucluse Road, following the public signs for "Strickland Estate" and "Milk Beach." Before descending, take a moment to view the cove and the path you have just traveled. Follow the clearly marked public path downward—do not enter adjacent private gardens. If you are carrying items for a picnic, keep in mind that the return journey will involve an uphill walk.
2. Once you reach the sandy shore or the public grassy slopes, take in the harbor view—observe the city skyline, the water nearby, and the sandstone formations at either end of the cove. As the space is limited, please choose a spot that does not obstruct the path. Do not venture onto wet, slippery rocks for a lower vantage point, and please do not climb on the historical structures.
3. You may follow the formal coastal path to a suitable viewpoint before turning back to rejoin the main public path. If you prefer a more relaxed visit, you can skip this section and spend your time simply sitting and watching the boats. Please note that Nielsen Park and the broader Hermitage Foreshore are separate destinations; do not assume they serve as a shortcut back to your starting point.
## Timing
Allow 45 minutes to explore the cove and grassy slopes; a 90-minute visit allows time for an additional viewpoint along the coastal path, a rest, and a look at the building’s exterior. The width of the sandy beach varies with the tide, but the views remain accessible from the open paths above. Remember to set aside extra time for the uphill return walk and the trek back to the bus stop.
## Getting there and costs
Navigate to "Milk Beach, Strickland Estate, Vaucluse." If arriving by bus, follow the public access paths from the nearby stop. Street parking is limited; please use only legal, designated parking spaces—observing all time limits and signage—and do not block private residential driveways. No reservation is required for a casual visit to the shoreline; please note that transportation, parking, refreshments, and specialized guided tours are separate arrangements.
## Nearby food
There are no centralized dining facilities at the beach, so it is best to bring your own water and light snacks. Alternatively, you can dine in Vaucluse or Rose Bay on your way back. Do not feel compelled to walk the entire coastal path just to find a restaurant, and please note that the historic estate is not necessarily open to the public as a café or dining space.
en.tips: The public path includes slopes and stairs; please wear shoes with good grip and travel light. As this is a national park, smoking and pets are prohibited. The cove is small, so please be mindful of others when taking photos or picnicking, and ensure you take all your trash with you when you leave.

items.title: 鹦鹉岛 Wareamah
items.summary: 先看船班，再按高处流放犯遗迹与低处船坞两段读岛屿历史。
items.guide:
## 简介
Cockatoo Island / Wareamah在悉尼海港的河流交汇附近，岛上的砂岩、监狱遗迹、船坞和工业大厅，把几种截然不同的历史叠在一起。1839至1869年间这里作为流放犯监禁场所，保留下来的相关建筑在2010年与其他澳洲流放犯遗址一起列入世界遗产；后来长期的造船、修船和工程活动，则留下了尺度巨大的机械空间与码头设施。与市中心修复精致的砂岩街景相比，它更容易让人感受到劳动、隔离和工业生产的实际空间。

岛分高处平台与低处船坞区，坡道、台阶和粗糙地面决定了路线强度。免费登岛不代表渡轮免费，也不代表每座厂房、隧道或活动场地随时能进。普通参观可以沿标示清楚的自助路线看开放遗迹，游客中心提供地图与帮助；付费导览、露营、住宿和展演是另外安排。岛上参观最需要先想好返程船班，尤其不是所有时段都有与到达时相同的频率，停留时间应给走回码头和候船留下余量。
## 这样逛
1. 下船后先到游客中心附近看地图、开放提示与返程船班，圈定高处遗迹和低处船坞两段路线，别一上岸就直走到最远的工业角落。
2. 体力允许时先上高处看流放犯建筑与港面，再沿开放坡道回低处，阅读遗迹用途说明；行动不便可优先低处路线，并问工作人员适用通道。
3. 按标示看船坞、厂房和旧机械空间的外观或开放内部，遇封闭门和作业区直接绕开。结束前回到码头附近休息，至少提早留出找泊位与等船的时间。
## 时间怎么用
2小时看主要遗迹，3小时可加慢读解说与午餐。本条采用10–16点参观窗口，渡轮往返和等候另计；不要等到岛上停留时间用完才查最后一班船。
## 怎么去与花费
从Circular Quay或其他当前有服务的码头乘公共渡轮，登船前确认屏幕确实停Cockatoo Island。岛上普通入场免费，渡轮、导览、住宿和活动另付；岛上没有普通游客驾车通行。
## 附近餐饮
可自带食物和无酒精饮料，使用允许的休息区；岛上咖啡店各有营业安排，晚到时不依赖完整热食菜单。
items.tips: 穿防滑鞋，带水、遮阳和外层；坡道、旧工业地面与近水区域照看儿童。不要攀机械或进入关闭隧道。

en.title: Cockatoo Island / Wareamah
en.summary: Check the ferry schedule first, then explore the island’s history by visiting both the convict-era sites on the higher ground and the dockyards on the lower ground.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Cockatoo Island (Wareamah), located near the confluence of waterways in Sydney Harbour, layers together distinct historical eras through its sandstone formations, remnants of a penal colony, shipyards, and industrial halls. Between 1839 and 1869, the island served as a convict prison; the surviving structures from this period were inscribed as a World Heritage site in 2010, alongside other Australian convict sites. Subsequent long-term shipbuilding, repair, and engineering activities left behind massive industrial spaces, machinery, and dock facilities. Unlike the meticulously restored sandstone streetscapes of the city center, this site offers a more visceral sense of the spaces once defined by labor, isolation, and industrial production.

The island is divided into an upper plateau and a lower shipyard area, with slopes, stairs, and uneven terrain influencing the physical demands of your visit. While entry to the island is free, ferry fares still apply, and not every building, tunnel, or event space is open to the public at all times. For a general visit, you can follow clearly marked self-guided routes to explore the accessible heritage sites; the visitor center provides maps and further assistance. Paid guided tours, camping, overnight accommodation, and special events are arranged separately. When planning your visit, be sure to check the return ferry schedule—service frequency may vary throughout the day—and allow ample time to walk back to the wharf and wait for your boat.
## How to explore
1. Upon disembarking, head to the area near the Visitor Centre to check the map, information on open areas, and return ferry schedules. Plan your visit by focusing on two distinct zones: the historic sites on the higher ground and the dockyards on the lower ground—avoid walking straight to the furthest industrial corners as soon as you arrive.
2. If you are physically able, start by heading to the higher ground to view the convict-era structures and the harbour vista, then make your way back down via the accessible ramps, taking time to read the descriptions of the various sites. If you have limited mobility, prioritize the lower-ground route and ask staff about accessible paths.
3. Follow the signage to explore the exteriors—or accessible interiors—of the dockyards, workshops, and areas housing old machinery. Steer clear of any closed doors or active work zones. Before concluding your visit, return to the vicinity of the wharf to rest, and ensure you leave enough time to locate your departure point and wait for the ferry.
## Timing
Allow 2 hours to see the main historic sites, or 3 hours if you wish to take your time reading the interpretive signage and having lunch. This itinerary assumes a visit between 10:00 and 16:00; ferry travel time and waiting periods are separate. Do not wait until your allotted time on the island has run out to check the schedule for the final ferry.
## Getting there and costs
Take a public ferry from Circular Quay or another wharf currently serving the island; confirm on the display screen that the vessel stops at Cockatoo Island before boarding. General admission to the island is free, but there are separate charges for ferries, guided tours, accommodation, and specific activities. Private vehicles are not permitted on the island.
## Nearby food
You are welcome to bring your own food and non-alcoholic beverages to enjoy in designated rest areas. Please note that the island’s cafés have their own operating hours; if you arrive late, do not rely on the availability of a full hot-food menu.
en.tips: Wear non-slip footwear, and bring water, sun protection, and an extra layer of clothing. Keep a close eye on children near ramps, old industrial surfaces, and the waterfront. Do not climb on machinery or enter tunnels that are closed to the public.

items.title: 穆雷罗斯泳区与红叶海滩
items.summary: 从花园台阶下到港湾，沿陆侧看泳区、帆船与Double Bay景色。
items.guide:
## 简介
Murray Rose Pool是Double Bay的一处港湾潮汐围网泳区，岸边连着常称Redleaf Beach的小沙岸，上方是花园与New South Head Road。它并不是室内游泳馆，围网、浮台、沙滩和海港水面彼此相连；从高处花园到海滨的台阶，让抵达过程带来很清楚的高差变化。

泳区原名Redleaf Pool，Woollahra Council于2012年决定以奥运游泳选手Murray Rose命名。今天它与周边花园、公共座位及海滨售卖亭一起构成居民休闲空间。普通到访可以只看港景、观察围网和船只、在陆侧休息。
## 这样逛
1. 从536 New South Head Road公共入口进入，先在上方花园看港湾和下行台阶，确认返回方向。这里从主路到海边有高差，推车或行动不便者先看正式路线，不把台阶当成可以轻松拖行装备的坡道。
2. 沿开放公共路径下到海滨，从陆侧看围网、浮台与Double Bay水面。沙地与通道都不宽，选择一处干燥宽位停留；拍照别挡住泳客与公共设施的通行，不需要走到浮台外侧才能看海。
3. 在公共座位或允许休息的地方坐一会儿，再沿原路径慢慢返回上方。想加一点绿色，可在开放花园公共路径短走，比较高处与海边两种视角；附近画廊和专门展览有独立开放安排，本次不自动包含入馆。
## 时间怎么用
45分钟适合花园到海滨往返和看景；90分钟可加休息、咖啡及上方短走。返程有台阶，别把最后几分钟全留给上坡。夏季周末人较多，早些到访更容易找到公共休息位置。 夜间以岸边散步、听海和休息为主，沿入口附近能看清路面的公共路径往返；不下水、不走礁石、崖边或无照明的延伸山径。救生巡逻、浴场设施和停车场有各自时间，不能把可到岸边等同于有人巡逻或可夜泳。
## 怎么去与花费
导航Murray Rose Pool, 536 New South Head Road, Double Bay。公交可到主路附近，渡轮到Double Bay后仍需街道步行与台阶下行。周边车位有限，按街边或公共停车场时限使用。个人公共岸边到访无需预约，咖啡、交通和停车另计。
## 附近餐饮
海滨售卖亭有适合短停的饮品与简餐，可完成下行散步后再决定是否消费。需要更多选择则回Double Bay商区，把较完整的午餐放在返程上坡之后；不要端着热食上下台阶或占用换衣、淋浴通道。
items.tips: 这里没有救生员服务，围网不代表有人看护；本次以陆侧到访为主。台阶和泳区旁湿地面会滑，穿抓地鞋。花园、泳区和议事厅附近宠物规则不同，按标识走，不进入禁止区域。

en.title: Murray Rose Pool & Redleaf Beach
en.summary: Descend the garden stairs toward the harbor; from the shore, you can take in views of the swimming enclosure, sailboats, and the Double Bay area.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Murray Rose Pool is a tidal, netted swimming enclosure located in Double Bay. It sits adjacent to a small sandy beach—commonly known as Redleaf Beach—with gardens and New South Head Road situated on the higher ground above. This is not an indoor swimming facility; the netted area, floating pontoons, beach, and harbor waters are all interconnected. A set of stairs leads down from the gardens to the shoreline, creating a distinct change in elevation as you arrive.

Originally called Redleaf Pool, the site was renamed in 2012 by the Woollahra Council in honor of Olympic swimmer Murray Rose. Today, the pool, along with its surrounding gardens, public seating, and a kiosk, serves as a recreational space for the local community. Visitors are welcome to simply enjoy the harbor views, observe the netted enclosure and passing boats, or relax on the shore.
## How to explore
1. Enter via the public access point at 536 New South Head Road. From the gardens above, take in the view of the harbor and note the stairs leading down—this will help you orient yourself for the return trip. Please be aware of the significant elevation change between the main road and the shoreline; if you are using a stroller or have limited mobility, check for the designated accessible route, as the stairs are not suitable for wheeling equipment.
2. Follow the public path down to the waterfront, where you can view the netted enclosure, floating pontoons, and the waters of Double Bay. As the beach and pathways are quite narrow, please find a dry, spacious spot to settle. Be mindful not to obstruct swimmers or others using the public facilities; you do not need to venture onto the outer side of the pontoons to enjoy the view of the harbor.
3. Take a moment to sit on the public benches or in other designated resting areas before making your way back up. If you’d like to add a touch of greenery to your visit, take a short stroll through the gardens to compare the perspectives from the upper level and the shoreline. Please note that nearby galleries and special exhibitions operate on their own schedules and are not included as part of this visit.
## Timing
Allow 45 minutes for a round trip between the gardens and the shoreline, including time to take in the scenery. A 90-minute visit allows extra time for resting, grabbing a coffee, and exploring the gardens above. Remember that the return journey involves stairs, so be sure to leave enough time for the climb back up. The area can get quite busy on summer weekends; arriving early makes it easier to secure a spot to sit and relax. After dark this is a shore-side walk and a chance to sit and listen to the water. Stay on visible public paths close to the approach; do not swim, enter rock platforms or continue onto unlit cliffs or bush tracks. Lifeguard patrols, bathing facilities, toilets and car parks have separate hours; public shore access does not imply a patrolled swim or an open car park.
## Getting there and costs
Navigate to Murray Rose Pool, 536 New South Head Road, Double Bay. The site is accessible via bus (alight near the main road) or ferry (arriving at Double Bay, followed by a walk along the streets and a descent via stairs). On-street parking and public car parks are limited; please adhere to the posted time restrictions. No reservation is required for public access to the waterfront; expenses for refreshments, transport, and parking are separate.
## Nearby food
A kiosk by the waterfront offers drinks and light snacks—feel free to decide whether to make a purchase after your walk down. For a wider variety of options, head back to the Double Bay commercial precinct; it is best to enjoy a full lunch after the return climb uphill. Please refrain from carrying hot food while navigating the stairs, and avoid blocking areas designated for changing or showering.
en.tips: There are no lifeguards on duty here; the presence of a perimeter fence does not imply supervision. This visit focuses on the shoreline area. Be aware that the stairs and the wet ground near the swimming enclosure can be slippery—wear shoes with good traction. Rules regarding pets vary across the garden, swimming area, and the vicinity of the council chambers; please follow the posted signage and avoid entering restricted zones.

items.title: 温特沃斯公园
items.summary: 探索内城公共绿地；体育比赛或其他活动另行安排。
items.guide:
## 简介
Wentworth Park建在Blackwattle Creek河口旧沼泽的填土地上。19世纪岸边工业污染之后，填土工程于1876至1880年进行，1882年公园与运动场逐渐成形，并以William Charles Wentworth命名。这里从一开始就兼具公共娱乐与体育功能，社区活动与运动始终是它的重要背景。

穿过场地的铁路高架桥留下了货运时代的印记，如今则与内西轻轨相连。开阔球场、草地、野餐座位和周边道路形成很直接的城市公园景观：既能看历史基础设施，也能观察今天居民如何使用公共空间。此次只逛园内开放绿地，正式体育活动与中央场馆另行安排。
## 这样逛
1. 从 Wentworth Park Road 或靠近轻轨的一侧进入公共绿地，先看当天球场是否比赛、草地是否封闭，再选择不穿越比赛区域的边缘路线。
2. 沿运动场外围走一段，看看铁路高架桥与宽阔绿地的组合，走到有树荫和座椅的位置稍作停留；如果想活动，可在空闲的健身站按标识做简单伸展。
3. 回到公共野餐区或树下休息，带孩子时可看现场开放的遮阴游乐区。最后由开放步道返回，赛狗、售票活动及看台内部不属于这次公园散步。
## 时间怎么用
30分钟走外围一段加休息；60分钟可多走一圈并做轻量活动。球场预约、正式比赛与其他活动另按运营方安排，按现场开放和预约安排使用。 夜间也可沿可通行的公共步道或建筑外侧散步，挑能看清台阶与路面的路线往返；室内、泳池、活动区域和园内设施按各自开放安排。
## 怎么去与花费
官方建议在 Wentworth Park 轻轨站下车后沿 Wattle Street 一侧步行；实际进园路线与站台出口按地图确认。
## 附近餐饮
可向Glebe Point Road找咖啡与餐饮，或沿自己下一程方向到Ultimo。带简单点心时使用公共休息区，运动进行中别坐在飞球或出入口位置。
items.tips: 东西两侧的遛狗规则不同：西侧部分空间允许脱绳，东侧须牵绳；游乐区和烧烤区不允许狗进入。避开飞球和运动场边界，不用球场最短直线穿行。

en.title: Wentworth Park
en.summary: Explore the public green spaces in the inner city; sporting matches and other events are handled separately.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Wentworth Park was constructed on reclaimed land—formerly a swamp at the mouth of Blackwattle Creek. Following industrial pollution along the shoreline in the 19th century, land reclamation took place between 1876 and 1880. By 1882, the park and sports grounds had taken shape, named in honor of William Charles Wentworth. From its inception, the site has served both public recreation and sporting purposes, with community activities and athletics remaining a core part of its identity.

The railway viaduct spanning the grounds serves as a relic of the freight era and is now integrated with the Inner West Light Rail. With its expansive sports fields, lawns, picnic seating, and surrounding pathways, the site presents a quintessential urban park landscape—offering a glimpse into both historical infrastructure and the way contemporary residents utilize public space. This visit is limited to the open green spaces within the park; formal sporting events and the central stadium facilities are separate matters.
## How to explore
1. Enter the public green space from Wentworth Park Road or the side near the light rail station. First, check whether any matches are taking place or if the playing fields are closed; then, choose a route along the perimeter that avoids crossing through active playing areas.
2. Walk along the outer edge of the sports fields, taking in the view of the railway viaduct set against the expansive green space. Pause for a while in a shaded area with seating; if you’d like to get active, feel free to use the available fitness stations for some simple stretches, following the posted instructions.
3. Return to the public picnic area or rest under the trees. If you are with children, you can make use of the shaded playground areas. Conclude your visit by following the designated walking paths. Please note that greyhound racing, ticketed events, and the interior of the grandstands are not part of this park stroll.
## Timing
A 30-minute visit allows for a walk along the perimeter with some time to rest; a 60-minute visit allows for an extra lap and some light physical activity. Bookings for sports fields, formal matches, and other events are managed by the operators; please follow on-site signage and booking arrangements. Evening visits use public paths and building exteriors where you can see the surface and steps clearly. Interiors, pools, event zones and other facilities retain their own access arrangements.
## Getting there and costs
It is recommended to alight at the Wentworth Park light rail station and walk along the Wattle Street side. Please consult the map to confirm your specific entry route and the appropriate station exit.
## Nearby food
For coffee and dining, head toward Glebe Point Road, or continue in the direction of your next destination toward Ultimo. If you have brought light snacks, please enjoy them in the public rest areas. When sports are in progress, avoid sitting in the path of stray balls or near the entrances and exits of the playing fields.
en.tips: Dog-walking rules differ between the eastern and western sides of the park: off-leash activity is permitted in certain areas on the western side, while dogs must be kept on a leash on the eastern side. Dogs are not permitted in playground or barbecue areas. Please stay clear of stray balls and the boundaries of the sports fields, and avoid taking shortcuts directly across the playing areas.

items.title: 雷德芬街区
items.summary: 铁路社区、市政老建筑和街区餐饮串成一段有内容的散步。
items.guide:
## 简介
Redfern的地名来自1817年获地的外科医生William Redfern。铁路和Eveleigh工坊带来的工作机会推动了19世纪的街区发展，1870年的Redfern Town Hall与后来的邮局等公共建筑，见证这里曾经独立的市政生活。沿Redfern Street走，可以看到砂岩公共建筑、窄店屋、排屋和后来开出的咖啡馆并列；这并不是一个把旧立面全部做成博物馆的区域，街道仍在服务居民的日常。

Redfern也是悉尼重要的原住民社区与社会运动记忆所在地，移民、工人、艺术与音乐文化让街区具有鲜明的公共性。到这里不只是找一面壁画拍照，更适合慢慢看主街如何与车站、社区空间和公园相连。从车站商业段走到Town Hall，在Redfern Park边休息，再回主街吃一餐，能把铁路社区、市政记忆和今天的生活连在一起。
## 这样逛
1. 从车站一端进入Redfern Street。先沿商铺连续的一侧慢走，看咖啡馆、小餐厅与旧店屋的关系。碰到壁画可在公共人行道停下来读内容，不把社区人物仅当成摄影背景；不进入围栏内、空地或看起来像捷径的私人通道。
2. 走到Pitt Street转角。观察Town Hall的对称立面、拱形开口与砂岩细部，再到Redfern Park边坐一会。这里适合把前半段所见串起来：车站带来的人流、市政建筑的规模、住家与公园的距离，都能帮助理解这片老社区。
3. 回主街吃一顿。想简单可找咖啡馆或面店，想晚餐就看RaRa等当前有位的店；顺路到Breadfern买一份烘焙点心也能结束。吃完回车站，不必再越过铁路去South Eveleigh把两个不同片区强行连成赶路。
## 时间怎么用
30分钟可走一小段主街并休息；想逛店或用餐可留120分钟左右，另加候位时间。公共街道昼夜可走，店铺、拱廊、市场和餐厅各按自己的营业时间，深夜可以只散步，不必消费。晚上沿人行道和正式过街点往返，先认好返程车站；遇已关门的商场或私人通道就沿公共道路绕行。
## 怎么去与花费
Redfern Station出站后按路牌找Redfern Street商业段；不同站口到主街的距离不完全相同。也可搭公交到Regent Street一带。公共道路散步无需预约，馆舍活动和餐厅分别管理；餐费、停车与车票按实际消费。
## 附近餐饮
拉面适合想要一碗完整热食时，先选汤底和辣度，再看是否需要加小菜；咖啡馆主食则更适合想边吃边歇的人。烘焙可以留作饭后小点，买一份自己喜欢的即可。若想晚餐配酒，街区还有小酒吧可选，饮品与正餐都不需要连吃几家才能体验。
items.tips: 经过社区活动、宗教场所或人物壁画时保持礼貌，拍到近距离人物先征得同意。Town Hall这里只看公共外观，不默认任何房间、婚礼或活动都可旁观。

en.title: Redfern Street Village
en.summary: This route weaves together the area’s railway heritage, historic civic architecture, and local dining spots, making for a truly engaging walk.
en.guide:
## Introduction
The name "Redfern" originates from William Redfern, a surgeon who was granted land in the area in 1817. The arrival of the railway and the Eveleigh Workshops fueled the development of this neighborhood in the 19th century. Public landmarks—such as the Redfern Town Hall (built in 1870) and the former post office—stand as testaments to a time when Redfern functioned as an independent municipality. Walking along Redfern Street, you will see a mix of sandstone public buildings, narrow shophouses, terrace homes, and contemporary cafés. This is not a district turned into a museum of preserved façades; the streets remain very much a part of daily life for local residents.

Redfern also holds deep significance as a hub for Sydney’s Indigenous community and a site of social activism. A rich tapestry of immigrant history, working-class heritage, and vibrant art and music culture gives the neighborhood a distinct, public-facing character. Rather than simply stopping for a photo in front of a mural, take your time to observe how the main street connects to the railway station, community spaces, and local parks. A route that leads from the commercial strip near the station to the Town Hall, followed by a rest by Redfern Park and a meal on the main street, allows you to weave together the area’s railway roots, its civic history, and its present-day life.
## How to explore
1. Enter Redfern Street from the end near the railway station. Stroll along the side lined with shops, observing how cafés and small eateries integrate with the historic shophouses. If you encounter a mural, take a moment to read its story—engage with the figures depicted rather than treating them merely as a backdrop for photographs. Please respect the community by staying on public footpaths; do not enter fenced-off areas, vacant lots, or private passages that might look like shortcuts.
2. Continue to the corner of Pitt Street. Take in the symmetrical façade, arched openings, and sandstone detailing of the Town Hall, then spend a while relaxing by the edge of Redfern Park. This is a perfect spot to synthesize what you have seen so far: the flow of people from the station, the scale of the civic architecture, and the proximity of homes to the park—all of which offer insight into this historic neighborhood.
3. Enjoy a meal on the main street. For something casual, look for a café or a noodle shop; for dinner, check for availability at spots like RaRa. You might also pick up a baked treat from Breadfern before you head back to the station. Once you’ve finished, return to the station—there is no need to cross the railway tracks toward South Eveleigh, as that would only force a connection between two distinct areas.
## Timing
Allow 30 minutes for a short main-street walk and a rest. Browsing and an optional meal can extend the outing to around 120 minutes, plus any queue. Public footpaths remain available independently of business hours: shops, arcades, markets and restaurants operate their own schedules, and a late walk does not require a purchase. At night use the main pavement and marked crossings, identify your return stop first, and go around closed shopping centres on public streets rather than through private passages.
## Getting there and costs
After exiting Redfern Station, follow the signs toward the commercial section of Redfern Street; the distance to the main street varies depending on which station exit you use. Alternatively, you can take a bus to the Regent Street area. No reservations are required for walking along public streets, though venues and restaurants may have their own policies. You are responsible for your own dining, parking, and transport costs.
## Nearby food
Ramen is a great choice if you’re craving a hearty, hot meal—simply select your preferred soup base and spice level, and decide if you’d like to add any side dishes. Cafés, meanwhile, are ideal if you want to rest while you eat. You might also pick up a treat from a bakery to enjoy after your meal. If you’d like a drink with dinner, the neighborhood offers several small bars; you don’t need to hop between multiple venues to enjoy a full dining and drinking experience.
en.tips: Please be respectful when passing by community events, religious sites, or murals depicting individuals; always ask for permission before taking close-up photos of people. At the Town Hall, please limit your visit to the exterior—do not assume that you are welcome to enter rooms or observe private events, such as weddings.

items.summary: 沿老商铺吃一餐、看剧院外观，再用一份冰淇淋结束。
items.guide:
## 简介
Enmore Road从Newtown方向延伸到Enmore，是内西区餐饮、音乐与独立零售相互交织的一条街。连续的老商店楼面、雨棚和酒店转角保存了维多利亚时期商业街的轮廓，街上又不断出现新餐馆、唱片与二手服饰店。它有自己的夜间文化与社区节奏，因此和King Street分开安排也成立，不必一次把两条街走尽。

Enmore Theatre是当地最醒目的文化地标之一，装饰艺术风格的立面与演出招牌，使看剧前后用餐成为街区生活的一部分。餐饮并不只有酒吧：埃及、尼日利亚、印度和巴基斯坦等风味，加上咖啡与gelato，让白天的小范围到访也很丰富。此行以街面观察和一餐为主，剧院演出、现场音乐和酒吧消费均是额外选择，不购买演出票也能完成路线。
## 这样逛
1. 从Newtown方向进入Enmore Road，先沿公共人行道看剧院外观与附近老商铺，留意演出散场时的人流。看门口海报和立面即可，不把后台、排练区或封闭入口当普通参观空间。
2. 默认找一份可以坐下吃的主食。想吃植物食材可看Cairo Takeaway一类埃及风味菜单，喜欢香料饭可看Little Lagos等方向；先选一种菜系和一份主食，怕辣或有过敏在下单前说清。
3. 饭后沿街看一两家开放小店，再到Cow and the Moon一类gelato店选小份冰淇淋收尾。选择一个方向后就返回，不为了同时逛Newtown、Enmore和Marrickville一路走到疲惫；若已经订演出，另留检票时间。
## 时间怎么用
30分钟可走一小段主街并休息；想逛店或用餐可留120分钟左右，另加候位时间。公共街道昼夜可走，店铺、拱廊、市场和餐厅各按自己的营业时间，深夜可以只散步，不必消费。晚上沿人行道和正式过街点往返，先认好返程车站；遇已关门的商场或私人通道就沿公共道路绕行。
## 怎么去与花费
导航Enmore Road, Enmore Theatre附近。Newtown站出来可步行接入，公交也沿街服务；停车位有限时优先公共交通。街道游览无需订票，剧院仅外观包含在路线中，餐饮、演出及酒吧各自消费。
## 附近餐饮
把一份有特色的正餐和一小份gelato作为默认组合。香料饭、falafel、烤肉或咖喱按当日门面菜单选择，餐后再买甜品，避免拿着冰淇淋排热食队。饮酒不是路线要求，咖啡与无酒精饮料同样适合停留。
items.tips: 窄人行道上会有排队和公交候车人群，站到一边看手机和拍照。剧院演出与酒吧可能有年龄、票务或入场要求，按各自规则进入；同行想安静休息时选坐席餐厅，不在门口等候区占道。

en.title: Enmore Road
en.summary: Enjoy a meal amidst the historic storefronts, take in the theatre’s exterior, and wrap up your visit with an ice cream.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Extending from the direction of Newtown into Enmore, Enmore Road is a street in the Inner West where dining, live music, and independent retail converge. A continuous stretch of historic storefronts, awnings, and corner pubs preserves the silhouette of a Victorian-era commercial strip, now enlivened by a steady arrival of new restaurants, record stores, and vintage clothing shops. With its own distinct nightlife and community rhythm, Enmore Road stands well on its own—there is no need to combine it with a visit to King Street in a single outing.

The Enmore Theatre serves as one of the area’s most prominent cultural landmarks; its Art Deco façade and marquee make dining before or after a show an integral part of local life. The culinary scene extends well beyond pubs: offerings range from Egyptian, Nigerian, Indian, and Pakistani cuisine to coffee and gelato, ensuring a rich experience even during a daytime visit. This itinerary focuses on street-level observation and a meal; attending a performance, catching live music, or visiting a bar are optional—you can fully enjoy the route without ever purchasing a theater ticket.
## How to explore
1. Enter Enmore Road from the direction of Newtown. Begin by walking along the public footpath to take in the exterior of the theater and the surrounding historic storefronts—take note of the crowds when a show lets out. Simply observe the posters and the façade; please do not attempt to enter backstage areas, rehearsal spaces, or restricted zones.
2. Plan for a sit-down meal. For plant-based options, consider an Egyptian spot like Cairo Takeaway; if you prefer spiced rice dishes, look into places like Little Lagos. Choose a cuisine and a main dish, and be sure to mention any spice preferences or food allergies before placing your order.
3. After your meal, browse one or two of the local shops, then wrap up your visit with a small serving of gelato from a place like Cow and the Moon. Once you’ve explored a section of the street, head back—don’t exhaust yourself by trying to cover Newtown, Enmore, and Marrickville all at once. If you have tickets for a performance, remember to set aside extra time for the entry and ticket-checking process.
## Timing
Allow 30 minutes for a short main-street walk and a rest. Browsing and an optional meal can extend the outing to around 120 minutes, plus any queue. Public footpaths remain available independently of business hours: shops, arcades, markets and restaurants operate their own schedules, and a late walk does not require a purchase. At night use the main pavement and marked crossings, identify your return stop first, and go around closed shopping centres on public streets rather than through private passages.
## Getting there and costs
Navigate to Enmore Road, near the Enmore Theatre. You can reach the area on foot from Newtown Station, and several bus routes also serve the street. Parking is limited, so public transport is the preferred option. No tickets are required to explore the street; the route includes the exterior of the theatre only. Dining, performances, and visits to bars are separate, individual expenses.
## Nearby food
A great default combination is a distinctive main meal followed by a serving of gelato. Choose from options like spiced rice, falafel, grilled meats, or curry based on the daily menu, and pick up your dessert afterward—this way, you won’t have to stand in a queue for hot food while holding an ice cream. You don’t have to drink alcohol; coffee or non-alcoholic beverages are just as suitable for a relaxing break.
en.tips: The narrow sidewalks can get crowded with people queuing or waiting for the bus—please step aside if you need to check your phone or take photos. The theatre and bars may have specific age restrictions, ticketing requirements, or entry policies; please follow the rules for each venue. If your companions would like a quiet rest, opt for a restaurant with seating rather than waiting in the crowded areas near the entrances.

items.title: 新南威尔士议会大厦
items.summary: 从旧医院立面走进公共展览区，看看一座仍在运作的州议会。
items.guide:
## 简介
新南威尔士议会大厦沿Macquarie Street展开，临街部分原是1816年“朗姆酒医院”的北翼。早期殖民公共建筑被改作政治机构后，随着立法制度与议会工作扩展，又逐步加入议事厅和后方现代空间；它因此不是一座单一时代、单一风格的纪念碑。街边较克制的双层回廊与砂岩建筑，和两院议事空间以及后面的Fountain Court形成层次。站在外面先看柱距、阳台和建筑长度，再进公共区域，会更容易理解一个仍在工作的机构如何保留并继续使用老建筑。

这里的特别之处在于历史与制度并行：建筑曾服务医疗，如今服务立法，游客和来工作的人员在不同区域使用同一组空间。Fountain Court等公共区域有展览与访客设施，可以从当前展示开始认识这座机构；议事厅则按议程、安检和当天开放安排进入。把普通到访安排为建筑、公共展览和短暂休息，就能保持轻松；想听导览或旁听时，再按对应规则向工作人员咨询。这样既能看到真实运作，也给需要专注办公、会议和议事的人保留清楚边界。
## 这样逛
1. 到6 Macquarie Street，先在街边看旧医院北翼的回廊与立面，然后按访客入口标识通过安检。到接待处说明普通参观，先了解当天开放的公共区域。
2. 前往获准开放的Fountain Court及公共展览位置，选一组展示仔细看，再留意老建筑与现代空间的连接。不要自行进入会议室、办公室或议员专用通道。
3. 想旁听或参加当天导览就先向工作人员问入口、时间与寄存要求；不参加也可在公共咖啡区域短休后离开。回到Macquarie Street，从外部再次看一遍建筑，完成这次普通参观。
## 时间怎么用
45分钟适合安检、公共区域与一组展览；75–90分钟可加咖啡或当天可参加的活动。完整导览约一小时，属于额外安排，别把它与普通开放时间混为一谈。
## 怎么去与花费
从Martin Place火车／地铁站或St James站步行至6 Macquarie Street，入口经安检。普通公共区域参观免费，导览可另向馆方询问；没有面向公众的院内停车位，餐饮及附近停车另付。
## 附近餐饮
Long Bell Café是较轻松的咖啡与简餐停留点，先看当天柜台和座位。Strangers’ Restaurant属于另行安排的餐厅用餐，想随意吃一顿也可离开后在Martin Place周围选择，避免把餐厅预约变成参观前提。
items.tips: 安检前整理随身物品，进入旁听席时须按要求寄存手机及个人物品，并接受额外检查。拍照、座位与通行范围听从工作人员，不影响议事或其他访客。

en.title: NSW Parliament House
en.summary: Enter the public exhibition area through the façade of the former hospital and discover a state parliament that remains in active operation.
en.guide:
## Introduction
The NSW Parliament House stretches along Macquarie Street; its street-facing section was originally the north wing of the "Rum Hospital," built in 1816. As this early colonial public building was repurposed for political use, it expanded alongside the legislative system—incorporating parliamentary chambers and, later, modern spaces at the rear. Consequently, it is not a monument defined by a single era or architectural style. The restrained, two-story colonnades and sandstone structures along the street contrast with the legislative chambers and the Fountain Court located further back, creating a rich, layered architectural composition. By observing the column spacing, balconies, and overall length of the building from the outside before entering the public areas, you can better appreciate how an active institution has preserved and repurposed a historic structure.

What makes this place unique is the intersection of history and governance: the building once served a medical purpose and now houses a legislative body—with visitors and staff sharing the same space, albeit in different zones. Public areas like the Fountain Court feature exhibitions and visitor facilities, offering a perfect starting point to learn about the institution. Access to the legislative chambers, meanwhile, is subject to specific agendas, security protocols, and the day’s operational schedule. A casual visit—focused on the architecture, public exhibitions, and a brief rest—keeps the experience relaxed. If you wish to join a guided tour or observe proceedings, simply consult the staff regarding the relevant rules and procedures. This approach allows you to witness the institution in action while maintaining clear boundaries for those engaged in official work, meetings, or legislative sessions.
## How to explore
1. Arrive at 6 Macquarie Street. Take a moment to observe the colonnades and façade of the former hospital’s north wing from the street, then follow the signs to the visitor entrance to clear security. At the reception desk, state that you are here for a general visit and inquire which public areas are open that day.
2. Proceed to the accessible public areas, such as the Fountain Court and exhibition spaces. Take your time exploring the displays, and look for the points where the historic architecture meets modern interventions. Please do not enter meeting rooms, offices, or areas reserved for members of parliament.
3. If you are interested in observing proceedings or joining a guided tour, ask the staff about entry points, schedules, and policies regarding the storage of personal belongings. Alternatively, you may simply enjoy a short break in the public café area before concluding your visit. Once back on Macquarie Street, take one last look at the building from the outside to round off your visit.
## Timing
A 45-minute visit is sufficient to clear security and explore the public areas and one exhibition; a 75–90 minute visit allows time for a coffee or participation in any scheduled daily activities. A full guided tour lasts approximately one hour; please note that this is a separate offering and should not be confused with the general public access hours.
## Getting there and costs
6 Macquarie Street is within walking distance of the Martin Place train/metro station or St James station. Entry is subject to a security check. General public areas are free to visit; inquiries regarding guided tours can be made with the venue staff. There is no on-site parking available to the public; dining and nearby parking are at your own expense.
## Nearby food
Long Bell Café offers a relaxed setting for coffee and light meals—check the daily menu at the counter and available seating upon arrival. Strangers’ Restaurant requires a separate reservation; alternatively, you can explore the area around Martin Place for a casual meal, ensuring that a restaurant booking does not become a prerequisite for your visit.
en.tips: Please organize your belongings before reaching the security checkpoint. When entering the public gallery, you will be required to store your mobile phone and personal items, and undergo additional screening. Please follow staff instructions regarding photography, seating, and designated access areas, ensuring that your presence does not disrupt parliamentary proceedings or other visitors.

items.title: Fairfield 多元食街
items.summary: 在老店屋之间吃一顿老挝家常饭，再顺路逛中东面包与甜点店。
items.guide:
## 简介
Fairfield市中心的骨架来自铁路与日常买卖。1856年车站启用后，周围农场的果蔬、木材和货运逐渐汇入这个节点；The Crescent沿铁路线展开，Ware Street及附近横街后来成为更密集的商业街。今天站前仍能看到低层店屋、遮棚和高出招牌的装饰女儿墙，视线从底层便利店移到楼上窗户，会发现不同时期的建筑被保留在同一段街道里。它的趣味在于这层连续使用的城市生活：商铺不是为游客布置的展台，而是附近居民买菜、吃午饭与见朋友的地方。

战后移民让这里形成了多种饮食并存的格局，老挝与泰东北菜、中东烤物、黎巴嫩甜点和菲律宾杂货都能在市中心找到。老挝菜的香草、酸味与糯米，中东面包店的芝麻、奶酪和烤炉气味，在短短几条街里形成很鲜明的对照。市政食物地图收录了Lao Village、Song Fang Khong和多家面包甜点店，适合用“一顿主餐加一份小点”来认识街区。这里不需要等某次夜市举办，普通营业日的沿街店面就是主要内容。
## 这样逛
1. 从Fairfield站走到The Crescent商铺一侧，先沿遮棚下的人行道看一小段老店屋；用10–15分钟建立方向，再由站前街道进入Ware Street一带，不急着在第一家店吃满。
2. 把Dale Street的Lao Village（29号）作为主餐停留点，先看当日菜牌，再点一份主食配一盘适合分享的老挝菜。若同行者第一次尝试，先说明可接受的辣度与是否吃内脏，留出35–50分钟坐下来吃。
3. 饭后返回市中心主要商铺街，挑一家仍开门的中东面包或甜点店买一份小点，带走或在店内获准的位置吃；沿原路回站，想多走的人再看相邻街段，避免把整趟变成跨郊区赶店。
## 时间怎么用
30分钟可走一小段主街并休息；想逛店或用餐可留120分钟左右，另加候位时间。公共街道昼夜可走，店铺、拱廊、市场和餐厅各按自己的营业时间，深夜可以只散步，不必消费。晚上沿人行道和正式过街点往返，先认好返程车站；遇已关门的商场或私人通道就沿公共道路绕行。
## 怎么去与花费
搭车到Fairfield站，从市中心商铺方向出站，按The Crescent／Ware Street及29 Dale Street步行。这里使用车站作街区参考点，导航到具体餐馆更方便；开车选市中心停车位并看现场时限，主餐、饮品和停车分别付费。
## 附近餐饮
老挝菜可以用糯米配larb香草拌肉或青木瓜沙拉，点单时先问当日供应、发酵鱼露和辣椒强度；想吃热菜再选烤肉或汤。两个人先点两道配米饭，吃完再加，甜点留一小份即可。花生、鱼露和虾酱可能出现在酱汁里，过敏需求直接告诉店员。
items.tips: 带一只可装外带点心的小袋，杂货和餐厅都按店内规则拍照；在人行道转角停下看路线，不挡店门。普通散步不依赖广场活动、节庆摊位或某个演出。

en.title: Fairfield — The Crescent & Dale Street
en.summary: Enjoy a home-style Lao meal nestled among historic shophouses, then stop by a nearby shop specializing in Middle Eastern breads and sweets.
en.guide:
## Introduction
The framework of Fairfield’s town center is rooted in its railway and the rhythms of daily commerce. Following the opening of the railway station in 1856, the area became a hub for produce, timber, and freight from surrounding farms. The Crescent developed along the railway line, while Ware Street and its intersecting side streets evolved into a denser commercial district. Today, the area in front of the station still features low-rise shophouses, awnings, and decorative parapets that rise above the signage. A glance from the ground-floor shops to the windows above reveals a collection of buildings from different eras, preserved side-by-side along the same street. The charm lies in this continuous, living urban fabric: these shops are not staged exhibits for tourists, but rather places where local residents go to shop for groceries, enjoy lunch, or meet with friends.

Post-war immigration has fostered a diverse culinary landscape here; one can find everything from Laotian and Northeastern Thai cuisine to Middle Eastern grilled dishes, Lebanese sweets, and Filipino groceries. The aromatic herbs, tangy flavors, and sticky rice characteristic of Laotian cuisine, alongside the scents of sesame, cheese, and wood-fired ovens from Middle Eastern bakeries, create a vivid and striking contrast within just a few short blocks. This local food map features Lao Village, Song Fang Khong, and several bakeries and dessert shops—perfect for exploring the neighborhood through a combination of a main meal and a light treat. You don’t need to wait for a night market; the storefronts along the streets are the main attraction on any regular business day.
## How to explore
1. From Fairfield Station, head toward the shops on The Crescent. Walk along the sidewalk under the awnings to take in the historic shophouses—spend 10–15 minutes getting your bearings—before turning from the street in front of the station toward the Ware Street area. There’s no need to fill up at the very first place you see.
2. Make Lao Village (29 Dale Street) your stop for a main meal. Check the daily menu, then order a staple dish paired with a Lao-style plate to share. If you’re dining with someone new to this cuisine, clarify their spice tolerance and whether they eat offal; set aside 35–50 minutes to sit and enjoy your meal.
3. Afterward, head back to the main commercial strip and pick up a treat—perhaps from a Middle Eastern bakery or dessert shop—to enjoy on the go or in a designated seating area. Retrace your steps to the station; if you’re feeling energetic, you can explore the adjacent blocks, but try to keep your visit contained to a single, walkable neighborhood rather than rushing across the suburbs to hit too many spots.
## Timing
Allow 30 minutes for a short main-street walk and a rest. Browsing and an optional meal can extend the outing to around 120 minutes, plus any queue. Public footpaths remain available independently of business hours: shops, arcades, markets and restaurants operate their own schedules, and a late walk does not require a purchase. At night use the main pavement and marked crossings, identify your return stop first, and go around closed shopping centres on public streets rather than through private passages.
## Getting there and costs
Take the train to Fairfield Station and exit toward the town center, following the route along The Crescent/Ware Street toward 29 Dale Street. Using the station as a landmark makes it easier to navigate to specific restaurants. If you’re driving, look for parking in the town center and check the posted time limits; keep in mind that you will need to pay separately for your meal, drinks, and parking.
## Nearby food
Lao cuisine pairs well with sticky rice, larb (herbed minced meat salad), or green papaya salad. When ordering, ask about the day’s specials, the use of fermented fish sauce, and the spice level; for hot dishes, consider grilled meats or soups. If dining as a pair, start with two dishes and rice, then order more if needed—save room for a small dessert. Be aware that peanuts, fish sauce, and shrimp paste may be used in sauces; inform the staff if you have any allergies.
en.tips: Bring a small bag for any takeaway treats. Always check for and follow the specific photography policies at each shop or restaurant. If you need to pause on the sidewalk to check your route, step aside so you don’t block any doorways. This is a casual, independent stroll—it does not rely on public square events, festival stalls, or scheduled performances.

items.title: 帕斯利湾保护地
items.summary: 从公共步行入口进入小海湾，看悬索桥、林地与水面。
items.guide:
## 简介
Parsley Bay藏在Vaucluse住宅街区之间，窄海湾向内连接绿谷，跨湾的人行悬索桥是最容易辨认的地标。海水、树木、桥与后方草地在很小范围内叠合，比开阔长滩更适合放慢观察。湾内还保留一段通向谷地水道的短公共步行线路。

1907年，这片地方被留作公众休闲使用，此后成为居民野餐、带孩子出门与看港湾的空间。悬索桥把两侧高地和海湾联系起来，既是通行设施，也是理解地形的好位置。到访可以围绕桥、海滨与后方草地完成，不需要进入周边住宅或把整段港湾长线一起走完。
## 这样逛
1. 从The Crescent或Fitzwilliam Road一侧的现有公共步行连接进入，先看现场通行标识。下到海湾附近后辨认桥、草地和自己返回的入口，尤其不要把Horler Avenue停车场当成可用的抵达方式。
2. 沿开放公共路径到桥或桥附近的观景位置，看看窄湾如何连接港面与绿谷。桥上拍照保持短停，让开对向行人；不跨栏杆，也不为拍桥下画面走到湿滑岩面。
3. 返回海湾后方公共草地休息，体力允许可沿标识明确的谷地短步道走一小段再折返。水道与瀑布受天气影响，重点是林地和地形，不必追求固定水量的照片；结束后从原开放步行入口返回。
## 时间怎么用
60分钟看桥、海湾与草地；120分钟可加谷地短线和野餐。谷地官方短线约15至20分钟往返，另留进出住宅街区的坡路时间。带推车时先评估台阶，不将地图上的短距离等同于平路。 夜间以岸边散步、听海和休息为主，沿入口附近能看清路面的公共路径往返；不下水、不走礁石、崖边或无照明的延伸山径。救生巡逻、浴场设施和停车场有各自时间，不能把可到岸边等同于有人巡逻或可夜泳。
## 怎么去与花费
导航Parsley Bay Reserve, The Crescent, Vaucluse，步行按The Crescent或Fitzwilliam Road的公共连接进入。公交到附近街区后仍需步行，自驾在合法街边车位停车并看时限。个人公共空间到访无需预约，交通、餐饮与停车另计。
## 附近餐饮
可备三明治、水果和饮用水在允许野餐的草地吃；海湾售卖亭可作补充，需要更多选择再回Vaucluse主要街道。上下坡时尽量不用手提热饮，食物收进背包更方便。
items.tips: 穿防滑鞋，谷地路面雨后较湿。海湾没有救生员巡逻，照看孩子时留意水边与桥面；保护水道和植被，不搬石头、不投喂水龙。施工范围沿围挡绕行，不进车辆封闭区。

en.title: Parsley Bay Reserve
en.summary: Enter the small bay via the public footpath to view the suspension bridge, the surrounding woodland, and the water.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Tucked away within the residential neighborhood of Vaucluse, Parsley Bay features a narrow inlet that extends inland toward a lush, green valley. Its most recognizable landmark is the pedestrian suspension bridge spanning the bay. With the water, trees, bridge, and grassy area all concentrated in a compact space, it offers a more intimate setting for observation than an expansive, open beach. A short public walking path also runs from the bay toward the waterway in the valley.

Set aside for public recreation in 1907, the area has long served as a spot for residents to enjoy picnics, bring their children, and take in views of the harbor. The suspension bridge connects the high ground on either side of the bay; it functions both as a practical crossing and as an excellent vantage point for understanding the local topography. A visit can easily center around the bridge, the waterfront, and the grassy area—there is no need to enter the surrounding private residences or attempt to walk the entire length of the harbor coastline.
## How to explore
1. Enter via the existing public pedestrian access points from either The Crescent or Fitzwilliam Road; be sure to check the on-site signage for directions. Upon reaching the vicinity of the bay, take note of the bridge, the grassy area, and the entrance you used to arrive—and be sure not to mistake the Horler Avenue car park for a valid public access point.
2. Follow the designated public footpaths toward the bridge or the nearby vantage points to observe how the narrow inlet connects the harbour to the lush valley. If taking photos on the bridge, please keep your stop brief and make way for others; do not climb over the railings, and avoid venturing onto slippery rocks to capture shots from beneath the bridge.
3. You may rest on the public lawn behind the bay. If you have the energy, consider a short walk along the clearly marked trail into the valley before heading back. As water levels in the creek and waterfall fluctuate with the weather, focus on the woodland and the terrain rather than expecting a specific volume of water. When finished, return via the same public entrance you used to enter.
## Timing
Allow 60 minutes to explore the bridge, the bay, and the grassy area; allocate 120 minutes if you wish to include the short valley trail and a picnic. The official valley trail takes approximately 15–20 minutes (round trip); remember to also account for the time needed to walk along the sloping streets leading to and from the residential area. If you are bringing a stroller, please assess the stairs beforehand—do not assume that a short distance on a map implies flat, accessible terrain. After dark this is a shore-side walk and a chance to sit and listen to the water. Stay on visible public paths close to the approach; do not swim, enter rock platforms or continue onto unlit cliffs or bush tracks. Lifeguard patrols, bathing facilities, toilets and car parks have separate hours; public shore access does not imply a patrolled swim or an open car park.
## Getting there and costs
Set your navigation to "Parsley Bay Reserve, The Crescent, Vaucluse." Access the reserve via the public footpaths located on The Crescent or Fitzwilliam Road. If arriving by public transport, be prepared for a short walk from the nearest stop. If driving, please park only in legal street-side spaces and check for any posted time limits. No reservations are required to visit this public space; please note that transport, dining, and parking are separate considerations.
## Nearby food
Feel free to bring sandwiches, fruit, and water to enjoy on the lawns where picnicking is permitted. A kiosk at the bay offers additional refreshments, though you can also head back to the main streets of Vaucluse for a wider variety of options. When navigating slopes, it is best to avoid carrying hot drinks by hand; storing food and beverages in a backpack is much more convenient.
en.tips: Wear non-slip footwear, as the paths in the valley can become quite damp following rain. There are no lifeguards patrolling the bay; please keep a close watch on children near the water’s edge and on bridges. Help protect the waterways and vegetation—do not move rocks or feed the water dragons. Please navigate around the construction zones by following the designated detours, and do not enter areas cordoned off for vehicles.

items.title: 克朗塔夫海滩
items.summary: 在Middle Harbour的沙岸和树荫间休息，适合轻松野餐与短走。
items.guide:
## 简介
Clontarf Beach面向Middle Harbour，是一片带树荫、草地和儿童游乐空间的港湾海岸。这里的景色主要是近处沙岸、锚泊船只与对岸高地，少了外海长滩不断涌来的大浪画面，适合把一次出门安排成看港湾、野餐和短距离步行。围网泳区与公共海滨空间相邻，但并不因此有救生员巡逻。

Clontarf得名于爱尔兰都柏林同名地区。1868年，维多利亚女王的儿子爱丁堡公爵Alfred王子在这里参加野餐时遭枪击并幸存，让这个海湾进入澳大利亚殖民史的重要叙事。今天到访无需追逐某个“历史机位”，把树荫下的公共休闲空间与19世纪港湾出游传统联系起来看，就多了一层理解。
## 这样逛
1. 从Sandy Bay Road连接的海滨公共区域开始，先认清停车场、草地、游乐场和沙岸的位置。同行有孩子时先约好休息基地；想安静看港湾可找离游乐设施稍远、仍属公共范围的座位。
2. 沿海滨干燥沙岸或后方公共路径短走，看看围网泳区、锚泊船与对岸的层次。低潮与较高水位时可用沙地不同，走到宽度变窄或靠近船只操作区域就折返，不穿越码头或私人临水设施。
3. 回树荫与允许野餐的地方休息，吃完后可在海滨后方再走一小段。Manly Scenic Walkway在这一带有较长延伸，本次轻松行程以海湾为中心；若要继续走整条Spit至Manly步道，应另行安排距离和交通，不在休息后临时一口气加完。
## 时间怎么用
45分钟看海湾和短走；90分钟适合野餐、游乐场与休息。午餐时段家庭较多，想清静可在较早的白天到访；树荫会随太阳移动，不把一处阴凉当作全天有遮阴。 夜间以岸边散步、听海和休息为主，沿入口附近能看清路面的公共路径往返；不下水、不走礁石、崖边或无照明的延伸山径。救生巡逻、浴场设施和停车场有各自时间，不能把可到岸边等同于有人巡逻或可夜泳。
## 怎么去与花费
导航Clontarf Beach, Sandy Bay Road。公交下车点与海滨之间可能有坡路，按自己的起点核对步行连接；自驾使用海湾公共停车区域并依标识付费，不能占住宅车道。普通个人岸边到访无需预约，组织活动与场地使用另有申请规则。
## 附近餐饮
适合带三明治、水果和饮用水，在允许野餐区域坐下；海滨咖啡或外带窗口可作补充。若需要完整正餐，返程去Seaforth或Manly商区更容易集中比较菜单，不为一次简短看海临时寻找需要预约的餐厅。
items.tips: 照看孩子时同时留意海水与车辆，游乐场边休息不等于可以忽略水边。穿能走沙地的鞋，带防晒；不要在船只上岸或下水通道停留，也不要进入相邻私人码头拍照。

en.title: Clontarf Beach
en.summary: Relax along the sandy shores and shaded areas of Middle Harbour—an ideal spot for a casual picnic or a short, leisurely walk.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Facing Middle Harbour, Clontarf Beach is a harbourside stretch featuring shaded areas, grassy lawns, and a children’s playground. The scenery—comprising the sandy shore, anchored boats, and the elevated terrain on the opposite side—is defined by the calm waters of the harbour rather than the crashing surf of the open ocean. It is an ideal spot for a relaxed outing, combining harbour views, a picnic, and a short walk. While there is an enclosed swimming area adjacent to the public foreshore, please note that it is not patrolled by lifeguards.

Clontarf takes its name from a district in Dublin, Ireland. In 1868, Prince Alfred, Duke of Edinburgh—a son of Queen Victoria—was shot while attending a picnic here; he survived, and the incident became a notable chapter in Australia’s colonial history. Today, rather than seeking out a specific "historical landmark," one can gain a deeper appreciation of the site by connecting its shaded public leisure spaces to the 19th-century tradition of harbour-side excursions.
## How to explore
1. Begin at the public foreshore area accessible via Sandy Bay Road, and take note of the locations of the car park, grassy lawns, playground, and sandy beach. If you are visiting with children, establish a "home base" for resting; if you prefer a quieter spot to take in the harbour views, look for a seat further away from the playground while remaining within the public area.
2. Take a short stroll along the dry sand or the public path running behind the beach, observing the enclosed swimming area, the anchored boats, and the layered landscape across the water. Be mindful that the available sandy space changes with the tide; turn back if the path narrows significantly or if you approach areas where boats are being operated. Avoid crossing onto private jetties or waterfront properties.
3. Return to the shaded areas or designated picnic spots to relax. Afterward, you might enjoy another brief walk behind the foreshore. While the Manly Scenic Walkway extends through this area, this particular outing is focused on the bay itself. If you wish to complete the full Spit-to-Manly trail, it is best to plan that as a separate excursion with appropriate arrangements for distance and transport, rather than attempting to add it on spontaneously after your break.
## Timing
A 45-minute visit is sufficient for taking in the bay views and enjoying a short walk; a 90-minute stay allows time for a picnic, a visit to the playground, and some relaxation. The area tends to be crowded with families around lunchtime, so visit earlier in the day if you prefer a quieter atmosphere. Keep in mind that patches of shade shift with the sun—do not assume a spot that is shaded at one moment will remain so throughout the day. After dark this is a shore-side walk and a chance to sit and listen to the water. Stay on visible public paths close to the approach; do not swim, enter rock platforms or continue onto unlit cliffs or bush tracks. Lifeguard patrols, bathing facilities, toilets and car parks have separate hours; public shore access does not imply a patrolled swim or an open car park.
## Getting there and costs
Navigate to Clontarf Beach, Sandy Bay Road. Be aware that there may be inclines between public transport drop-off points and the waterfront; check your walking route beforehand. If arriving by car, please use the designated public parking areas and follow the signage for payment—do not park in or block private residential driveways. No booking is required for casual individual visits, though organized events or specific site usage may be subject to separate application requirements.
## Nearby food
It is a good idea to bring sandwiches, fruit, and drinking water to enjoy in the designated picnic areas; alternatively, you can pick up refreshments at the waterfront café or takeaway window. If you are looking for a full meal, you will find a better selection of restaurants in the commercial hubs of Seaforth or Manly—it is often easier to compare menus there than to scramble for a reservation-only restaurant during a brief seaside outing.
en.tips: When supervising children, keep a close watch on both the water and nearby traffic; relaxing near the playground does not mean you can lose sight of the water’s edge. Wear footwear suitable for walking on sand and remember sun protection. Please avoid lingering in areas used for launching or retrieving boats, and do not enter adjacent private jetties for the sake of taking photos.

items.title: 司法与警察博物馆
items.summary: 周末探索司法与警察历史展厅；Police Cells暂时关闭，不包含该区域。
items.guide:
## 简介
Justice & Police Museum位于Albert Street与Phillip Street转角，由旧法院与警察建筑组成，靠近早年繁忙的Circular Quay。这里的历史与水警、港口城市治安及司法制度相连；原有房间与建筑用途本身，就是理解展览的重要线索。

展陈通过历史照片、器物与案件材料讲述悉尼城市生活，适合把注意力放在人与制度的关系，而不只是猎奇的犯罪故事。旧建筑尺度较紧凑，展柜、法院空间与走廊连在一起，让参观者可以把“发生过什么”与“事情发生在怎样的场所”同时理解。
## 这样逛
1. 在 Albert Street 与 Phillip Street 转角报到，先问工作人员当前开放的展厅与动线。按导览图从法院空间开始。
2. 从开放的旧水警法院与警察历史空间开始，看建筑用途、历史照片和实物说明，选两三件感兴趣的材料仔细读，分清当时制度与今天的不同。
3. 继续看开放展厅里的案件、城市生活与司法叙事；如当天有免费短导览且尚有名额，可加入听一段，再回到喜欢的展柜补看。离馆前看街角历史建筑的外观。
## 时间怎么用
45分钟看当前开放的核心展厅；90分钟可听现场导览、细读史料。可在参观前后回街角看建筑外观。
## 怎么去与花费
离 Circular Quay 火车、渡轮和轻轨不远，按 Albert/Phillip 街角导航。普通入场免费，馆方建议提前预约；20人及以上团体需另作安排。
## 附近餐饮
可步行回Circular Quay或沿Phillip Street找简餐和咖啡。馆内看完一段内容再出门休息，若计划参加现场短导览，先在前台确认集合时间。
items.tips: 涉及犯罪、监禁和历史影像，带孩子时先判断内容接受度。避开保育围挡，沿开放动线参观。馆内摄影和器材限制按展签执行，辅助路线可在前台询问。

en.title: Justice & Police Museum
en.summary: Explore the galleries dedicated to the history of the justice system and the police force. Please note that the Police Cells are currently closed and not accessible.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Located at the corner of Albert Street and Phillip Street, the Justice & Police Museum occupies the site of a former courthouse and police station, situated near what was once the bustling Circular Quay. The history here is deeply intertwined with the water police, the maintenance of law and order in a port city, and the evolution of the judicial system. The original rooms and the intended functions of the buildings themselves serve as essential context for understanding the exhibitions.

Through historical photographs, artifacts, and case files, the museum explores life in Sydney. It encourages visitors to focus on the relationship between individuals and the legal system, rather than simply viewing the exhibits as sensationalized tales of crime. The historic building features a compact layout, with display cases, courtroom spaces, and corridors seamlessly integrated. This allows visitors to grasp both the events that took place and the specific settings in which they unfolded.
## How to explore
1. Check in at the corner of Albert Street and Phillip Street; ask the staff which exhibition areas are currently open and the recommended route. Begin your visit with the courtroom spaces, following the provided map.
2. Start by exploring the former Water Police Court and the police history exhibits. Examine the building’s original functions, historical photographs, and artifacts. Select a few items that interest you—read the accompanying information carefully and consider how the systems of the past differ from those of today.
3. Continue exploring the open galleries, which cover specific legal cases, urban life, and the history of the justice system. If a free, short guided tour is available and has space, consider joining it; afterwards, you can return to any specific displays that caught your eye. Before leaving, take a moment to observe the exterior of this historic corner building.
## Timing
A 45-minute visit is sufficient to see the core exhibition areas currently open to the public. A 90-minute visit allows time for a guided tour and a more in-depth study of historical materials. You may also wish to view the building’s exterior from the street corner either before or after your visit.
## Getting there and costs
Located near the Circular Quay train, ferry, and light rail terminals; navigate to the corner of Albert and Phillip Streets. General admission is free, though the museum recommends booking in advance. Groups of 20 or more require separate arrangements.
## Nearby food
You can walk back to Circular Quay or find light refreshments and coffee along Phillip Street. Feel free to step outside for a break between sections of the exhibition. If you plan to join a short guided tour, please confirm the meeting time at the front desk.
en.tips: As the exhibits cover topics such as crime, imprisonment, and historical imagery, please assess whether the content is appropriate for any children in your party. Please steer clear of areas cordoned off for conservation and follow the designated visitor route. Refer to the signage at each exhibit for specific rules regarding photography and equipment; feel free to ask the front desk staff for guidance on the recommended path.

items.title: 好市围Forest Road
items.summary: 沿南区华人生活主街慢走，以一顿饮茶或烧味饭作为中心。
items.guide:
## 简介
Hurstville的名字由表示林地高处的“hurst”和城镇的“ville”组合而成，反映了当地早期森林与木材业的地貌记忆。1884年车站开通后，沿山脊的Forest Road逐渐成为商业主轴，店屋、旅馆与公共建筑围绕交通发展。今天走在街上，仍可看到较窄的老铺面、转角建筑和后来更高的商业住宅混合在一起，斜向路口与高低变化也保留了旧道路顺地形生长的痕迹。

好市围后来成为悉尼南区重要的华人生活与餐饮中心，Forest Road上的中式餐馆、烧味、面包店和日常商店让它具有很强的生活感。这里适合认真吃一顿，而不是只到购物中心里转一圈；想看街区，可以在用餐前后走一小段主街，把老建筑与今天的中文招牌一起看。围绕车站北侧商业段慢走，再把一顿饮茶或热食作为中心，既能看到南区街景，也适合在忙碌一天里认真坐下来吃饭。
## 这样逛
1. 从车站北侧接上Forest Road。先确认自己在主街商业段，再沿一侧慢走看烧味、茶餐厅和烘焙店橱窗。路口较多，想看对面店面就在信号灯处过街；长街不用全走，先选一顿饭的大方向更实用。
2. 到Park Road附近看转角街景。比较低层老店屋与新商业楼的高度、骑楼与招牌，找一个不挡行人的位置拍街角。若想少走，就在这一段坐下来休息，买水或看菜单；不要为了“逛完”一直走到住宅或车辆更密的路段。
3. 把午餐当作主站。想饮茶可考虑Golden Sands，点心先点少量再加，留出坐着喝茶的时间；想快一点就用烧味饭、面食或其他当前有位的店代替。饭后在主街买一份面包带走，再回车站结束。
## 时间怎么用
30分钟可走一小段主街并休息；想逛店或用餐可留120分钟左右，另加候位时间。公共街道昼夜可走，店铺、拱廊、市场和餐厅各按自己的营业时间，深夜可以只散步，不必消费。晚上沿人行道和正式过街点往返，先认好返程车站；遇已关门的商场或私人通道就沿公共道路绕行。
## 怎么去与花费
Hurstville Station有主街一侧和巴士换乘一侧，出站看Forest Road指示；公交也可到附近。开车留意单行、装卸及停车限制。点心按份、茶位和其他费用以菜单为准，未知总价不能当作免费或固定预算套餐。
## 附近餐饮
饮茶先点两三笼自己喜欢的蒸点，再加一份肠粉或其他主食，人数多时按吃完的速度续点；蒸点、煎炸和甜点分开安排，更容易吃到热的。烧味饭或汤面适合赶时间的另一条路线。点心含虾、猪肉、蛋或其他馅料的情况很多，忌口直接向店员确认。
items.tips: 跨Forest Road请等行人灯，主街有坡度和车辆出入口。多人饮茶先说清忌口和预算，海鲜、坚果或乳制品过敏应直接向店家确认。

en.title: Hurstville — Forest Road
en.summary: Take a leisurely stroll along the main street—the heart of the local Chinese community—with a yum cha meal or a roast meat rice dish as the centerpiece of your visit.
en.guide:
## Introduction
The name "Hurstville" is a combination of "hurst"—denoting a wooded hill—and "ville" (town), a nod to the area’s early landscape, once defined by forests and the timber industry. Following the opening of the railway station in 1884, Forest Road—which runs along the ridgeline—emerged as the primary commercial artery, with shops, hotels, and public buildings developing around this transport hub. Walking along the street today, one can still spot narrow, historic storefronts and corner buildings interspersed with taller, modern mixed-use commercial and residential structures. The angled intersections and varying elevations serve as a reminder of how the original roads were laid out to follow the natural contours of the land.

Hurstville has since evolved into a vital hub for the Chinese community in Sydney’s southern suburbs, with Forest Road home to a vibrant array of Chinese restaurants, siu mei (roast meat) shops, bakeries, and everyday retail stores. This is a place for a proper meal, rather than just a quick spin through a shopping mall. To get a feel for the neighborhood, take a stroll along the main street before or after your meal—you’ll see historic architecture standing alongside contemporary Chinese signage. A leisurely walk through the commercial stretch north of the station, anchored by a yum cha session or a hot meal, offers a great glimpse into the streetscape of Sydney’s southern suburbs and provides the perfect excuse to sit down and enjoy a meal during a busy day.
## How to explore
1. Access Forest Road from the north side of the station. Ensure you are in the main commercial section, then take a slow walk along one side of the street, observing the displays in the windows of siu mei shops, cha chaan tengs (Hong Kong-style cafés), and bakeries. There are many intersections; if you’d like to see the storefronts on the opposite side, simply cross at the traffic lights. There is no need to walk the entire length of the street—focusing on finding a spot for a meal is a more practical approach.
2. Head toward Park Road to take in the streetscape at the corner. Observe the contrast in height between the low-rise historic shops and the newer commercial buildings, and take note of the verandas (covered walkways) and signage. Find a spot that doesn’t obstruct pedestrians to capture a photo of the street corner. If you prefer to walk less, simply settle down in this area to rest, grab a drink, or browse a menu. There is no need to continue walking into the more residential or traffic-heavy sections just for the sake of "covering" the whole area.
3. Make lunch the centerpiece of your visit. For yum cha (dim sum), consider Golden Sands; order a small amount to start, then add more as you go—this leaves you time to sit back and enjoy your tea. If you’re in a rush, opt for a roast meat rice dish, noodles, or another establishment with immediate seating. Before heading back to the station, pick up some bread from a bakery on the main street.
## Timing
Allow 30 minutes for a short main-street walk and a rest. Browsing and an optional meal can extend the outing to around 120 minutes, plus any queue. Public footpaths remain available independently of business hours: shops, arcades, markets and restaurants operate their own schedules, and a late walk does not require a purchase. At night use the main pavement and marked crossings, identify your return stop first, and go around closed shopping centres on public streets rather than through private passages.
## Getting there and costs
Hurstville Station has exits leading toward the main street and the bus interchange; follow the signs for "Forest Road." The area is also accessible by bus. If driving, be mindful of one-way streets, loading zones, and parking restrictions. Costs for dim sum dishes, tea service, and other charges are as listed on the menu; do not assume a meal is free or part of a fixed-price package just because the final total is unknown.
## Nearby food
When having yum cha, start by ordering two or three baskets of your favorite steamed dim sum, along with a cheung fun (steamed rice noodle roll) or another main dish. If dining in a larger group, order additional items as you finish what’s on the table. To ensure your food stays hot, order steamed dishes, fried items, and desserts in separate rounds. If you are short on time, opt for a roast meat rice dish or a bowl of noodle soup instead. Many dim sum items contain shrimp, pork, eggs, or other ingredients—if you have dietary restrictions, be sure to check with the staff.
en.tips: When crossing Forest Road, please wait for the pedestrian signal. Note that the main street has inclines and various vehicle entry/exit points. If dining with a group, clarify any dietary restrictions and budget expectations beforehand; if anyone has allergies—such as to seafood, nuts, or dairy—confirm directly with the restaurant staff.

items.title: 达令港WILD LIFE动物园
items.summary: 在达令港用一段紧凑展线认识澳洲动物，互动加项可以按需选择。
items.guide:
## 简介
WILD LIFE Sydney是位于达令港的一处紧凑动物展示设施，以澳洲栖地和本土物种为主题。它于2006年开放，建筑与水族馆并排，采用多层次、相对集中的展线，把不同环境的动物放在一次较短的步行参观里。和Taronga的海港坡地或西悉尼大型动物园相比，这里更适合已经在CBD、想用一两个小时认识澳洲动物的游客；它们是不同场馆，门票和交通安排不能互换。

参观重点可放在考拉、袋鼠及爬行动物等展区的环境、行为和解说，动物在休息或隐蔽处活动是正常情况。设施是室内与遮蔽空间为主的城市动物园，不应把宣传里的早餐、合影或近距离接触理解为普通票全部包含。部分互动需要另外收费、预约或遵从工作人员安排。普通路线按单向展线慢看即可，不必把每一场额外活动都排进去；保持安静并给同伴留下观察时间，比不停催促动物动起来更有收获。
## 这样逛
1. 在Wheat Road沿岸确认WILD LIFE入口，买普通入场票或核对联票的单馆时段。先看当天路线图，把最想看的两三个动物区域安排在同一方向。
2. 顺展线观察本土动物，考拉区留几分钟看休息姿态，再比较袋鼠与爬行动物的栖地设计；先读说明牌，不把所有可见动物都概括成同一种袋鼠。
3. 接近出口前补看遗漏的解说与保育内容。想参加合影或早餐项目时另问价格和时段，普通参观结束后可以直接回海边，不需要追加消费。
## 时间怎么用
90分钟适合完整普通参观，120分钟可以慢看和拍照。当前每日10–17点、最后入场16点，建议15:30前入场，保留90分钟参观。
## 怎么去与花费
地址1–5 Wheat Road, Darling Harbour，Town Hall或Wynyard步行可达。门口可购票但受容量限制，官网建议提前选时段；门票价格浮动，上限未固定，早餐及合影另付。
## 附近餐饮
逛完再到Cockle Bay或附近公共餐饮区用餐；不带食物喂动物，场馆内有独立消费项目也可直接跳过。
items.tips: 勿越界、投喂或拍打玻璃；带儿童按展道行走。名字里的Sydney Zoo不要与Bungarribee的Sydney Zoo混淆。
