items.title: 和谐公园
items.summary: 在布里斯班街旁的社区公园休息，感受萨里山街区。
items.guide:
## 简介
Harmony Park位于Brisbane Street，名字与Surry Hills、Darlinghurst多元的社会和文化背景有关。这里经历了1924年的街区拆迁，后来长期闲置及用作停车空间；市政于2001年购回土地，2006年开放为公园，从原先的硬质城市用地转为居民可以停留的绿地。

小公园的草地、树木和周边道路形成紧凑但清楚的层次，邻近建筑又把它放在密集街区的生活背景中。园区还利用周边建筑收集的雨水灌溉。它适合一次短暂休息，看看公共绿地如何改变街道的步行感受，而不是需要很多设备或景点才能成立的目的地。
## 这样逛
1. 从Brisbane Street旁的公共入口进入，沿小公园边缘缓慢走一圈，先看可坐区域与狗活动的位置，选让自己舒服的停留点。
2. 看看周边Surry Hills街区与绿地的连接，想了解背景可读现场历史信息：这一带经历过城市改造与停车空间，后来在2006年转为公园。
3. 坐几分钟听街区声音，读几页自带的书或喝水，结束后沿公共步道返回。这里的价值是一次不用赶路的小休息，不需要添加虚构景点或必玩设施。
## 时间怎么用
20分钟走一圈加短坐；60分钟适合放慢节奏阅读或休息。公园规模有限，若没有适合的座位可以缩短停留，不必强行待满。 夜间也可沿可通行的公共步道或建筑外侧散步，挑能看清台阶与路面的路线往返；室内、泳池、活动区域和园内设施按各自开放安排。
## 怎么去与花费
位置在Brisbane Street, Surry Hills，按地图从附近公交或市区步行接近。道路过街与回程选择以当前位置为准。
## 附近餐饮
可沿Goulburn Street或向Surry Hills主要街道找咖啡与简餐。公园较小，带水和一本书即可完成短休息；需要正餐时离园到沿街店面会更方便。
items.tips: 官方列为全天允许狗脱绳的区域，怕狗或带幼童时先观察周围。带好水，离开时带走垃圾。

en.title: Harmony Park
en.summary: Take a break in this neighborhood park off Brisbane Street and soak in the atmosphere of Surry Hills.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Harmony Park, located on Brisbane Street, derives its name from the diverse social and cultural fabric of the Surry Hills and Darlinghurst areas. The site was once cleared of its original structures in 1924, after which it remained vacant for a long period and was later used as a parking lot. The local council reacquired the land in 2001, and in 2006, it was opened as a park—transforming what was once a hard-surfaced urban space into a green area where residents can linger.

The park’s lawns, trees, and surrounding pathways create a compact yet well-defined spatial arrangement, while the nearby buildings anchor it firmly within the context of a dense urban neighborhood. The park also utilizes rainwater collected from surrounding buildings for irrigation. This spot is perfect for a brief respite—a chance to see how a public green space can transform the pedestrian experience of a city street—rather than a destination that relies on elaborate facilities or attractions.
## How to explore
1. Enter via the public access point off Brisbane Street and take a leisurely stroll around the perimeter of the small park. Observe the designated seating areas and the space for dogs, then choose a spot where you feel most comfortable.
2. Take in how the park connects to the surrounding Surry Hills neighborhood. To learn more about its history, read the on-site information: this area once underwent urban redevelopment and served as a parking space before being converted into a park in 2006.
3. Sit for a few minutes to listen to the sounds of the neighborhood, read a few pages of a book you’ve brought along, or simply enjoy a drink. When you’re ready, head back out via the public footpath. The true value here lies in a relaxed, unhurried break—no need for artificial attractions or "must-do" amenities.
## Timing
A full loop plus a short rest takes about 20 minutes; 60 minutes is ideal if you want to slow down, read, or simply unwind. Given the park’s small size, feel free to shorten your stay if you can’t find a suitable place to sit—there’s no need to force yourself to stay longer. Evening visits use public paths and building exteriors where you can see the surface and steps clearly. Interiors, pools, event zones and other facilities retain their own access arrangements.
## Getting there and costs
Located on Brisbane Street in Surry Hills; you can reach it by following a map from nearby public transport stops or by walking from the city center. Plan your street crossings and return route based on your current location.
## Nearby food
You can find coffee and light bites along Goulburn Street or the main thoroughfares of Surry Hills. As the park is quite small, all you really need for a quick break is some water and a book; for a full meal, it’s best to head to one of the nearby cafés or restaurants.
en.tips: This is an officially designated off-leash dog area; if you are uncomfortable around dogs or are visiting with small children, take a moment to observe the surroundings first. Remember to bring water, and please take your trash with you when you leave.

items.title: 迪怀海滩
items.summary: 海滨步道、泳池景观和一条餐饮街，让看海无需远足。
items.guide:
## 简介
Dee Why既是北部海滩的重要生活与商业中心，也是一处有鲜明社区气氛的外海海滩。它的名称早在测量师James Meehan的1815年笔记里已出现。如今海岸南端的Dee Why Point塑造浪线，The Strand后方的餐馆、住宅与公共草地，则让这里兼具冲浪海岸和日常街区的性格。

海滩并不是只有一条沙岸：南端海水泳池、Ted Jackson Reserve的草地及游乐空间、往北延伸的海滨路径，提供了不同的停留方式。这里也承载体育与社区活动，平日散步和活动日的气氛差别很大。第一次来无需追赶整条海岸步行路线，从南端到北面走一小段，就能把海景和街区生活一起看到。
## 这样逛
1. 从The Strand南段靠近Oaks Avenue的位置抵达，先到海边公共路径看沙滩与Dee Why Point。这里餐饮与座位集中，适合先确定返回集合点。带小朋友可把Ted Jackson Reserve附近作为休息基地，不必马上走进沙地。
2. 沿路径向南端泳池方向走，在开放的公共观景位置看泳池、岩岸和外海的层次。观察泳池与自然海岸如何衔接即可，不需要绕到浪打得到的岩台；想看冲浪者，站在陆上宽处等一组浪，比沿礁石追着拍更轻松。
3. 折回后沿海滩向北散步，走到James Meehan Reserve一带或任何适合折返的位置。回程可换到The Strand街侧，挑一家合适的店休息。北面的泻湖与Long Reef需要更长行程，本次短线不用把它们作为必须抵达的终点。
## 时间怎么用
60分钟安排泳池观景、短距离海滨往返；120分钟可增加北段与用餐。避开正午最晒的时段更舒服；周末和活动日给停车、过街与等位多留时间。 夜间以岸边散步、听海和休息为主，沿入口附近能看清路面的公共路径往返；不下水、不走礁石、崖边或无照明的延伸山径。救生巡逻、浴场设施和停车场有各自时间，不能把可到岸边等同于有人巡逻或可夜泳。
## 怎么去与花费
导航Dee Why Beach, The Strand。公交可到Dee Why商圈再向海边步行，部分线路靠近海滩，按地图选择少走坡路的下车点。James Meehan Reserve有付费停车。公共海滩到访免费；餐饮和交通另计，普通散步不需预约。
## 附近餐饮
The Strand沿线适合早午餐、咖啡或较完整的午餐，可在回程时比较两三家菜单再坐下。想把预算留给出行，买一份外带简餐，在允许用餐的公共区域休息即可。靠海位置可能排队，街侧座位通常更便于带包和整理随身物品。
items.tips: 带防晒、水和挡风外层，推车尽量走公共人行路径。泳池边湿地面和岩面易滑；海滨活动布置或比赛围挡出现时按指示绕行。停车计时从离车开始计算，别把午餐时间漏在车位时限之外。

en.title: Dee Why Beach
en.summary: With its coastal promenade, swimming pools, and a street lined with eateries, this area lets you enjoy the seaside without needing to go on a strenuous hike.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Dee Why serves as a key residential and commercial hub on the Northern Beaches, offering a coastal beach experience with a distinct, vibrant community atmosphere. The name appears as early as 1815 in the field notes of surveyor James Meehan. Today, Dee Why Point—at the southern end of the coastline—shapes the incoming surf, while the restaurants, residences, and public lawns behind "The Strand" lend the area a dual character: part surf coast, part everyday neighborhood.

The beach offers more than just a stretch of sand; the ocean pool at the southern end, the lawns and play areas of Ted Jackson Reserve, and the coastal path extending northward provide various ways to enjoy the space. The area also hosts sports and community events, meaning the atmosphere can shift significantly between a quiet weekday stroll and a busy event day. On your first visit, there’s no need to commit to the entire coastal walk—simply exploring a short stretch from the southern end toward the north will allow you to take in both the seascape and the local neighborhood life.
## How to explore
1. Arrive near the southern end of The Strand, close to Oaks Avenue, and head to the public coastal path for a view of the beach and Dee Why Point. This area features a concentration of dining options and seating—a good spot to get your bearings and note your return meeting point. If you are visiting with children, Ted Jackson Reserve serves as an excellent base for resting, so you don’t have to head straight onto the sand.
2. Follow the path toward the southern ocean pool. From the open public vantage points, you can take in the layers of the pool, the rocky shoreline, and the open ocean beyond. Simply observe how the pool integrates with the natural coastline; there is no need to venture out onto the wave-swept rock platforms. If you’d like to watch surfers, it is much easier to wait for a set of waves from a wide, stable spot on land than to scramble along the rocks trying to follow them.
3. Turn back and stroll northward along the beach, heading toward James Meehan Reserve or any other point where you’d like to turn around. On your return, you might switch to the street side along The Strand to relax at one of the local establishments. The lagoon and Long Reef to the north require a longer excursion, so don’t feel pressured to reach them on this shorter outing.
## Timing
A 60-minute visit allows time to view the ocean pool and take a short walk along the coast; a 120-minute visit provides enough time to explore the northern section and enjoy a meal. It is more comfortable to visit outside of the peak midday sun, and if you are arriving on a weekend or during an event, be sure to allow extra time for parking, crossing the street, and waiting for a table. After dark this is a shore-side walk and a chance to sit and listen to the water. Stay on visible public paths close to the approach; do not swim, enter rock platforms or continue onto unlit cliffs or bush tracks. Lifeguard patrols, bathing facilities, toilets and car parks have separate hours; public shore access does not imply a patrolled swim or an open car park.
## Getting there and costs
Navigate to "The Strand, Dee Why Beach." You can reach the area by bus—alight at the Dee Why commercial hub and walk toward the beach. Some bus routes drop you off closer to the shore; check a map to select a stop that minimizes uphill walking. Paid parking is available at James Meehan Reserve. Access to the public beach is free; dining and transport costs are separate. No reservations are required for a casual stroll.
## Nearby food
The Strand offers plenty of options for brunch, coffee, or a full lunch. You might want to compare menus at a few spots before deciding where to sit—perhaps on your way back. If you’d prefer to save your budget for other travel expenses, grab a takeaway meal and enjoy it in a designated public seating area. Tables facing the ocean may have queues, while seating on the street side is often more convenient if you have bags or personal belongings to manage.
en.tips: Bring sun protection, water, and a windproof outer layer. If you have a stroller, stick to the public pedestrian paths. Be careful, as wet surfaces near the pools and rocky areas can be slippery. If you encounter barriers for events or competitions along the waterfront, please follow the posted detours. If you are parking, remember that the time limit begins the moment you leave your vehicle—ensure your lunch plans fit within your allotted parking duration.

items.title: Lord Nelson酿酒酒馆
items.summary: 在Millers Point砂岩酒馆坐下来，了解一杯现场酿造的啤酒。
items.guide:
## 简介
Lord Nelson在Kent Street与Argyle Place交会处，砂岩建筑与周围的旧住宅、仓储遗迹一起，保留了海港西侧街区的尺度。店方历史追溯至William Wells在1836年建造的住宅，1841年取得酒牌，随后转作以Lord Nelson命名的旅馆。理解它的意义，不只是比较谁自称“最老”，而是看一座早期城市房屋怎样持续承担社交、住宿与餐饮功能。

现场酿造让这里与主要售卖其他品牌的酒馆不同。酒吧和酿酒设备属于同一经营场所，Three Sheets、Old Admiral等常设酒款的名字也与海军和酒馆叙事联系。游客可以从颜色、苦度和轻重口味去认识一杯酒，而不必一次尝完所有种类。地面层公共酒吧、楼上餐厅和客房各有使用安排，来喝饮品并不自动获得参观酿酒工作区或进入住宿空间的权限。
## 这样逛
1. 从19 Kent Street的正常酒馆入口到地面层，先找空位、看黑板或酒单；店内忙时站在不挡吧台和送餐路线的位置等服务。
2. 告诉工作人员你偏清爽还是浓郁，可从一杯或较小份量开始；不喝酒也能选无酒精饮品。观察砂岩墙、窗洞和公共空间，酿造工作区只在明确允许的活动中进入。
3. 若想吃饭，先问地面层当天仍供应哪些酒馆菜；楼上Upstairs是另一个用餐选择，需按自己的营业时段与订位安排。离店后沿Argyle Place或Kent Street走回公开街道，不从后场图近路。
## 时间怎么用
45–60分钟适合坐下喝一杯、看建筑；90–120分钟可加一餐。地面层酒吧周一至周六11–23时、周日12–22时。Upstairs官网列周三至周六12–15:30及17:30–22时，周日12–16时；它不能替代地面层的营业安排，周日晚间也不能默认楼上提供正餐。
## 怎么去与花费
地址19 Kent Street, Millers Point。从Barangaroo Metro沿公开街道步行上来较顺路；Wynyard、Circular Quay也能步行接入，但有坡度，按Kent Street与Argyle Place定位，不走居民台阶或服务通道。饮品、酒馆菜、楼上餐厅分别按菜单结算；住宿、私人活动、酿造参观都不包含在普通酒吧短停里。饮酒后不驾车，返程先选车站方向。
## 附近餐饮
地面层可从一份适合食量的酒馆菜或小食开始；想正式坐下来吃一餐，再决定是否选择Upstairs。这里不需要安排啤酒巡礼，餐后可以在Millers Point公共街道走一小段，去海滨则选择能看清路面、明确通行的入口。
items.tips: 晚间酒吧按18岁以上安排，带有效证件，适量饮酒；无酒精选择同样合适。老建筑内楼层通行有台阶，需要无台阶座位时直接与员工确认，勿进入酿造区和客房。

en.title: The Lord Nelson Brewery Hotel
en.summary: A sandstone pub in Millers Point with beer brewed on the premises.
en.guide:
## Introduction
The Lord Nelson stands at Kent Street and Argyle Place, where sandstone buildings and old residential streets preserve the scale of the western harbour neighbourhood. The operator traces its history to William Wells’s 1836 home, a liquor licence obtained in 1841 and the subsequent conversion into the Lord Nelson Hotel. Rather than settling competing claims about Sydney’s oldest pub, look at how an early city building has continued to combine hospitality, accommodation and everyday social life.

Brewing on the premises gives the visit a different focus from a pub selling only outside brands. Familiar names such as Three Sheets and Old Admiral connect the beer list to the venue’s naval identity. A single drink is enough to begin comparing colour, bitterness and body; a visit does not require tasting the whole range. The ground-floor bar, upstairs restaurant, brewing areas and guest rooms are distinct spaces with separate access arrangements.
## How to explore
1. Enter the ground-floor pub at 19 Kent Street. Find a seat and read the beer board or drinks list, keeping bar queues and food-service routes clear while you wait.
2. Describe whether you prefer a lighter or fuller flavour and begin with one drink or a smaller serving. Non-alcoholic choices are equally suitable. Look at the sandstone walls, windows and public room; do not treat visible brewing equipment as an invitation to enter a work area.
3. If hungry, ask what the ground-floor kitchen is serving. The Upstairs restaurant is a separate option with its own hours and booking arrangements. Leave via public Kent Street or Argyle Place rather than looking for shortcuts through the back of the building.
## Timing
Allow 45–60 minutes for a drink and the building, or 90–120 minutes with a meal. Bar hours are 11:00–23:00 Monday–Saturday and 12:00–22:00 Sunday. Upstairs lists 12:00–15:30 and 17:30–22:00 Wednesday–Saturday, and 12:00–16:00 Sunday. Those restaurant sessions do not replace bar hours; in particular, an open Sunday-evening bar does not promise an upstairs dinner.
## Getting there and costs
Go to 19 Kent Street, Millers Point. Barangaroo Metro provides an approach on public streets; Wynyard and Circular Quay are also walkable with some gradients. Identify the Kent Street and Argyle Place corner rather than using residential stairs or service passages. Drinks, pub food and upstairs dining are charged from their respective menus. Rooms, private events and brewery tours are not part of this ordinary bar visit. Choose a station for the return and do not drive after drinking.
## Nearby food
For something simple, start with a ground-floor pub dish or snack that suits your appetite. Choose Upstairs only if you want a separate restaurant meal and its session fits. There is no need to make a pub crawl of the evening. A short walk through Millers Point can follow, using visible public routes if you continue towards the water.
en.tips: Plan a late bar visit as an adult outing and bring accepted ID. Drink moderately or choose alcohol-free. Ask staff about suitable seating if stairs are difficult; brewing spaces and guest rooms are private.

items.title: 维多利亚女王大厦
items.summary: 探索历史购物建筑的公共空间，购物与餐饮按实际消费。
items.guide:
## 简介
Queen Victoria Building通常简称QVB，是George Street上一整街区的历史商业建筑。它由George McRae设计，1893至1898年建造，采用罗马式复兴风格，原本作为市场使用。此后建筑经历不同用途、改造与衰败，直到20世纪后期修复，才重新成为今天的商业与公共步行空间。

外部可看连续拱窗、砂岩立面与中央穹顶，内部则由多层回廊围绕中庭展开。彩色玻璃、地砖、楼梯和悬挂大钟，使这座建筑即使不购物也有足够的观看内容。不同楼层能看到穹顶与中庭不同的比例，抬头与回望往往比沿店面一直走更有收获。
## 这样逛
1. 从455 George Street 的公共入口进入，先到中央中庭抬头看穹顶与各层回廊，别急着跟随店铺招牌走。
2. 按楼层指示上到开放的公共回廊，从不同高度看中庭和彩色玻璃；留意建筑内部的悬挂大钟，在不挡通道的位置看细节。
3. 回到另一侧中庭或地面层，比较拱窗、地砖和楼梯的装饰，再从方便前往 Town Hall 的出口离开。要喝咖啡可先看现场菜单，不需要购物才能欣赏公共空间。
## 时间怎么用
30分钟看中央中庭和一层回廊；60分钟可慢逛两侧空间并读介绍。楼层和店铺营业时间不完全一致，可先看公共中庭，再按楼层指引慢逛。
## 怎么去与花费
位于455 George Street，Town Hall 车站与轻轨沿线方便到达。购物、咖啡及付费历史导览均另计。
## 参观要点
建筑观察可分三轮：在地面看中庭的纵深，到开放回廊看中央穹顶与钟，再近看彩色玻璃和地砖。不要在扶梯出口停留，也不要把店铺门口当拍摄支架位置；选宽处站定后再抬头。
## 附近餐饮
楼内可找咖啡、茶点与简餐；想继续走街区，可从George Street或York Street出口离开后再选。先看菜单与营业楼层，公共空间散步、购物及付费导览分别安排；只欣赏建筑也完全成立。
items.tips: 室内适合避雨，但往返车站仍可能淋雨。站在扶梯出口、狭窄回廊拍照会影响通行，请移到宽处。付费导览需另查预约与场次，不能把公共区域随访等同于进入所有店铺或后台空间。

en.title: Queen Victoria Building
en.summary: Explore the public spaces of this historic retail building; shopping and dining are available at your own discretion and expense.
en.guide:
## Introduction
The Queen Victoria Building, commonly known as the QVB, is a historic commercial complex occupying an entire city block on George Street. Designed by George McRae and constructed between 1893 and 1898, the building features a Romanesque Revival style and was originally built as a marketplace. Over the years, it served various purposes and underwent several renovations—and periods of decline—before being restored in the late 20th century, transforming it into the commercial and public pedestrian space it is today.

From the outside, you can admire the continuous arched windows, sandstone façade, and central dome. Inside, the building is organized around a central atrium, surrounded by multi-level galleries. With its stained glass, intricate floor tiles, grand staircases, and a large suspended clock, the building offers plenty to see even if you aren't there to shop. Each floor provides a different perspective of the dome and atrium; looking up or glancing back often reveals more beauty than simply walking past the storefronts.
## How to explore
1. Enter via the public entrance at 455 George Street. Before following the shop signs, head to the central atrium and look up to admire the dome and the galleries on each level.
2. Use the floor directories to reach the accessible public galleries, where you can view the atrium and stained glass from various heights. Keep an eye out for the large, suspended clock—take a moment to observe its details from a spot that doesn’t obstruct the walkway.
3. Make your way to the other side of the atrium or the ground floor to compare the arched windows, floor tiles, and staircase ornamentation. When you’re ready to leave, choose an exit that offers convenient access to Town Hall. If you’d like a coffee, check the menu on-site; please note that you do not need to make a purchase to enjoy these public spaces.
## Timing
Allow 30 minutes to explore the central atrium and the first-level galleries, or 60 minutes for a more leisurely stroll through both sides of the building, including reading the informational displays. Please be aware that the operating hours for individual shops may differ from the building’s general access hours; it is best to visit the public atrium first, then explore the various levels at your own pace.
## Getting there and costs
Located at 455 George Street, the building is easily accessible from Town Hall Station and the light rail line. Shopping, café offerings, and paid historical tours are separate services.
## Highlights
You might approach your architectural observation in three stages: first, take in the depth of the atrium from the ground floor; next, head to the open galleries to view the central dome and the clock; finally, take a closer look at the stained glass and floor tiles. Please avoid lingering near the exits of escalators, and refrain from using shop doorways as makeshift tripods or camera supports—find a spacious area to stand before looking up.
## Nearby food
The building offers various options for coffee, refreshments, and light meals. If you wish to continue exploring the surrounding area, you can exit onto either George Street or York Street. Check the menus and operating hours for each level; you can easily combine a stroll through the public spaces with shopping or a paid tour—or simply visit solely to appreciate the architecture.
en.tips: While the interior provides shelter from the rain, please note that you may still be exposed to the elements when traveling to or from the nearby station. Taking photos at the exits of escalators or in narrow corridors obstructs the flow of foot traffic; please move to a more spacious area. Please note that paid guided tours require separate booking and are scheduled for specific times; access to public areas does not grant entry to individual shops or restricted "back-of-house" spaces.

items.title: 克利夫顿花园保护地
items.summary: 在Chowder Bay草地与沙滩边看港湾，走短线、野餐，避开正在维修的浴场与码头。
items.guide:
## 简介
Clifton Gardens位于Mosman面向Chowder Bay的一侧，绿地、沙滩、临水设施与后方树林叠在一起。海湾空间比长海滩紧凑，从草地就能看见水面，适合不想长途行走、但又想离开城市街道的人。岸边还能看到港口休闲与船艇活动如何共享一片水域。

这一带的海湾历史和悉尼港的防务、海事及休闲用途有关；附近Chowder Bay保留的旧防务建筑，与今日餐饮和公共步道共同构成地景。到Clifton Gardens可以把重点放在开放草地与沙滩边，历史建筑作为远近背景观看。浴场和码头目前正在整修，普通到访不需要以走上栈桥或使用泳区作为目的，围绕开放陆侧仍可完成一次野餐和看景。
## 这样逛
1. 从Morella Road方向公共入口进入，先看施工围挡和开放草地位置，找一处能看见海湾的休息点。车辆到访先确认车场入口和关门时间，步行不穿越施工区域。
2. 沿开放沙滩后方或公共岸线走一小段，看海湾、船只和对面林地。浴场与码头有维修限制，停在围挡外的稳定路面看景，不绕过围栏寻找栈桥末端的拍照位。
3. 回草地野餐或休息，带孩子可用开放游乐设施，再沿原路返回。若想加Chowder Bay方向短步道，先看现场开放标识并留返程体力，第一次到访只做海湾与草地也很完整。
## 时间怎么用
60分钟适合岸边短线和休息；90至120分钟可慢吃野餐。去其他防务遗址或走到Taronga方向会明显增加路程，不在这次普通短途里默认加入。 夜间以岸边散步、听海和休息为主，沿入口附近能看清路面的公共路径往返；不下水、不走礁石、崖边或无照明的延伸山径。救生巡逻、浴场设施和停车场有各自时间，不能把可到岸边等同于有人巡逻或可夜泳。
## 怎么去与花费
导航Clifton Gardens Reserve, Morella Road, Mosman。公交到附近高地后仍有下坡与返程爬坡，自驾使用正规收费车场。Morella Road车场通常21:30关门、6:00开放，白天游览仍提前收拾离开。普通小规模野餐无需场地预约，交通、餐饮与停车另计。
## 附近餐饮
带轻便野餐和水最方便，周边开放餐饮可作额外补给。公共野餐桌不接受预留，没空桌就换草地休息；不把店家的露台或专用座位当公共用餐区。
items.tips: 按围挡避开浴场、码头整修范围，岸上看景不要求下水。船艇与钓鱼活动附近留出距离，儿童在水边由成人照看。这里有分时分区的狗活动安排，按现场标识走，不能把所有沙滩与泳区当犬只活动区。

en.title: Clifton Gardens Reserve
en.summary: Enjoy views of the harbor from the grassy areas and beach at Chowder Bay. Take a short walk or have a picnic, while being sure to steer clear of the baths and jetty, which are currently undergoing repairs.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Located in Mosman and facing Chowder Bay, Clifton Gardens features a blend of green spaces, sandy beaches, waterfront amenities, and surrounding woodlands. The bay area is more compact than a long, expansive beach, with the water visible directly from the grassy lawns—an ideal destination for those who wish to escape the city streets without having to walk long distances. Along the shore, you can observe how recreational harbor activities and boating coexist within the same waters.

The history of this bay is tied to the defense, maritime, and recreational uses of Sydney Harbour. Nearby, the preserved historic defense structures at Chowder Bay now sit alongside contemporary dining venues and public walking paths, shaping the local landscape. When visiting Clifton Gardens, focus on the open lawns and the beachfront, while viewing the historic buildings as part of the backdrop. As the baths and the jetty are currently undergoing renovations, you may not be able to walk out onto the pier or access the swimming areas; however, the open land-side grounds remain perfectly suited for a picnic or simply taking in the scenery.
## How to explore
1. Enter via the public access point on Morella Road. Take note of the construction fencing and open grassy areas, then find a spot to rest while enjoying the view of the bay. If arriving by car, check the parking entrance and closing time; when on foot, ensure you do not cross into construction zones.
2. Take a short walk along the area behind the beach or the public shoreline to view the bay, the boats, and the wooded area on the opposite side. Please note that the baths and the jetty are currently restricted due to maintenance; view the scenery from stable ground outside the construction fencing, and do not bypass barriers to reach the end of the jetty for photos.
3. Return to the grassy area for a picnic or a rest—children can make use of the available playground facilities—before heading back the way you came. If you wish to add a short walk toward Chowder Bay, check the on-site signage first and ensure you have enough energy for the return trip; for a first-time visit, simply enjoying the bay and the grassy area makes for a complete experience.
## Timing
A 60-minute visit is sufficient for a short walk along the shore and a brief rest; 90 to 120 minutes allows for a leisurely picnic. Visiting other historic defense sites or walking toward Taronga would significantly extend the distance and is not included in this standard short-trip itinerary. After dark this is a shore-side walk and a chance to sit and listen to the water. Stay on visible public paths close to the approach; do not swim, enter rock platforms or continue onto unlit cliffs or bush tracks. Lifeguard patrols, bathing facilities, toilets and car parks have separate hours; public shore access does not imply a patrolled swim or an open car park.
## Getting there and costs
Set your navigation to Clifton Gardens Reserve, Morella Road, Mosman. If arriving by public transport, be aware that there is a downhill walk to the reserve and an uphill climb on the return; if driving, please use the designated paid parking facilities. The parking lot on Morella Road typically closes at 21:30 and opens at 06:00; please plan to depart well before closing. Small-scale, casual picnics do not require a site reservation; please note that transport, food, and parking are separate considerations.
## Nearby food
Bringing your own light picnic and water is the most convenient option, though there are food and beverage outlets nearby for additional supplies. Public picnic tables cannot be reserved—if none are available, feel free to relax on the grass instead. Please do not use the terraces or designated seating areas belonging to local businesses as public dining space.
en.tips: Respect the barriers around the baths and jetty renovation zones; you can enjoy the scenery from the shore without needing to enter the water. Keep a safe distance from areas where boating or fishing is taking place, and ensure children are supervised by an adult when near the water. There are designated times and zones for dogs—please follow the on-site signage, as not all beach or swimming areas are permitted for canine use.

items.title: 比尔戈拉海滩
items.summary: 走进绿坡包围的小海湾，看金色沙岸与两端岬角。
items.guide:
## 简介
Bilgola Beach夹在Newport与Avalon之间，约500米长的沙滩背后是陡升的绿色坡地。高处的Barrenjoey Road绕行山坡，下方小海湾则由The Serpentine连接，海岸与主干道之间有鲜明的上下层关系。它最有辨识度的风景是金橙色沙岸、植被和两端岩岬一起构成的弧线。

“Belgoula”这一地名在测量师James Meehan的1814年记录中已经出现，后来逐渐使用Bilgola拼写。20世纪初McLurcan家族的宅地及周边棕榈，也是地方历史的一部分。1960年代曾设想以桥梁绕过弯曲山路，计划没有实现；今天依山转弯的道路与保留的坡地，仍影响着这里与邻近街区的空间关系。
## 这样逛
1. 从The Serpentine进入海滩公共区域，在靠近救生俱乐部的位置先看海湾全景。认清离开时上坡的方向，再去沙地；下公交后的步行也算一段坡路，别刚到就安排整片海滩往返。
2. 沿干燥沙岸往一端短走，观察沙色、树木和岬角的层次。可把低处的海湾与背后植被一起入画，停留时让开出入口。两端岩石前保持距离，不为寻找“空无一人”的角度绕到岬角后方。
3. 返回俱乐部附近，想看泳池可沿南端正式开放通道到陆侧观景，再回公共休息区域。用一点时间坐下看浪，最后从原路返回The Serpentine；这一小海湾本身已足够，不必继续翻坡去Avalon。
## 时间怎么用
45分钟看海湾和一段沙岸；90分钟可加泳池观景、休息与慢慢返回坡路。日间山坡投影会移动，选择休息处时先看看接下来的阳光方向。 夜间以岸边散步、听海和休息为主，沿入口附近能看清路面的公共路径往返；不下水、不走礁石、崖边或无照明的延伸山径。救生巡逻、浴场设施和停车场有各自时间，不能把可到岸边等同于有人巡逻或可夜泳。
## 怎么去与花费
导航Bilgola Beach, The Serpentine。公交在Barrenjoey Road附近下车后需沿合法人行连接下坡，过主路使用安全过街设施，不能照直横穿弯道。自驾走The Serpentine到合法车位，按标识付费。个人岸边散步无需预约，停车与餐饮另计。
## 附近餐饮
可先看俱乐部附近当时营业的咖啡或外带窗口；需要更多选择，可在到达前于Avalon或Newport商区吃好再来。小海湾不适合临时来回找店，带一瓶水和简单点心能把时间留给沙滩。
items.tips: 上下坡穿稳固的鞋，不把沿公路车道步行当作捷径。海滩两端有礁石和水流影响，观景留在陆侧与干燥沙地。不要进入坡上住宅或以找历史宅邸为由打扰住户。

en.title: Bilgola Beach
en.summary: Step into this small bay, cradled by green hills, and take in the golden sands framed by headlands at either end.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Nestled between Newport and Avalon, Bilgola Beach features a 500-meter stretch of sand backed by steep, verdant slopes. Barrenjoey Road winds along the hillside above, while the small cove below is connected by a road called The Serpentine—creating a distinct vertical separation between the coastline and the main thoroughfare. The beach’s most iconic vista is the sweeping arc formed by its golden-orange sands, lush vegetation, and the rocky headlands at either end.

The name "Belgoula" appeared in surveyor James Meehan’s records as early as 1814, eventually evolving into the current spelling, "Bilgola." The early 20th-century homestead of the McLurcan family, along with its surrounding palm trees, remains a piece of local history. In the 1960s, there was a proposal to bypass the winding hillside road with a bridge, but the plan never materialized; today, the road that hugs the contours of the hill and the preserved slopes continue to shape the spatial relationship between this area and the neighboring streets.
## How to explore
1. Access the public beach area via The Serpentine. Before heading down to the sand, take in the panoramic view of the cove from near the surf lifesaving club. Note the direction of the uphill path for your return—remember that the walk from the bus stop also involves an incline, so plan your visit accordingly rather than attempting to traverse the entire length of the beach.
2. Take a short stroll along the dry sand to observe the interplay between the color of the sand, the surrounding vegetation, and the headlands. You can frame the bay below along with the surrounding vegetation, while ensuring you don’t block the access points. Keep a respectful distance from the rock formations at either end of the beach; there is no need to venture behind the headlands in search of a "completely deserted" spot.
3. Back near the surf club, you can view the ocean pool by taking the designated public access path on the southern side, then return to the public seating area. Take a moment to sit and watch the waves before heading back the way you came via The Serpentine. This small bay is a destination in itself—there’s no need to trek over the hill to Avalon.
## Timing
Allow 45 minutes to explore the bay and the stretch of sand; 90 minutes will give you time to view the ocean pool, relax, and take a leisurely walk back up the slope. As the sun moves throughout the day, the shadows cast by the hillside will shift—check the direction of the sunlight before choosing a spot to rest. After dark this is a shore-side walk and a chance to sit and listen to the water. Stay on visible public paths close to the approach; do not swim, enter rock platforms or continue onto unlit cliffs or bush tracks. Lifeguard patrols, bathing facilities, toilets and car parks have separate hours; public shore access does not imply a patrolled swim or an open car park.
## Getting there and costs
Set your navigation to "The Serpentine, Bilgola Beach." If arriving by bus, get off near Barrenjoey Road and follow the designated pedestrian path downhill; use the official crossing facilities to get across the main road—never attempt to cross directly across the bend. If driving, follow The Serpentine to a legal parking space and pay according to the posted signage. No reservation is required for a casual stroll along the shore; parking and dining are separate matters.
## Nearby food
Check what’s open near the surf club—there may be a café or a takeaway window. If you’d like more options, consider grabbing a bite in the commercial areas of Avalon or Newport before you arrive. This small bay isn't the place to wander around looking for shops; bring a bottle of water and a light snack so you can spend your time enjoying the beach.
en.tips: Wear sturdy footwear for the slopes, and do not use the road (intended for vehicles) as a shortcut. Be mindful of the rocks and currents at both ends of the beach; stick to the landward side or the dry sand. Please do not enter private residential properties on the hillside, and do not disturb residents under the guise of searching for historic homes.

items.title: 新南威尔士州立图书馆
items.summary: 参观图书馆公共阅览与展示空间，特藏和活动按独立规则安排。
items.guide:
## 简介
State Library of New South Wales是面向公众的研究与特藏图书馆，馆藏渊源可追溯到1826年的Australian Subscription Library，1869年成为公共机构。位于Shakespeare Place的Mitchell Wing由Walter Liberty Vernon参与设计，1905至1910年建造，后来又逐步扩充，今天的馆舍同时承载建筑、研究与展览功能。

这里保存着大量与澳大利亚及太平洋地区相关的手稿、地图、照片和其他资料，公众展览把其中一部分从研究库藏带到日常观看中。参观可同时看建筑细节、不同年代的图像以及人们如何记录城市；它既是一处安静阅读空间，也是一座可以从物件与图像理解历史的文化机构。
## 这样逛
1. 到Shakespeare Place / Macquarie Street一侧先看建筑与入口指示，在服务台确认当天开放的公共阅览、展览与走廊，特藏阅览室或活动区不当自由穿行空间。
2. 以Mitchell建筑的公共空间为起点，观察建筑细节与图书馆历史；如展览区开放，选一个关于地图、照片、艺术或悉尼历史的主题，慢看几件馆藏。
3. 再到允许公众使用的阅读区域找座位，读一段与刚才展览有关的书或资料。参观结束前按当天动线返回，不在需要读者证或预约的区域追逐旧照片里的“网红机位”。
## 时间怎么用
60分钟看建筑与一个展览；120分钟可加阅读与另一个主题。公共楼层、阅览室、咖啡区和活动各有时段，公共阅览、展览与餐饮按各自时段使用。
## 怎么去与花费
地址1 Shakespeare Place, Sydney，靠近Martin Place / St James一带。特藏、研究调阅与活动须另看预约和读者要求，餐饮与特殊服务另计。
## 附近餐饮
馆内咖啡按当天营业安排使用，也可回Martin Place或Macquarie Street周边用餐。若打算连续阅读，先看展览再休息，餐后回来专心读一段会比不断穿行更容易进入状态。
items.tips: 保持安静，拍照与包袋要求看入口和展厅提示；不触碰未开放互动的手稿或展品。座位先选空闲座位使用。需要辅助通路可先联系服务台，按楼内导览选择通路。

en.title: State Library of New South Wales
en.summary: These guidelines apply to the library’s public reading areas and exhibition spaces. Special collections and events are subject to separate policies.
en.guide:
## Introduction
The State Library of New South Wales is a research and special collections library open to the public. Its origins can be traced back to the Australian Subscription Library, established in 1826, which became a public institution in 1869. The Mitchell Wing, located on Shakespeare Place, was designed with the involvement of Walter Liberty Vernon and constructed between 1905 and 1910. Following subsequent expansions, the current facility now serves as a venue for architecture, research, and exhibitions.

The library houses an extensive collection of manuscripts, maps, photographs, and other materials related to Australia and the Pacific region. Through public exhibitions, a selection of these items is brought out from the research archives for general viewing. Visitors can appreciate the architectural details, explore imagery from various eras, and discover how people have documented the city. It functions both as a quiet space for reading and as a cultural institution where history can be understood through objects and images.
## How to explore
1. Upon arriving at the Shakespeare Place/Macquarie Street side, take note of the building and entrance signage. Check with the service desk to confirm which public reading rooms, exhibition spaces, and corridors are open that day; please note that special collection reading rooms and event areas are not accessible for casual exploration.
2. Begin in the public areas of the Mitchell Wing to observe the architectural details and the history of the library. If exhibitions are open, choose a theme—such as maps, photography, art, or the history of Sydney—and take your time viewing a few items from the collection.
3. Afterward, find a seat in a designated public reading area and spend some time reading a book or document related to the exhibition you just visited. When concluding your visit, follow the designated route back to the exit; please refrain from entering areas that require a reader’s card or a prior appointment in search of "Instagrammable" spots seen in historical photographs.
## Timing
A 60-minute visit allows time to explore the architecture and one exhibition; a 120-minute visit provides additional time for reading and exploring a second thematic area. Please be aware that public floors, reading rooms, café areas, and event spaces have specific operating hours; ensure you use these facilities—including public reading areas, exhibitions, and dining services—within their respective designated times.
## Getting there and costs
Address: 1 Shakespeare Place, Sydney (near Martin Place/St James). Access to special collections, research materials, and events is subject to specific appointment and reader requirements. Dining and other specialized services are handled separately.
## Nearby food
The café inside the library operates according to the day’s schedule; alternatively, you can dine in the vicinity of Martin Place or Macquarie Street. If you plan to spend an extended period reading, it is better to visit the exhibitions first, take a break for a meal, and then return to focus on your reading—this approach makes it easier to settle into a deep state of concentration than constantly moving back and forth.
en.tips: Please maintain a quiet environment. Refer to the signage at entrances and within exhibition halls for rules regarding photography and the handling of bags. Do not touch manuscripts or exhibits unless they are explicitly designated for interactive use. You may occupy any available seat. If you require accessible routes, please consult the service desk or follow the building’s wayfinding signage.

items.title: 环形码头 Circular Quay
items.summary: 沿东西两岸看渡轮与城市地标，想加乘Manly渡轮也有清楚的出发思路。
items.guide:
## 简介
Circular Quay位于Sydney Cove，也称Warrane，是悉尼从海港聚落发展为现代城市的重要起点。欧洲殖民船队于1788年在附近建立聚落，之前这里已是Gadigal人的生活海岸。名字里的“环形”来自早期围绕海湾的弧形岸线与码头，而今天填筑、改造后的岸边更接近矩形；理解这一点，再看老海关、仓储遗迹和渡轮泊位，就能读出城市不断向水面扩展的过程。

这里兼有交通枢纽和步行观景带的双重性：渡轮、火车、轻轨在同一片区域相接，东西两岸分别通向歌剧院与The Rocks。海港大桥与歌剧院并不需要同时挤进一张照片，沿码头多走几百米就能改变角度。Manly公共渡轮本身也是经典观光体验，但它有船费、候船和返程，本条免费散步不把渡轮行程算作已经完成；想乘船可在现场线路屏幕选择F1，并为Manly另留半天左右的完整时间。
## 这样逛
1. 从码头南端公共步道开始，先看各泊位的目的地显示屏，分清公共渡轮、私人游船与快船，不进入排队闸口拍照。回望海关和高架铁路，观察老港口与现代交通叠在一起的街景。
2. 向东走到East Circular Quay，看渡轮进出和大桥方向；再沿原路回到湾底，根据体力继续到西侧MCA外的公共岸边，获得与东岸不同的歌剧院视角。
3. 在公共座椅停留后回交通站点。若决定加乘Manly渡轮，核对F1当前时刻及返程，公共Opal/银行卡与私人快船票不能想当然混用；船上选择允许的露天区域并扶好栏杆。
## 时间怎么用
45分钟走南岸与一侧海边；90分钟可覆盖东西两岸并休息。单程Manly渡轮约20–30分钟只是航程，排队、候船、游Manly和返航都要另外留时。 夜间也可沿可通行的公共步道或建筑外侧散步，挑能看清台阶与路面的路线往返；室内、泳池、活动区域和园内设施按各自开放安排。
## 怎么去与花费
导航Circular Quay，火车、L2/L3轻轨与多条渡轮抵达。公共岸边散步免费；乘船另付交通费，遵从码头当天屏幕。付费游船推销点不是公共渡轮唯一购票处。
## 附近餐饮
码头简餐方便但价格偏游客区，可步行到The Rocks或往市中心一两条街再用餐。食物留在有座位的位置，海鸥会抢露天食物。
items.tips: 不要挡住上下船人流或进入工作人员区域；近水看好儿童。大邮轮停靠时西侧视线会改变，改走东岸即可。

en.title: Circular Quay
en.summary: Explore both the eastern and western shores to view the ferries and city landmarks; you will also find clear information on how to board the Manly ferry if you choose to do so.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Circular Quay, located at Sydney Cove—also known as Warrane—marks a pivotal starting point in Sydney’s evolution from a harbor-side settlement into a modern metropolis. While the area became the site of a European colonial settlement in 1788, it had long served as a coastal home for the Gadigal people. The term "circular" refers to the original curved shoreline and wharves that once hugged the bay; today, following extensive land reclamation and redevelopment, the waterfront has taken on a more rectangular shape. Recognizing this transformation—while observing the old Customs House, remnants of historic warehouses, and the ferry berths—reveals the story of a city that has continuously expanded outward into the harbor.

This area functions as both a transport hub and a scenic pedestrian promenade. Ferries, trains, and light rail converge here, with the eastern and western shores leading toward the Sydney Opera House and The Rocks, respectively. You do not need to cram both the Harbour Bridge and the Opera House into a single photograph; simply walking a few hundred meters further along the wharves will provide a different perspective. While the public ferry to Manly offers a classic sightseeing experience, it involves fares, waiting times, and a return journey—therefore, this self-guided walking tour does not include the ferry trip. If you wish to take the ferry, look for the "F1" route on the digital displays at the terminal, and plan to set aside about half a day for a dedicated visit to Manly.
## How to explore
1. Start at the public walkway on the southern end of the wharf. Check the destination displays at each berth to distinguish between public ferries, private cruise vessels, and fast ferries. Do not enter the boarding gates just to take photos. Look back toward the Customs House and the elevated railway to observe the juxtaposition of the historic port and modern transport infrastructure.
2. Walk east toward East Circular Quay to watch the ferries arrive and depart, with the Harbour Bridge in view. Retrace your steps back to the head of the bay; if you have the energy, continue to the western side—near the Museum of Contemporary Art (MCA)—for a different perspective of the Opera House compared to the eastern side.
3. After a rest on the public seating, head back to the transport hub. If you decide to take the Manly ferry, check the current F1 route schedule and return times. Note that public transport payment methods (Opal cards or bank cards) cannot be used for private fast ferries. When on board, stay within designated outdoor areas and hold onto the railings.
## Timing
A 45-minute visit covers the southern shore and one side of the harbour; a 90-minute visit allows for exploring both the eastern and western sides with time for a break. A one-way trip to Manly takes about 20–30 minutes, but remember to factor in extra time for queuing, waiting, exploring Manly, and the return journey. Evening visits use public paths and building exteriors where you can see the surface and steps clearly. Interiors, pools, event zones and other facilities retain their own access arrangements.
## Getting there and costs
Navigate to Circular Quay, which is accessible by train, L2/L3 light rail, and various ferry services. Walking along the public waterfront is free; ferry travel requires a fare—please follow the information displayed on the wharf’s screens that day. Be aware that kiosks selling private commercial cruises are not the only places to purchase tickets for public ferries.
## Nearby food
While quick bites are available on the wharf, prices reflect the tourist-heavy location; consider walking to The Rocks or a street or two further into the city centre for a meal. If you are eating outdoors, keep a close eye on your food—seagulls will swoop in to snatch it.
en.tips: Do not obstruct the flow of passengers boarding or disembarking, and avoid entering staff-only areas. Keep a close watch on children when near the water. When large cruise ships are docked, the view from the western side may be obstructed; simply head to the eastern side instead.

items.title: Opera Bar海港露台
items.summary: 在歌剧院下层海港露台坐一会儿，看渡轮与城市夜景。
items.guide:
## 简介
Opera Bar位于悉尼歌剧院Lower Concourse，靠近水面的高度，使它与广场上仰望白色屋顶的体验很不一样：视线沿着港湾展开，海港大桥、Circular Quay和渡轮成为前景。歌剧院1973年启用的建筑背景当然是这里最鲜明的部分，但酒吧是其中独立经营的餐饮空间，不等于买到剧场参观或演出票。把公共广场散步和到露台坐下看景分开安排，会更清楚哪些内容免费、哪些属于消费。

这里的吸引力主要在公共建筑、水面与城市生活同时入画。日落后可以慢慢看渡轮灯光移动，不需要追求特殊节庆或固定烟花。现场往往热闹，风声、音乐与周围谈话都会进入体验；若只想安静独处，先沿公共岸边走一段，再决定是否入座，比把第一排座位当作唯一目标轻松。
## 这样逛
1. 从Circular Quay东侧公共岸边走向歌剧院，找到Lower Concourse的餐饮入口，不沿剧场票务或后台通道穿行。先看当前露台开放和座位安排。
2. 选座后按现场点单方式选择一份饮品或餐食，拍照时保留公共通行宽度。想看海港大桥，可留意面向西侧港湾的位置；如果座位已满，可先在公共岸边散步，不占用已预留餐桌。
3. 结束后沿来时岸边回Circular Quay，认清火车、轻轨或渡轮入口；已关门的植物园不是返程捷径，深夜也不把“码头在”当作仍有渡轮。
## 时间怎么用
45–60分钟适合饮品与看景，90–120分钟可加用餐和广场散步。官网列每日10时至午夜，厨房及不同点餐区按现场服务安排；较晚到访以饮品短停为主。
## 怎么去与花费
地址Sydney Opera House, Lower Concourse Level, Bennelong Point。从Circular Quay步行约7–10分钟，按歌剧院外部公共通道前往下层海滨；开车落客在Macquarie Street指定位置后仍需步行。公共外部散步不需购买酒吧餐食，入座点单按菜单、份量和适用附加费计算；剧场、导览、停车和交通另付。酒吧消费没有统一上限。
## 附近餐饮
可以只选一杯无酒精饮品，也可以按当时菜单选一份轻食或共享菜，先按食量少点。想吃完整晚餐应较早安排，不能因为酒吧到午夜就推断厨房连续供应全部菜单。海鸥会靠近食物，桌面保持整洁，不投喂。
items.tips: 这是热闹的海滨餐饮空间，想聊天可先挑远离音箱的位置。带外层防风，不在近水边缘放松对儿童的照看；酒精服务按18岁以上和店方入场规则执行。

en.title: Opera Bar
en.summary: A harbour-side pause below the Opera House, with ferries and the city lights in view.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Opera Bar occupies the Lower Concourse of the Sydney Opera House, close enough to the water to give a different perspective from the forecourt above. The Harbour Bridge, Circular Quay and passing ferries become part of the foreground. The Opera House, opened in 1973, supplies the architectural setting, but the bar is a separately operated hospitality space. A drink here does not include a theatre tour or a performance ticket. Distinguishing a public exterior walk from sitting down to order makes the visit easy to plan.

The experience brings together the harbour, public architecture and the working rhythms of the city. After sunset you can watch lights move across the water without waiting for a festival or expecting fireworks. Music, wind and conversation can make the space lively rather than quiet. If you want time alone, walk the public shoreline first, then decide whether a table suits your mood instead of treating a front-row seat as essential.
## How to explore
1. Follow the public eastern Circular Quay waterfront towards the Opera House and find the Lower Concourse hospitality area. Do not cut through theatre-ticket queues or backstage passages. Check the available terrace and seating arrangements before settling in.
2. Order from the operating service point or ordering system at your table. A drink or one dish is a sufficient start. Keep the public passage clear when taking photos and look towards the western harbour for the bridge. If seats are full, continue the public walk rather than occupying a reserved table.
3. Return along the same waterfront to Circular Quay and identify your train, light-rail or ferry entrance. Closed Botanic Garden gates are not a shortcut, and an accessible wharf does not mean a ferry is still running.
## Timing
Allow 45–60 minutes for a drink and view, or 90–120 minutes with food and an exterior stroll. The operator lists 10:00–midnight daily. Kitchen and ordering-area service is separate; a late visit should work as a drinks stop. 
## Getting there and costs
Use Sydney Opera House, Lower Concourse Level, Bennelong Point as the destination. Circular Quay is about 7–10 minutes away on foot. Vehicle drop-off is on the designated Macquarie Street approach, with a walk remaining. The public exterior is free to walk; seated food and drinks follow the menu, quantities ordered and any applicable surcharges. Theatre tickets, tours, parking and transport are separate, with no fixed ceiling on bar spending.
## Nearby food
A non-alcoholic drink is a practical choice. For food, begin with a light meal or something to share rather than ordering everything at once. Come earlier for a complete dinner; midnight bar trading does not promise the whole food menu until midnight. Keep food attended and do not feed the gulls.
en.tips: Choose a position away from speakers if conversation matters. Bring a windproof layer and supervise children near the water. Alcohol service is for adults 18 and over; follow the venue’s entry arrangements.

items.title: 海德公园兵营博物馆
items.summary: 通过自助音频体验了解兵营历史；最后入场16:30，建议提前预约。
items.guide:
## 简介
Hyde Park Barracks由曾是囚犯的建筑师Francis Greenway设计，1817至1819年建造，最初为男性流放犯提供集中住宿。这座砖建筑与院落是悉尼殖民历史的重要遗存，也作为Australian Convict Sites的一部分被列入世界遗产；后来场所又与女性移民、收容及行政用途联系在一起。

今天的参观重点是建筑、考古物与个人经历之间的关系。墙面、房间与日常小物件不只是背景，音频会把它们放进居住、劳动、迁移与制度的故事中；同时也需要关注殖民扩张对原住民社群的影响，避免只把这里看作一栋漂亮的老房子。
## 这样逛
1. 到 Queens Square 的入口报到，领取馆方提供的播放器与耳机，先试音量和操作；普通个人参观可提前预约时段，减少到门口等待。
2. 跟着音频与现场动线进入旧兵营空间，从流放者的生活、物品和建筑痕迹开始看，给每个故事留出听完的时间。
3. 继续看后来女性移民、收容与殖民影响的叙事，对照原住民视角理解这片地方的不同经历；完成后归还设备，再回院落看建筑外观。
## 时间怎么用
60分钟走核心音频路线；90分钟可慢读展签、在院落整理参观感受。音频场次约每半小时安排，馆方最后入场16:30；请在最后入场前抵达，留足完整参观时间。
## 怎么去与花费
Macquarie Street / Queens Square，靠近 St James 或 Martin Place。普通入场免费，建议预约；活动可能另有安排。音频设备由馆方提供，可自带3.5毫米耳机，不能假设蓝牙耳机可连接。
## 参观要点
听音频时留意叙事中的时间与人物身份。流放犯、移民与管理者的处境不同，同一个房间在不同时期也可能承担不同用途；把两种视角放在一起，能更清楚地理解制度与日常生活之间的关系。
## 附近餐饮
参观后可沿Macquarie Street或向Martin Place方向找咖啡与简餐。先归还音频设备再离馆用餐，避免为赶餐食漏掉结尾；随身水和点心在允许区域使用，展厅内按馆方规定收好。
items.tips: 官方音频体验建议8岁及以上；涉及监禁与殖民历史，按自身接受程度选择。旧建筑的楼梯和动线需要留意，需要辅助路线请先联系馆方。保持耳机音量适中，别边听边急走或挡住通道。

en.title: Hyde Park Barracks
en.summary: Explore the history of the barracks through a self-guided audio tour. Last entry is at 16:30; advance booking is recommended.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Designed by the architect Francis Greenway—himself a former convict—and built between 1817 and 1819, the Hyde Park Barracks originally served as a centralized lodging facility for male convicts. This brick complex and its courtyard are significant remnants of Sydney’s colonial history and are inscribed as part of the "Australian Convict Sites" World Heritage property. Over time, the site also became associated with female immigrants, institutional care, and various administrative functions.

Today, the visitor experience focuses on the interplay between the architecture, archaeological artifacts, and the personal stories of those who lived here. The walls, rooms, and everyday objects are more than just a backdrop; the audio guide weaves them into narratives of daily life, labor, migration, and institutional control. It is also essential to consider the impact of colonial expansion on Indigenous communities, rather than viewing the site merely as a picturesque historic building.
## How to explore
1. Check in at the entrance on Queens Square to collect your audio guide and headphones. Take a moment to test the volume and controls. For individual visits, booking a time slot in advance is recommended to minimize wait times upon arrival.
2. Follow the audio guide and the suggested route into the former barracks. Begin by exploring the lives of the convicts, the artifacts they left behind, and the physical traces within the architecture—be sure to allow enough time to listen to each story in full.
3. Continue through the narratives concerning female immigrants, institutional care, and the broader colonial impact. Consider the site’s history from the perspective of Indigenous peoples to gain a more nuanced understanding of the diverse experiences that unfolded here. Once finished, return your equipment and take a final look at the building’s exterior from the courtyard.
## Timing
A core visit following the audio guide takes approximately 60 minutes; a 90-minute visit allows time to read the exhibition labels more thoroughly and reflect on your experience while in the courtyard. Audio sessions are scheduled roughly every half hour, and the final admission is at 16:30. Please arrive before this cutoff to ensure you have sufficient time for a complete visit.
## Getting there and costs
Located on Macquarie Street / Queens Square, near St James or Martin Place. General admission is free; advance booking is recommended. Special events may follow a different schedule. Audio guides are provided by the venue—you may bring your own 3.5mm wired headphones, but please note that Bluetooth headphones may not be compatible.
## Highlights
As you listen to the audio guide, pay close attention to the timeline and the identities of the individuals described. Convicts, immigrants, and administrators experienced life very differently, and the same room may have served various purposes over time. By considering these different perspectives, you can gain a clearer understanding of the relationship between institutional systems and daily life.
## Nearby food
After your visit, you can find coffee and light meals along Macquarie Street or toward Martin Place. Please return your audio guide before leaving to dine, ensuring you don’t miss the conclusion of the narrative. Food and drinks (including water) may only be consumed in designated areas; please stow them away while inside the exhibition galleries, in accordance with venue policy.
en.tips: The official audio tour is recommended for ages 8 and up. As the content covers themes of imprisonment and colonial history, please choose whether to participate based on your own comfort level. Be mindful of the stairs and the layout of this historic building; please contact the venue in advance if you require an accessible route. Keep your headphone volume at a moderate level, and avoid walking too quickly or blocking pathways while listening.

items.title: 柯尔柯尔海滩
items.summary: 从南端海滨看长弧沙滩，在步道上观察海岸地形。
items.guide:
## 简介
Curl Curl位于Freshwater与Dee Why之间，是一片约1.2公里长、面向东南外海的沙滩。人们习惯称它为North Curl Curl和South Curl Curl，两端各有救生俱乐部与海水泳池；本页把同一片海岸作为一个目的地。北端泻湖、连续的沙丘与南端岩岸共同构成它的地貌，视线比港内小海湾更开阔，也更能感受到外海风浪。

当地旧地名的范围与今天不同：现在的Curl Curl Lagoon过去称Harbord Lagoon，后来才调整为现名。因此看旧照片或历史地图时，要先辨认海湾和泻湖的位置。今天南端的海滨公共空间与向Freshwater方向延伸的高位步道，使不下水的人也能方便地观察这片冲浪海岸。
## 这样逛
1. 以Carrington Parade的South Curl Curl为起点，在俱乐部旁海滨路径看海湾全景。先分辨脚下的沙滩、南端泳池和北面长海岸的位置；若只想轻松走走，就在这一带选一段平整路径往返。
2. 向南侧正式海岸步道走一小段，从高于沙滩的位置回望Curl Curl。留意岩层、岬角与沙滩之间的高度变化，遇到第一个适合停留的开阔处便可折返；这段重点是换视角，不需要一路走到Freshwater。
3. 回到海边后决定是否加走沙滩。体力足可向北走15至20分钟，再沿原方向返回；沙地比人行道费力，想去北端泻湖须额外留出回程。若主要想观察泻湖，也可一开始就把到访起点改为North Curl Curl，避免横穿整片沙滩。
## 时间怎么用
60分钟足够南端海滨与一小段高位步道；120分钟可加向北的沙滩往返和休息。南北两端不是相邻的两个路口，不要把走到北端后返回的时间忽略。日间光线充足时更容易看清台阶与路面。 夜间以岸边散步、听海和休息为主，沿入口附近能看清路面的公共路径往返；不下水、不走礁石、崖边或无照明的延伸山径。救生巡逻、浴场设施和停车场有各自时间，不能把可到岸边等同于有人巡逻或可夜泳。
## 怎么去与花费
南端导航South Curl Curl Beach或Carrington Parade，北端导航North Curl Curl Beach；到访前先选好公交下车位置。两端均有停车区域，一般游客按计费器付费。普通海滩到访免费，无需预约；泳池清洁、俱乐部活动和咖啡消费另有安排。
## 附近餐饮
南端俱乐部附近有面海咖啡与简餐选择，适合步道折返后休息；北端周边餐饮较分散，若从那里开始可自带轻食和水。用餐前先把沙从鞋底和衣物抖净，外带食品在允许停留的公共空间享用。
items.tips: 海风大时别把相机或手机放在栏杆上；沿高位路径走，遇到围挡原路返回。沙滩往返可穿运动鞋，想省体力就留在海滨路径。不要把拍摄冲浪者的位置选在泳池出口或俱乐部器材通道。

en.title: Curl Curl Beach
en.summary: Take in the sweeping arc of the beach from the southern waterfront, and observe the coastal topography as you walk along the trail.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Situated between Freshwater and Dee Why, Curl Curl is a beach approximately 1.2 kilometers long, facing the open ocean to the southeast. It is commonly referred to as "North Curl Curl" and "South Curl Curl," with a surf lifesaving club and an ocean pool located at each end; for the purpose of this entry, the entire stretch is treated as a single destination. The landscape features a lagoon at the northern end, a continuous stretch of sand dunes, and a rocky shoreline to the south. The view here is more expansive than in the sheltered coves of the harbor, offering a stronger sense of the open ocean’s wind and waves.

Historical place names in the area differ from those used today: what is now known as Curl Curl Lagoon was formerly called Harbord Lagoon, before being renamed to its current designation. When looking at old photographs or historical maps, it is helpful to first identify the locations of the bay and the lagoon. Today, the public waterfront space at the southern end, combined with an elevated coastal path that extends toward Freshwater, allows those who prefer to stay dry to easily observe this surf-swept coastline.
## How to explore
1. Start at South Curl Curl (via Carrington Parade) and take in the panoramic view of the bay from the coastal path next to the surf club. Orient yourself by locating the beach beneath your feet, the ocean pool at the southern end, and the long stretch of coastline to the north. If you prefer a leisurely stroll, simply walk along a flat section of the path in this area and back again.
2. Follow the coastal path heading south for a short distance to view Curl Curl from an elevated vantage point. Observe the rock formations, the headland, and the varying elevations along the beach. You can turn back once you reach the first open area suitable for a pause—the goal here is to gain a new perspective, so there is no need to walk all the way to Freshwater.
3. Once back by the shore, decide whether you would like to walk along the sand. If you have the energy, you can head north for 15–20 minutes before returning the same way. Walking on sand is more strenuous than on a paved path; if you intend to reach the lagoon at the northern end, remember to factor in the time required for the return journey. Alternatively, if your primary interest is the lagoon, you might consider starting your visit at North Curl Curl to avoid crossing the entire length of the beach.
## Timing
60 minutes is sufficient to explore the southern waterfront and a short section of the elevated path. 120 minutes allows for a round trip along the northern stretch of the beach, with time for a break. Note that the northern and southern ends are not immediately adjacent; be sure to account for the time needed to return if you walk all the way to the northern end. The steps and path surfaces are easiest to navigate in good daylight. After dark this is a shore-side walk and a chance to sit and listen to the water. Stay on visible public paths close to the approach; do not swim, enter rock platforms or continue onto unlit cliffs or bush tracks. Lifeguard patrols, bathing facilities, toilets and car parks have separate hours; public shore access does not imply a patrolled swim or an open car park.
## Getting there and costs
For the southern end, set your navigation to South Curl Curl Beach or Carrington Parade; for the northern end, set it to North Curl Curl Beach. Plan your bus drop-off point in advance. Parking is available at both ends, with paid parking (via meters) for visitors. Access to the beach is free and requires no reservation; however, separate arrangements or fees may apply for use of the ocean pool, surf club events, or purchases at local cafés.
## Nearby food
Near the southern end, you will find cafés and casual dining options—perfect for a rest after completing your walk. Dining options are more scattered around the northern end, so if you are starting your journey there, it is best to bring along some light snacks and water. Please shake the sand from your shoes and clothing before dining, and ensure that any food brought from outside is consumed only in designated public areas.
en.tips: When the sea breeze is strong, avoid placing your camera or mobile phone on the railings. Stick to the higher-level paths, and if you encounter any barriers or fencing, please turn back. You can wear sneakers for walking on the beach, but if you prefer to conserve energy, stick to the coastal paths. When photographing surfers, be careful not to position yourself near the exit of the swimming pool or the access paths used by the club for its equipment.

items.title: 悉尼市政厅 Town Hall
items.summary: 从钟塔和砂岩雕饰读悉尼市政史，连走Sydney Square与QVB街景。
items.guide:
## 简介
Town Hall既是市中心常用的集合点，也是悉尼市政历史最直观的一座建筑。市政厅在1868年奠基，经过两大阶段营建，于1889年完成主体；它坐落在早期欧洲移民墓地旧址，地方政府争取独立办公场所的过程，也反映了殖民时期市议会与殖民政府之间的关系。最早设计来自J. H. Willson，后续由多位建筑师修改、续建，因此它并非一次完成的单一作品。

本地砂岩砌筑的立面、钟塔、柱廊和密集雕饰带有鲜明的维多利亚时代市政建筑气质，和街对面的QVB共同构成George Street最有辨识度的历史街景。内部的Centennial Hall以大型管风琴闻名，但建筑今天仍承担办公、会议和演出用途。普通散步的重点是外部建筑及南侧Sydney Square；礼堂、管风琴演奏和室内参观属于另行开放的活动，不能把工作场所当作随时可进的博物馆。
## 这样逛
1. 从George Street正面看钟塔和主入口，先在离轻轨轨道较远的步行区拍全景，再靠近观察砂岩雕饰、柱头与门窗比例。台阶人多时不要堵住出入口。
2. 绕到Druitt Street一侧比较侧立面，再进入市政厅与St Andrew’s Cathedral之间的Sydney Square；从广场看两座砂岩建筑的体量和不同装饰，比只拍正门更完整。
3. 沿George Street走到对面QVB一侧回望市政厅，完成一小段老城建筑环线；想听管风琴可另选官方列出的演奏活动，本次路线不依赖进入礼堂。
## 时间怎么用
30分钟完成正面、侧面与广场；60分钟可逐段观察雕饰，再步行到QVB。白天砂岩细节清楚，建筑灯光下则适合晚间外观短停，晚间也可看灯光下的外观和公共广场。 夜间也可沿可通行的公共步道或建筑外侧散步，挑能看清台阶与路面的路线往返；室内、泳池、活动区域和园内设施按各自开放安排。
## 怎么去与花费
地址483 George Street。Town Hall火车站及Town Hall轻轨站紧邻；出站按市政厅而非Town Hall House办公楼寻找正面。外观和公共广场免费，无需预约。室内活动按各自票务，不含在免费散步里。
## 附近餐饮
QVB地下层、The Galeries与George Street都有简餐和咖啡，适合参观后再选；不要在拥挤的市政厅台阶长时间占位用餐。
items.tips: 穿过George Street注意双向轻轨；不要进入办公门或攀爬雕塑。广场若有活动围挡，沿开放公共步道绕行。

en.title: Sydney Town Hall
en.summary: Explore the history of Sydney’s municipal governance through the clock tower and sandstone carvings, and take in the streetscapes of Sydney Square and the QVB.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Town Hall serves as a common meeting point in the city center and stands as one of the most iconic landmarks of Sydney’s municipal history. The foundation stone was laid in 1868, and following two major phases of construction, the main structure was completed in 1889. It sits on the site of an early European settler cemetery; the local government’s pursuit of an independent administrative space reflects the complex relationship between the municipal council and the colonial government during that era. The initial design came from J. H. Willson, with subsequent modifications and additions by several other architects—meaning it is not a single, unified work completed in one go.

With its façade built from local sandstone, a clock tower, colonnades, and intricate ornamentation, the building embodies the quintessential style of Victorian-era civic architecture. Together with the Queen Victoria Building (QVB) across the street, it forms one of the most recognizable historic streetscapes along George Street. The interior’s Centennial Hall is renowned for its grand pipe organ, though the building continues to function today as a space for offices, meetings, and performances. For casual visitors, the primary points of interest are the exterior architecture and Sydney Square on the southern side. Access to the auditorium, pipe organ recitals, or interior tours is subject to separate arrangements; please remember that this is a working environment, not a museum open to the public at all times.
## How to explore
1. Begin by viewing the clock tower and main entrance from George Street. Capture a panoramic shot from the pedestrian area—ideally further away from the light rail tracks—then move closer to examine the sandstone carvings, column capitals, and the proportions of the doors and windows. Please ensure you do not block the entrance or exit when the steps are crowded.
2. Make your way around to the Druitt Street side to observe the building’s flank, then enter Sydney Square—the space situated between the Town Hall and St Andrew’s Cathedral. Viewing both sandstone structures from this square offers a more comprehensive perspective of their scale and distinct decorative details than focusing solely on the main entrance.
3. Continue along George Street to the side of the Queen Victoria Building (QVB) and look back toward the Town Hall to complete a short circuit of the city’s historic architecture. If you wish to hear the pipe organ, you may check the official schedule for scheduled performances; this suggested route does not require entry into the main auditorium.
## Timing
A visit covering the front, side, and square can be completed in 30 minutes; a 60-minute visit allows for a more detailed look at the carvings before walking over to the QVB. The sandstone details are best appreciated in daylight, though the building’s exterior is also striking when illuminated at night—perfect for a brief evening stop. Evening visits cover the illuminated exterior and public square. Evening visits use public paths and building exteriors where you can see the surface and steps clearly. Interiors, pools, event zones and other facilities retain their own access arrangements.
## Getting there and costs
Located at 483 George Street, the site is immediately adjacent to the Town Hall train and light rail stations. Upon exiting, follow signs for the "Town Hall" (the civic building) rather than "Town Hall House" (the office complex) to find the main entrance. The exterior and the public square are free to visit and require no reservation. Indoor events are subject to separate ticketing and are not included in this self-guided walking route.
## Nearby food
There are various options for light meals and coffee in the QVB basement, The Galeries, and along George Street—ideal for a post-visit break. Please refrain from occupying space on the busy Town Hall steps for extended periods to eat.
en.tips: When crossing George Street, please be mindful of light rail vehicles moving in both directions. Do not enter doors designated for office use, and please do not climb on any sculptures. If parts of the square are cordoned off for an event, please follow the designated public walkways to navigate around the area.

items.title: 沃里伍德海滩
items.summary: 从坡顶看海湾，再下到沙岸听浪，走一段就能换两种景色。
items.guide:
## 简介
Warriewood Beach藏在北部半岛的坡地与岬角之间，主要海滩与上方街道有明显高度差。不同于沿主路平铺展开的长海岸，这里先有俯看海湾的视角，再通过正式下行路线接近沙滩。它北面是Mona Vale方向的高岸，南侧与Turimetta周边的海岸步行环境相邻。

Warriewood一名来自20世纪初分割开发的Warriewood Estate，周边后来逐渐形成今天的住宅街区。海滩本身仍保留被高地围住的空间感，救生俱乐部、观景平台和野餐空间集中在有限区域。来这里的重点可以只是观察地形、看冲浪和短距离散步，没必要把陡坡与长途海岸线同时加入一趟轻松出门。
## 这样逛
1. 从Narrabeen Park Parade附近的公共位置开始，在下坡前先俯看海湾，辨认海滩入口和返回路径。选择能在回程轻松上来的路线，拍照时站在人行区域内，别在弯道车道上停留。
2. 沿正式开放入口下到海滩公共空间，在救生俱乐部附近看浪与沙岸形状。想走沙滩就沿干燥较平缓的一段往返，遇到海水逼近岩壁的地方提前折返，不从礁石绕向Mona Vale。
3. 回到海滩后方野餐或公共休息空间坐一会儿，再慢慢上坡。返回高处后再看一次刚才走过的路线，会更容易读出岬角和海湾的比例。结束前确认返程站点位于道路哪一侧，给上坡后喝水休息留几分钟。
## 时间怎么用
45分钟可看坡顶和海滩入口一带；90分钟适合下沙散步、休息并从容上坡。体力有限时可把重点留在上方合法观景空间。中午坡道较晒，清晨与较凉的白天更舒服。 夜间以岸边散步、听海和休息为主，沿入口附近能看清路面的公共路径往返；不下水、不走礁石、崖边或无照明的延伸山径。救生巡逻、浴场设施和停车场有各自时间，不能把可到岸边等同于有人巡逻或可夜泳。
## 怎么去与花费
地图选择Warriewood Beach，公交通常需要从主干线转接或步行到Narrabeen Park Parade一侧，下车后仍有坡路。自驾可到海滩停车区域，依现场规则付费；不要占用救援或住宅出入口。个人岸边散步无需预约，停车、餐饮与交通另计。
## 附近餐饮
上方Narrabeen Park Parade一带有咖啡与简餐，适合回程上坡后再吃，省去拿着热饮走陡路。若主要想在海边坐一会儿，可提前备水和轻食，在指定野餐区域休息，不依赖俱乐部内部空间。
items.tips: 穿适合坡道的鞋，背包比手提袋方便，给往返上坡留体力。浪拍到的岩面不属于捷径；不要进入滑翔、救援或施工限制区。需要卫生间时可先看俱乐部附近公共设施指示。

en.title: Warriewood Beach
en.summary: You can enjoy two distinct perspectives in one short walk: take in the view of the bay from the top of the slope, then head down to the sandy shore to listen to the crashing waves.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Nestled between the slopes and headlands of the Northern Beaches peninsula, Warriewood Beach sits well below the street level above. Unlike stretches of coastline that unfold flatly along a main road, this location offers an elevated vantage point overlooking the bay before you descend via a designated path to the sand. To the north, the coastline rises toward Mona Vale, while to the south, it connects to the coastal walking trails around Turimetta.

The name "Warriewood" originates from the Warriewood Estate—a subdivision developed in the early 20th century—which eventually evolved into the residential neighborhood seen today. The beach itself retains a sense of enclosure, framed by high ground, with a surf lifesaving club, viewing platforms, and picnic areas concentrated in a compact space. A visit here is best enjoyed by observing the topography, watching the surf, or taking a short stroll; there is no need to combine the steep climb with a long-distance coastal trek if you are looking for a relaxed outing.
## How to explore
1. Begin near the public access point off Narrabeen Park Parade. Before heading down, take in the view of the bay and identify both the beach entrance and your return route. Choose a path that will be manageable to climb back up later, and ensure you stay within designated pedestrian areas—avoid standing on the roadway, especially near curves.
2. Follow the official access path down to the beach. Near the surf lifesaving club, observe the waves and the contours of the shoreline. If you choose to walk along the sand, stick to the drier, flatter sections; if the tide approaches the cliff face, turn back—do not attempt to navigate around the rocks toward Mona Vale.
3. Spend some time in the picnic or public rest area behind the beach before beginning your ascent. Once back at the top, look back at the path you took; it will be easier to appreciate the scale of the headlands and the bay. Before leaving, confirm which side of the road your return transport stop is on, and allow a few minutes to rest and hydrate after the climb.
## Timing
A 45-minute visit is sufficient to explore the clifftop and the beach entrance area; a 90-minute visit allows time for a walk on the sand, a break, and a leisurely climb back up. If your energy is limited, you can simply focus on the designated viewing areas at the top. The slopes can be quite exposed to the sun around midday; early mornings or cooler days offer a more comfortable experience. After dark this is a shore-side walk and a chance to sit and listen to the water. Stay on visible public paths close to the approach; do not swim, enter rock platforms or continue onto unlit cliffs or bush tracks. Lifeguard patrols, bathing facilities, toilets and car parks have separate hours; public shore access does not imply a patrolled swim or an open car park.
## Getting there and costs
Set your map destination to Warriewood Beach. If arriving by public transport, you will likely need to transfer from a main route or walk from Narrabeen Park Parade—be prepared for some uphill walking after you disembark. If driving, you can park in the designated beach parking areas (fees may apply; please check local signage). Ensure you do not block emergency access points or private residential driveways. No booking is required for a casual stroll along the shore; however, you will need to make your own arrangements for parking, refreshments, and transport.
## Nearby food
There are cafés and light meal options near Narrabeen Park Parade at the top of the hill. It is best to stop here on your way back up, saving you the trouble of carrying hot drinks while navigating the steep incline. If you plan to spend some time relaxing by the water, consider bringing your own water and light snacks to enjoy in the designated picnic areas, rather than relying on the facilities inside the surf club.
en.tips: Wear footwear suitable for sloping terrain, and opt for a backpack rather than a handheld bag—this will help you conserve energy for the uphill return journey. Please note that the rock surfaces washed by the waves are not intended as shortcuts. Avoid entering areas restricted for activities like hang-gliding, emergency operations, or construction. If you need a restroom, look for signs pointing toward public facilities near the surf club.

items.title: 柯林斯浅湾海滩
items.summary: 走进林带包围的小海湾，岸上看港口入口、岩面与溪流。
items.guide:
## 简介
Collins Flat Beach位于Little Manly与North Head之间，沙滩被林地和岬角围成较隐蔽的湾口。与有连续商业街的大海滩不同，这里的到访需要先走一段公共路径，下到海湾后再沿原路返回。树林、岩面与海港入口的方向感，是它最值得慢看的部分。

海滩后方有溪流与瀑布地貌，水量随降雨变化；把它看作自然地形的一部分，比专程追求固定瀑布画面更合适。这里也处于悉尼港国家公园的保护背景下，与周边检疫、防务及海港历史地景相邻。普通到访只走开放海滩和标识路径，不需要进入Q Station酒店、旧检疫设施或未开放岬角，就能在有限范围内完成一次安静的看景与野餐。
## 这样逛
1. 从Collins Beach Road方向按国家公园公共路径指示进入，先辨认回程坡路与台阶。走到沙滩边再找稳定的休息位置，雨后有积水或冲刷处就绕开放路线，不穿私人通道。
2. 沿干沙看湾口与港面，想看后方溪流就站在公开可达的稳固位置观察，不爬瀑布、湿岩或钻入水道。若水量很小也不必继续往林中找，海湾、植被与岩面仍构成完整景色。
3. 吃自带点心、在岸边停留片刻，再按原公共路径返回。手里尽量不拿热饮和散装餐盘，上坡时双手空出来更方便；不临时沿无标识岩岸绕去另一海湾。
## 时间怎么用
45至60分钟适合路径与海滩短停；90分钟可加野餐和慢看溪流。沙地、台阶与回程上坡另留余量，最后一段不用走到海滩两端才算完成。
## 怎么去与花费
导航Collins Flat Beach, Collins Beach Road, Manly。从Manly交通枢纽到公共入口仍有步行，可结合本地巴士再走最后一段；停车遵守街边和公园规定，不占狭窄道路。普通岸上到访无需预约，车辆、公园相关收费与交通、食物另计。
## 附近餐饮
水和冷食提前在Manly备好，海滩不作为餐饮补给点。想吃热食就把正餐留到返回主要街区后，避免携带过多包装、杯子与餐盘走台阶；吃完带走全部垃圾。
items.tips: 穿防滑鞋，台阶上尽量双手空出，不提热汤或散装餐盘。走原标识路径，遇大浪、湿滑岩面或恶劣天气及时缩短行程；下到沙滩前就确认返回的路。

en.title: Collins Flat Beach
en.summary: Step into a small cove framed by woodland, where you can take in views of the harbor entrance, rock faces, and streams from the shore.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Nestled between Little Manly and North Head, Collins Flat Beach is a secluded cove framed by woodlands and headlands. Unlike larger, commercialized beaches, this spot requires a walk along a public path to reach the cove, with the return journey following the same route. The interplay of the woodlands, rock formations, and the orientation toward the harbor entrance makes it a place best explored at a leisurely pace.

Behind the beach, you will find a creek and waterfall—though the water flow varies depending on recent rainfall. It is best to view these as natural features of the landscape rather than expecting a permanent, dramatic waterfall. The area is also part of the protected Sydney Harbour National Park, situated amidst a landscape rich in history, including former quarantine stations, defense sites, and maritime heritage. For a casual visit, stick to the accessible beaches and marked trails. You can enjoy a peaceful outing—taking in the scenery and having a picnic—without needing to enter the Q Station hotel grounds, the historic quarantine facilities, or the restricted headland areas.
## How to explore
1. Follow the public park trail signs from Collins Beach Road, and take note of the slope and stairs you will need to use for your return journey. Once you reach the beach, find a stable spot to rest. If there is standing water or erosion following rain, navigate around these areas; do not cross into private property.
2. Enjoy views of the bay entrance and the harbor from the dry sand. If you wish to see the creek further inland, observe it only from a stable, publicly accessible vantage point—do not climb on waterfalls or wet rocks, and do not venture into the watercourse itself. If the water flow is minimal, there is no need to push deeper into the woods; the bay, the surrounding vegetation, and the rock formations already offer a complete, scenic experience.
3. Enjoy your own snacks and spend some time by the shore, then return via the same public trail. It is best to keep your hands free—avoid carrying hot drinks or loose plates—as this makes the uphill climb easier. Do not attempt to take shortcuts along unmarked rocky shorelines to reach other bays.
## Timing
Allow 45 to 60 minutes for a walk along the trail and a brief stop on the beach; allocate 90 minutes if you plan to have a picnic or take your time observing the creek. Factor in extra time for navigating sandy terrain, stairs, and the uphill return. You do not need to reach the far ends of the beach to consider your visit complete.
## Getting there and costs
Navigate to Collins Flat Beach, Collins Beach Road, Manly. From the Manly transport hub, there is a walk to the public entrance; you may wish to take a local bus for the final leg of the journey. Please observe all street-side and park parking regulations, and ensure you do not obstruct narrow roads. No reservation is required for a standard visit; please note that vehicle/park entry fees, transport costs, and food expenses are separate.
## Nearby food
Purchase water and cold food in Manly beforehand, as the beach offers no facilities for replenishing supplies. If you prefer a hot meal, wait until you return to the main town center; this also helps avoid carrying excessive packaging, cups, or open food containers while navigating the stairs. Please take all your trash with you when you leave.
en.tips: Wear non-slip footwear. Keep your hands free while on the stairs—avoid carrying items like hot soup or open trays of food. Stick to the marked trails, and if you encounter high waves, slippery rocks, or adverse weather, consider cutting your visit short. Confirm your return route before descending to the beach.

items.title: Annandale 老街与咖啡
items.summary: 沿宽阔的Johnston Street看老店屋，再到旧家具厂改成的咖啡馆坐一会。
items.guide:
## 简介
Annandale的街道记录了庄园转为郊区住宅的过程。George Johnston与Esther Abrahams一家在这里经营土地，庄园名称后来成为地名；1877年，John Young购入庄园土地后推动分割与住宅开发。Johnston Street较开阔的街宽、沿线成组的老店屋与附近住宅，留下了这一时期对理想郊区的想象。步行时可以比较上层山墙、窗楣、阳台与底层招牌的关系：很多建筑继续承担商铺和日常服务功能，因此历史并没有从生活中被单独抽走。

Booth Street把这种老街气氛与当代咖啡文化连在一起。43号Black Toast使用一座19世纪家具厂改造的空间，外面仍是普通商业街，里面则能看到裸露梁架、不同层次的室内与把光引进来的中庭。改造让过去生产家具的场所变成吃饭和见面的地方，也提供了比单看建筑立面更具体的空间体验。Johnston Street北段另有著名的哥特复兴住宅群，说明当年开发者对建筑造型的重视；第一次到访可把精力留在Booth街口一带，用旧店屋与工厂咖啡馆完成一段连贯的小走。
## 这样逛
1. 先在Booth Street与Johnston Street附近走一圈，抬头看店屋上层的年代铭牌、山墙和窗户，再看底层遮棚如何连接人行道。选安全街角停下来拍照，约15–20分钟。
2. 到43 Booth Street的Black Toast用餐，入座后看看梁架、中庭与分层空间如何保留旧厂房尺度。点咖啡加一份正餐，想拍室内避开其他客人，留40分钟左右慢慢体验。
3. 饭后沿Johnston Street再走一两个街段，看主街转入住宅街后的变化，然后回到公交方向。还有体力才向北延长建筑散步，私人住宅只从公共人行道欣赏外观。
## 时间怎么用
30分钟可走一小段主街并休息；想逛店或用餐可留120分钟左右，另加候位时间。公共街道昼夜可走，店铺、拱廊、市场和餐厅各按自己的营业时间，深夜可以只散步，不必消费。晚上沿人行道和正式过街点往返，先认好返程车站；遇已关门的商场或私人通道就沿公共道路绕行。
## 怎么去与花费
公交到Booth Street／Johnston Street附近后步行，餐饮导航用Black Toast，43 Booth Street。轻轨到Rozelle Bay后仍有一段向内陆及上坡步行，按地图看当天路线；开车注意住宅限时车位。餐费、饮品与停车另计。
## 附近餐饮
Black Toast有早午餐与午餐选择，先选一份咸食，再决定要不要加蛋糕。咖啡以Campos豆为主，店里也供应来自合作烘焙品牌的点心；不想吃大餐可用一杯咖啡配一份小点，想吃完整午饭则先问当天厨房菜单。
items.tips: 这里有坡度，穿适合街走的鞋；店内分层座位的通行条件先问店员。看建筑不需要进入工作区、私人住宅或门前花园，街口拍照时给过路行人留出通道。

en.title: Annandale — Booth & Johnston Streets
en.summary: Stroll along the wide Johnston Street to admire the historic shophouses, then stop for a while at a café housed in a former furniture factory.
en.guide:
## Introduction
The streets of Annandale document the transformation of a grand estate into a suburban residential area. The land was once managed by the family of George Johnston and Esther Abrahams—the estate’s name eventually becoming the name of the suburb itself. In 1877, John Young acquired the estate and spearheaded its subdivision and residential development. With its relatively wide thoroughfare, clusters of historic shopfronts, and surrounding homes, Johnston Street preserves a vision of an "ideal suburb" from that era. As you walk, observe the relationship between the upper-level gables, window lintels, and balconies, and the storefronts below; many of these buildings still house shops and provide everyday services, ensuring that history remains an integral part of contemporary life.

Booth Street bridges this historic atmosphere with today’s vibrant café culture. At number 43, "Black Toast" occupies a converted 19th-century furniture factory. While the exterior retains the character of a typical commercial street, the interior reveals exposed structural beams, multi-level spaces, and an atrium designed to draw in natural light. Adaptive reuse has transformed former furniture-manufacturing sites into spaces for dining and socializing, offering a more immersive spatial experience than simply observing the building facades from the outside. Further north along Johnston Street, you will find a notable collection of Gothic Revival-style residences—a testament to the importance early developers placed on architectural form. For a first-time visit, focus your exploration around the intersection of Booth Street, where a sequence of converted shophouses and factory-turned-cafés makes for a cohesive, short walking route.
## How to explore
1. Begin by wandering around the intersection of Booth Street and Johnston Street. Look up to examine the date plaques, gables, and windows on the upper levels of the shophouses, and observe how the ground-floor awnings connect to the sidewalk. Find a safe street corner to pause and take photos—allow about 15–20 minutes for this.
2. Head to Black Toast (43 Booth Street) for a meal. Once seated, take note of how the exposed beams, atrium, and split-level layout preserve the original scale of the former factory. Order a coffee and a main course; if you wish to photograph the interior without other patrons in the frame, set aside about 40 minutes to enjoy the space at a leisurely pace.
3. After your meal, continue along Johnston Street for a block or two to observe the transition from the main thoroughfare into a residential area, then head back toward your public transport stop. If you still have energy, you can extend your architectural walk further north—just remember to view the private residences only from the public sidewalk.
## Timing
Allow 30 minutes for a short main-street walk and a rest. Browsing and an optional meal can extend the outing to around 120 minutes, plus any queue. Public footpaths remain available independently of business hours: shops, arcades, markets and restaurants operate their own schedules, and a late walk does not require a purchase. At night use the main pavement and marked crossings, identify your return stop first, and go around closed shopping centres on public streets rather than through private passages.
## Getting there and costs
Arrive via public transport near the intersection of Booth Street and Johnston Street; for dining, navigate to Black Toast at 43 Booth Street. If arriving by light rail at Rozelle Bay, be prepared for a walk inland and uphill—check your map to plan your route. If driving, please be mindful of time-restricted parking in residential areas. Costs for meals, drinks, and parking are separate.
## Nearby food
Black Toast offers brunch and lunch options. Start by choosing a savory dish, then decide whether to add a slice of cake. The café primarily uses Campos coffee beans and also stocks treats from partner bakeries. If you’re not looking for a full meal, you can simply pair a coffee with a small snack; for a substantial lunch, check the kitchen’s daily menu.
en.tips: The area is sloped, so wear comfortable walking shoes. If you have mobility concerns regarding the multi-level seating inside, please ask the staff for assistance. When viewing the architecture, please respect private workspaces, residences, and front gardens; if taking photos from the street corner, ensure you leave enough space for pedestrians to pass.

items.summary: 在环形码头附近的海关大楼阅读和浏览公共展览。
items.guide:
## 简介
Customs House位于Circular Quay的Alfred Street，最初由Mortimer Lewis设计，于1845年建造，长期承担港口海关职能。建筑后来经过多次扩展，在海关迁出后转向公共文化与商业用途，并成为City of Sydney Library的馆舍之一；它的厚重立面仍能让人想起这里与港口管理的联系。

今天公众可以在同一栋建筑内看城市展示、读书和观察Circular Quay。进入历史外壳后，楼内阅读空间与街面交通形成鲜明节奏变化；与其只在正门拍一张照片，不如先理解这座楼过去为何靠近码头，再看看它如何继续服务今天的城市使用者。
## 这样逛
1. 从31 Alfred Street的海关大楼进入，先看入口层玻璃地面下的悉尼市中心模型与楼层导览，再按电梯或楼梯指示到图书馆，餐饮空间不属于公共阅览区。
2. 在书架选一本城市、旅行或文化主题读物，或看看本馆多语言馆藏；若有免费展览开放，读一组作品背景，根据现场展览导览选择内容。
3. 找公共阅览座位读书或看报，留意朝向Circular Quay的窗景；不占用通道和别人正在使用的桌位拍照，最后回到Alfred Street继续或结束行程。
## 时间怎么用
30分钟看楼内公共空间并短读；90分钟可加当期展览和连续阅读。建筑、图书馆与楼内餐饮时段不同，按实际开放楼层安排。
## 怎么去与花费
地址31 Alfred Street，紧邻Circular Quay火车、轻轨、公交与渡轮。前入口有台阶及坡道，按楼内指示选择通路；
## 附近餐饮
Alfred Street和Circular Quay周边餐饮集中，馆内其他商业楼层有各自安排。若只想喝一杯，完成阅读后在返程方向找店最省来回；不要把餐饮专用座位当公共阅览桌。
items.tips: 打印、借阅和电脑使用按会员或临时使用规则，按实际使用付费。馆内可能举办活动，部分桌位不可用；保持音量、不给读者拍特写，公共展览也遵守摄影说明。
