en.title: Customs House Library
en.summary: Read and browse public exhibitions at the Customs House, located near Circular Quay.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Located on Alfred Street at Circular Quay, the Customs House was originally designed by Mortimer Lewis and built in 1845, serving as the port’s customs facility for many years. Following several expansions and the eventual relocation of the customs office, the building was repurposed for public, cultural, and commercial use—now housing a branch of the City of Sydney Library. Its imposing façade remains a reminder of its historical role in port administration.

Today, the public can visit the building to view exhibitions about the city, read, or simply observe Circular Quay. Stepping inside this historic shell, you’ll notice a distinct shift in rhythm between the quiet reading spaces and the bustling street traffic outside. Rather than just snapping a photo of the main entrance, take a moment to consider why the building was originally positioned near the docks, and how it continues to serve the city’s residents and visitors today.
## How to explore
1. Enter the Customs House at 31 Alfred Street. On the ground floor, take a look at the model of Sydney’s city center beneath the glass floor and consult the building directory. Use the elevator or stairs to reach the library; please note that the dining areas are separate from the public reading zones.
2. Browse the shelves for books on urban themes, travel, or culture, or explore the library’s multilingual collection. If there is a free exhibition on display, take some time to read about the works and follow the provided exhibition guide to enhance your experience. 3. Find a seat in the public reading area to enjoy a book or newspaper, and take in the view through the windows facing Circular Quay. Please avoid blocking walkways or occupying tables already in use by others when taking photographs. Afterward, return to Alfred Street to continue or conclude your visit.
## Timing
A 30-minute visit allows time to explore the building’s public spaces and enjoy some light reading; a 90-minute visit provides enough time to also view current exhibitions and engage in more extended reading. Please note that the building, the library, and the on-site dining venues have different operating hours; plan your visit based on the floors currently open to the public.
## Getting there and costs
Located at 31 Alfred Street, the building is immediately adjacent to the Circular Quay train, light rail, bus, and ferry terminals. The front entrance features both stairs and a ramp; please follow the signage inside the building to choose your preferred route.
## Nearby food
There is a high concentration of dining options around Alfred Street and Circular Quay, while other commercial levels within the building have their own specific arrangements. If you would simply like a drink, it is most convenient to stop at a café on your way back from the library. Please do not use seating designated for dining as a public reading space.
en.tips: Services such as printing, borrowing items, and using computers are subject to membership or casual-use policies, with fees applicable based on actual usage. The building may occasionally host events, which could render some tables unavailable. Please keep noise to a minimum, refrain from taking close-up photos of other readers, and adhere to any photography guidelines posted for public exhibitions.

items.title: 温迪秘密花园
items.summary: 在薰衣草湾的多层花园中散步，留意坡道与台阶。
items.guide:
## 简介
Wendy’s Secret Garden藏在Lavender Bay的坡地上，由Wendy Whiteley逐渐营造。她与画家Brett Whiteley于1970年在附近安家；1992年Brett去世后，Wendy开始清理屋下废弃铁路土地上的杂物与杂生植物，后来将这片谷地变成向公众开放的花园。

花园更像一幅可以走进去的作品：弯曲小径把竹丛、棕榈、榕树、砂岩壁、雕塑与零散座椅连接起来，植物之间留出的空隙又让Lavender Bay突然出现在视野里。布置并非整齐的轴线式园林，而是顺着地形展开，转过一个弯就会看到不同的小空间。
## 这样逛
1. 从 Lavender Street 一侧寻找花园标识，先在上部路径看清坡度与下行台阶，选一条身体能够轻松返回的路线。
2. 顺着小径下行，留意植物之间的雕塑、手作细节和小座椅；这里的乐趣是慢慢发现，不用追逐固定拍照点。
3. 找一张空椅坐下，从枝叶间看 Lavender Bay；最后沿明确的公共小径返回。不要进入相邻住宅或把 Wendy 的私人房屋当参观空间。
## 时间怎么用
30分钟走上部和一小段下坡；60分钟可在花园内慢逛并休息。不含通勤。官方表示花园始终开放，白天更容易看清台阶和植物细节。 夜间也可沿可通行的公共步道或建筑外侧散步，挑能看清台阶与路面的路线往返；室内、泳池、活动区域和园内设施按各自开放安排。
## 怎么去与花费
Lavender Street, Lavender Bay。官方给出的步行参考为 North Sydney 或 Milsons Point 车站约5–10分钟、Milsons Point 或 McMahons Point 码头约10–15分钟，实际路线以地图为准。个人随意散步免费；组织活动需另向市政申请。
## 参观要点
植物和艺术品可以交替观看：竹与大树形成不同的遮阴，小雕塑和零散座位藏在植被之间。这里的布置以色彩、形状和趣味组织空间，并不是必须按固定方向逐点完成的展园。
## 附近餐饮
可回到North Sydney或Milsons Point车站周边用餐，按返程方向选一边即可。花园里适合带水短坐，避免在窄小径旁摆开餐食；如果自带点心，吃完将包装全部带走。
items.tips: 穿抓地鞋，雨后坡道和石阶可能打滑。花园有陡坡，行动不便者主要考虑上部有限区域，不能视为全园无障碍。带水并带走垃圾；保持小音量，让其他人也能安静休息。

en.title: Wendy’s Secret Garden
en.summary: As you stroll through this multi-tiered garden in Lavender Bay, please be mindful of the slopes and steps.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Wendy’s Secret Garden is tucked away on a hillside in Lavender Bay, a space lovingly cultivated over time by Wendy Whiteley. She and her husband, the painter Brett Whiteley, settled in the area in 1970. Following Brett’s passing in 1992, Wendy began clearing away debris and overgrowth from a disused railway site below their home, eventually transforming the valley into a garden open to the public.

The garden feels like a living artwork you can step into: winding paths connect bamboo groves, palms, fig trees, sandstone walls, sculptures, and scattered benches, while gaps between the foliage reveal sudden, striking glimpses of Lavender Bay. The garden is not laid out along a rigid, axial plan; instead, it unfolds organically with the terrain, revealing distinct, intimate spaces around every bend.
## How to explore
1. Look for the garden signage on the Lavender Street side. From the upper path, take note of the slope and the descending steps, and choose a route that you can easily navigate back up.
2. Follow the path downward, keeping an eye out for sculptures, handcrafted details, and small benches tucked among the plants. The joy here lies in spontaneous discovery—there is no need to rush toward specific "photo spots."
3. Find an empty seat, take a moment to sit, and enjoy glimpses of Lavender Bay through the foliage. When you’re ready to leave, follow the clearly marked public path. Please respect the privacy of neighboring residences and do not enter Wendy’s private home.
## Timing
A 30-minute visit allows enough time to explore the upper level and a portion of the lower slopes; a 60-minute visit offers ample time for a leisurely stroll and a rest. (This estimate excludes travel time to/from the site.) The garden is officially open at all times, though visiting during the day makes it easier to navigate the steps and appreciate the finer details of the plants. Evening visits use public paths and building exteriors where you can see the surface and steps clearly. Interiors, pools, event zones and other facilities retain their own access arrangements.
## Getting there and costs
Located on Lavender Street, Lavender Bay. It is approximately a 5–10 minute walk from North Sydney or Milsons Point train stations, and about 10–15 minutes from the Milsons Point or McMahons Point ferry wharves—please consult a map for the exact route. Casual, individual visits are free of charge; organized events require a separate permit from the local council.
## Highlights
The garden offers a blend of botanical features and artworks: bamboo and large trees create varying patterns of shade, while small sculptures and scattered benches are nestled within the greenery. The space is organized through color, form, and a sense of playfulness—it is not a formal exhibition garden that must be navigated in a fixed sequence.
## Nearby food
You can find dining options near North Sydney or Milsons Point stations, depending on which direction you are heading back. While it is perfectly fine to bring water and sit for a while, please avoid setting out a full meal along the narrow paths. If you bring snacks, kindly ensure that all packaging is taken with you when you leave.
en.tips: Wear shoes with good traction; slopes and stone steps can become slippery after rain. The garden features steep inclines, so those with limited mobility should focus on the more accessible upper areas—the garden is not fully barrier-free. Please bring water, take your trash with you, and keep noise levels low so that others may also enjoy a peaceful rest.

items.title: Crows Nest餐饮街
items.summary: 一条餐厅密集、地铁可达的北岸食街，适合临时决定吃点什么。
items.guide:
## 简介
Crows Nest的名字来自Edward Wollstonecraft在19世纪早期庄园中建造的“乌鸦巢”小屋，指的是地势较高、视野开阔的位置。后来土地分割、道路和住宅逐渐形成街区，Willoughby Road成为商业与社交活动集中的一条街。今天的低层店屋、街边树、转角建筑和连续餐厅，与不远处Pacific Highway的大尺度交通形成对比；不用走远，就能从交通干线进入适合用餐散步的村落街道。

餐饮是这里最实际的到访理由，咖啡、亚洲家常菜、意式餐厅和甜点店分布得很密。2024年开通的Crows Nest地铁站也让这个原本以公交和步行为主的商业圈更容易到达。Willoughby Road、Ernest Place与相邻公共支路适合串成短距离餐饮散步：先看树荫下的店面，再在热食与甜点之间选一个方向，坐下来享受一段不用赶路的时间。
## 这样逛
1. 从地铁方向走入商业街。按路牌接上Willoughby Road，先走一侧看店屋、骑楼和菜单，把想吃的类型缩成一两种。主街比地图上的名字看起来长，没必要一直走到街道尽头；到餐厅密集段就可以慢下来。
2. 在Ernest Place附近停一下。看街边座位与小型公共空间怎样接在店铺之间，喜欢拍街景可在树荫与路口找位置。若有现场活动就按开放通道走；活动不是日常到访的前提，平日也能完成同一段餐饮散步。
3. 用主餐或甜点收尾。想简单就找一间当前有位的亚洲餐厅吃面或饭，想下午茶可到110–112 Willoughby Road的Kürtősh选一份甜点。吃完回地铁或公交站，若已经饱了不用为了“再体验一家”继续买。
## 时间怎么用
30分钟可走一小段主街并休息；想逛店或用餐可留120分钟左右，另加候位时间。公共街道昼夜可走，店铺、拱廊、市场和餐厅各按自己的营业时间，深夜可以只散步，不必消费。晚上沿人行道和正式过街点往返，先认好返程车站；遇已关门的商场或私人通道就沿公共道路绕行。
## 怎么去与花费
Crows Nest地铁站可步行进入Willoughby Road商业圈，Pacific Highway及附近也有公交。St Leonards火车站是另一选择，但到餐厅仍有步行，别把两个站当成同一出口。用餐和交通按实际付费。
## 附近餐饮
甜点店的烟囱卷外层裹糖或其他配料，适合现做后分着吃；切块蛋糕则方便按想吃的大小搭配咖啡。若先吃亚洲家常菜，一份汤面或饭通常比先点很多小菜更容易掌握份量。甜味不必叠加，买了大份甜点，饮品可以选无糖茶或普通咖啡。
items.tips: 地铁出口、店铺和餐饮座位之间仍要步行，带一件薄外套适合晚间返程。店外排队别堵路口和通道，看到更轻松的备选可以直接坐下。

en.title: Crows Nest — Willoughby Road
en.summary: A dining strip on the North Shore—accessible by metro and packed with restaurants—is an ideal spot when you’re deciding on a meal at the last minute.
en.guide:
## Introduction
The name "Crows Nest" originates from a cottage—dubbed the "Crow's Nest"—built by Edward Wollstonecraft on his estate in the early 19th century, a nod to its elevated position and expansive views. Over time, the land was subdivided, roads and residences emerged, and Willoughby Road evolved into a hub for commerce and social life. Today, the area’s low-rise shophouses, street-lining trees, corner buildings, and continuous row of restaurants offer a striking contrast to the heavy, large-scale traffic of the nearby Pacific Highway. Just a short distance from the main arterial road, you find yourself in a village-like setting perfect for dining and strolling.

Dining is the primary draw here, with a dense concentration of cafés, Asian eateries, Italian restaurants, and dessert shops. The opening of the Crows Nest Metro station in 2024 has made this commercial precinct—historically reliant on buses and walking—even more accessible. Willoughby Road, Ernest Place, and the surrounding side streets are ideal for a short, leisurely "dine-and-stroll" outing: browse the storefronts shaded by trees, decide between a savory meal or a sweet treat, and take a moment to sit back—no need to rush.
## How to explore
1. Enter the commercial strip from the direction of the Metro station. Follow the signage to Willoughby Road and walk along one side to take in the shophouses, covered walkways, and menus, narrowing down your choices to one or two types of cuisine. The main street is longer than it might appear on a map; there is no need to walk to the very end—simply slow down once you reach the stretch where restaurants are most concentrated.
2. Pause near Ernest Place. Observe how the outdoor seating and small public spaces integrate with the shops; if you enjoy street photography, look for spots among the trees or near the intersections. If an event is taking place, follow the designated open pathways. Events are not a prerequisite for a visit—you can enjoy the same dining and strolling experience on any ordinary day. 3. Wrap up with a main meal or dessert. For something simple, look for an Asian restaurant with available seating and enjoy a noodle or rice dish; alternatively, head to Kürtősh at 110–112 Willoughby Road for a dessert. Once finished, make your way back to the metro or bus stop—if you’re already full, there’s no need to force another stop just for the sake of "trying one more place."
## Timing
Allow 30 minutes for a short main-street walk and a rest. Browsing and an optional meal can extend the outing to around 120 minutes, plus any queue. Public footpaths remain available independently of business hours: shops, arcades, markets and restaurants operate their own schedules, and a late walk does not require a purchase. At night use the main pavement and marked crossings, identify your return stop first, and go around closed shopping centres on public streets rather than through private passages.
## Getting there and costs
You can reach the Willoughby Road commercial district on foot from the Crows Nest metro station; there are also bus services along the Pacific Highway and nearby areas. St Leonards train station is another option, though it will require a bit more walking to reach the restaurants—don’t mistake the two stations for the same access point. You are responsible for your own dining and transportation costs.
## Nearby food
At dessert shops, chimney cakes—coated in sugar or other toppings—are perfect for sharing when served fresh. Alternatively, sliced ​​cakes offer the flexibility to choose a portion size that pairs well with a coffee. If you’re starting with an Asian-style meal, a single bowl of noodle soup or a rice dish is generally easier to portion-control than ordering a variety of small side dishes. There’s no need to double up on sweetness; if you’ve opted for a large dessert, consider pairing it with an unsweetened tea or a standard coffee.
en.tips: Expect some walking between the metro exit, the shops, and the dining areas; bringing a light jacket is a good idea for your return trip in the evening. When queuing outside a venue, be careful not to block intersections or walkways—and if you spot a less crowded alternative, feel free to head there instead.

items.title: 哈伯菲尔德意式街区
items.summary: 看花园郊区的老街格局，再用意式餐食和糕点收尾。
items.guide:
## 简介
Haberfield与悉尼早期的花园郊区规划紧密相连。Richard Stanton在1901年开始开发这里，以相对宽的地块、独立住宅、前院花园和有组织的街道，提供了与内城密集排屋不同的居住理想。周围联邦时期住宅的红砖、瓦顶、山墙和前廊很有辨识度，Ramsay Street与Dalhousie Street的低层店屋则承担日常商业，让住宅区有一个步行可到的中心。

这片土地更早属于Dobroyde Estate和Ramsay家族，Ramsay与Dalhousie等街名仍保留了家族背景。后来意大利移民带来面包、熟食、糕点与餐厅，老商业街在历史外壳内延续新的饮食生活。Papa的烤ricotta蛋糕是这里广为人知的甜点入口，但到访也值得看看店屋上层与相邻住宅的变化。把建筑散步、意式咸食和一小份糕点结合，能比只买蛋糕多了解一层地方性格。
## 这样逛
1. 先看Ramsay Street店屋。以Ramsay与Dalhousie街口附近为中心，沿商业段走一侧，抬头看阳台、山墙和老招牌位置。等过街灯后再到对面比较立面，喜欢哪一间就停一下，不需要把整条Ramsay Street走完。
2. 走一小段住宅支路。沿Dalhousie Street邻近的公共人行道看看前院与独立住宅，比较它们和刚才商店的关系。绕到下一路口就回主街，住宅花园在院门外欣赏；把“花园郊区”当作能直接观察的街道格局，而非进入私人宅院的理由。
3. 坐下一顿再带走甜点。可到145 Ramsay Street的Papa看现场餐饮与糕点，想轻松吃就先找有位的咖啡或简餐。吃完选一小份蛋糕或糕点带走，再沿原街返回；若想认真吃餐厅正餐，另外留出坐下用餐的时间。
## 时间怎么用
30分钟可走一小段主街并休息；想逛店或用餐可留120分钟左右，另加候位时间。公共街道昼夜可走，店铺、拱廊、市场和餐厅各按自己的营业时间，深夜可以只散步，不必消费。晚上沿人行道和正式过街点往返，先认好返程车站；遇已关门的商场或私人通道就沿公共道路绕行。
## 怎么去与花费
公交可接近Ramsay Street商业段，也可从Ashfield方向转公交进入。轻轨到Marion等站后仍有步行，出发时按实际站点确认方向。街边停车遵守限时与居民标识，餐点、蛋糕与交通另付；只买一片蛋糕也可以完成一次短出门。
## 附近餐饮
Ricotta蛋糕口感偏绵密，适合一片配咖啡，不必买整只；cannoli的脆壳与奶酪内馅是另一种口感。想吃咸的，可先点意式三明治、披萨或当天主食，再决定甜食份量。两人分享时先选一咸一甜，避免提着太多外带食物继续走住宅段。
items.tips: 带一个能稳放糕点的袋子，奶油和奶酪类点心尽快食用。坐户外时注意过往行人，给推车留路；拍住宅立面以远景为主，避开窗内的人与住家细节。

en.title: Haberfield — Ramsay and Dalhousie Streets
en.summary: Take in the layout of the old streets in this garden suburb, and wrap up your visit with some Italian-style cuisine or pastries.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Haberfield is closely linked to the early "garden suburb" planning movement in Sydney. Developed by Richard Stanton starting in 1901, the area offered an alternative to the dense, terraced housing of the inner city, featuring wider plots, detached homes, front gardens, and a structured street layout. The neighborhood is defined by its Federation-style architecture—characterized by red brick, tiled roofs, gables, and front verandas—while the low-rise shopfronts along Ramsay and Dalhousie Streets serve as a local commercial hub, ensuring that the residential area has a center within easy walking distance.

The land was once part of the Dobroyde Estate, owned by the Ramsay family—a legacy still reflected in street names like Ramsay and Dalhousie. Later, Italian immigrants introduced bakeries, delis, patisseries, and restaurants, breathing new culinary life into the historic commercial strip. While the baked ricotta cake at "Papa’s" is a famous local treat, it’s also worth taking a closer look at the upper levels of the shopfronts and the surrounding homes. By combining an architectural stroll with some Italian savory bites and a small pastry, you’ll gain a much deeper appreciation for the character of the neighborhood than you would by simply buying a cake.
## How to explore
1. Start by taking a look at the shopfronts along Ramsay Street. Start near the intersection of Ramsay and Dalhousie Streets. Walk along one side of the commercial strip, taking time to look up at the balconies, gables, and the spots where old signage once hung. Cross the street to compare the facades on the other side; feel free to pause whenever a particular building catches your eye—there’s no need to walk the entire length of Ramsay Street.
2. Take a short detour into the residential side streets. Walk along the public footpaths near Dalhousie Street to observe the front gardens and detached homes, and consider how they relate to the shops you just passed. Loop back to the main street at the next intersection. Please admire the residential gardens from outside the property gates—think of this "garden suburb" style as a streetscape to be observed from the public realm, rather than an invitation to enter private property.
3. Sit down for a meal, then pick up a dessert to go. You might visit "Papa" (at 145 Ramsay Street) to see their dine-in menu and selection of pastries; for a more casual experience, look for a café or eatery with available seating. Afterward, pick out a slice of cake or a pastry to take with you as you head back the way you came. If you’re planning a full, formal meal, be sure to set aside extra time for a proper sit-down dining experience.
## Timing
Allow 30 minutes for a short main-street walk and a rest. Browsing and an optional meal can extend the outing to around 120 minutes, plus any queue. Public footpaths remain available independently of business hours: shops, arcades, markets and restaurants operate their own schedules, and a late walk does not require a purchase. At night use the main pavement and marked crossings, identify your return stop first, and go around closed shopping centres on public streets rather than through private passages.
## Getting there and costs
You can reach the commercial section of Ramsay Street by bus, including routes connecting from the direction of Ashfield. If arriving via light rail (e.g., at the Marion stop), be prepared for a short walk; check your specific stop to confirm the correct direction. If parking on the street, be mindful of time limits and signage reserved for local residents. Expenses for meals, pastries, and transport are separate. Even just buying a single slice of cake is a perfectly valid reason for a short outing.
## Nearby food
The ricotta cake has a dense, rich texture—perfect for enjoying a single slice with coffee, so there’s no need to buy a whole cake. Alternatively, try a cannoli, which offers a delightful contrast between a crispy shell and a creamy ricotta filling. If you’re in the mood for something savory, start with an Italian-style sandwich, a pizza, or one of the daily specials, then decide how much room you have left for something sweet. When sharing food, opt for one savory and one sweet item to avoid carrying too many takeaway bags while walking through the residential sections.
en.tips: Bring a bag that allows pastries to sit upright and stable; consume any items containing cream or cheese promptly. When seated outdoors, be mindful of passersby and ensure there is enough space for strollers to pass. If photographing residential facades, focus on wide shots and avoid capturing people inside or specific details of private homes.

items.title: 西悉尼Sydney Zoo
items.summary: 在平缓、开阔的西悉尼园区看多种动物，预留完整半日更从容。
items.guide:
## 简介
位于Bungarribee的Sydney Zoo于2019年开放，是西悉尼一处现代动物园，与Mosman的Taronga以及达令港WILD LIFE是三个不同目的地。园区利用较平缓的场地组织动物栖地和步行路线，把澳洲本土动物、其他地区动物以及水族、爬行动物相关展区组合在一次较完整的半日游里。它的体验重点是较宽敞的路线和连续观察，不需要为了海港风景反复上坡。

对游客来说，最容易出错的是只看“悉尼动物园”中文名字就买错馆的票或导航到另一端城市。本条明确位于700 Great Western Highway，普通参观与专门的动物接触、会员项目及活动票分开。建议把普通游览安排在9–16点内，上午抵达时可以从容看完主要区域。这样的安排也能让首次到访者在下午留出返程余量，而不是临近闭园才抵达远离CBD的园区。
## 这样逛
1. 到入口先确认园区图和当天护理员讲解，再选一个方向按相邻展区前进。安排澳洲动物和其他大型栖地时留出中间休息，不为赶某一场讲解多次穿越全园。
2. 在每个主要展区停留几分钟，先看动物在哪里休息和活动，再读保育与栖地说明；室内水族及爬行动物区域可以作为正午避晒的一段。
3. 午餐后补齐尚未经过的开放区域，最后按出口方向返回。想参加动物接触项目先询问额外票务和剩余容量，普通门票不需要将所有互动买齐。
## 时间怎么用
最低3小时，4小时更适合慢看和午餐。建议在9–16点内完成普通游览，上午入园更从容。
## 怎么去与花费
地址700 Great Western Highway, Bungarribee。自驾可使用园方停车场；公共交通需先到西悉尼枢纽再接本地服务，不能按CBD两个街口的距离安排。门口可购票但受容量限制，票价随日期/渠道变化，预算上限未固定。
## 附近餐饮
园内餐饮和休息设施可用于午餐，带水及适合携带的食物更方便；餐饮、动物接触与普通票分别计算。
items.tips: 不要误导航至Taronga或WILD LIFE。园区开阔注意防晒，儿童不能越过围栏；动物展示以当天状态为准。

en.title: Sydney Zoo — Bungarribee
en.summary: Set in the open, gently sloping landscape of Western Sydney, this park is home to a wide variety of animals—plan for a full half-day to enjoy your visit at a relaxed pace.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Located in Bungarribee, Sydney Zoo—which opened in 2019—is a modern zoological facility in Western Sydney. It is a distinct destination, separate from Taronga Zoo in Mosman or WILD LIFE Sydney Zoo in Darling Harbour. The park utilizes a relatively flat landscape to organize animal habitats and walking paths, integrating native Australian wildlife, animals from other regions, and exhibits for aquatic life and reptiles into a cohesive half-day excursion. The experience is defined by spacious pathways and a continuous viewing flow, sparing visitors from the frequent uphill climbs often associated with harbor-side locations.

A common pitfall for visitors is relying solely on the Chinese name "Sydney Zoo," which can lead to purchasing tickets for the wrong venue or navigating to the opposite side of the city. Please note that this facility is located at 700 Great Western Highway. General admission tickets are separate from those for specialized animal encounters, membership programs, or specific events. It is recommended to plan your visit between 9:00 AM and 4:00 PM; arriving in the morning allows ample time to explore the main areas at a relaxed pace. This also ensures that first-time visitors have enough time for their return journey, rather than arriving at this location—situated far from the CBD—just as the park is closing.
## How to explore
1. Upon arrival, check the park map and the schedule for keeper talks, then choose a direction and proceed through the exhibits in sequence. Build in breaks between visiting Australian wildlife and other large habitats; avoid crisscrossing the entire park repeatedly just to catch specific keeper talks. 2. Spend a few minutes in each major exhibit area—observe where the animals are resting or moving about before reading the information on conservation and their natural habitats. The indoor aquarium and reptile enclosures are great spots to escape the midday sun.
3. After lunch, visit any outdoor areas you missed, then head toward the exit. If you’re interested in animal encounter experiences, check for ticket availability and remaining capacity; you do not need to purchase every available interactive activity.
## Timing
Allow at least 3 hours for your visit; 4 hours is better for a more leisurely pace, including lunch. A standard visit is best planned between 9:00 AM and 4:00 PM—arriving in the morning allows for a more relaxed experience.
## Getting there and costs
Located at 700 Great Western Highway, Bungarribee. If driving, you may use the park’s on-site parking. If arriving by public transport, you will need to reach a Western Sydney transit hub and transfer to a local service; do not assume it is as close as a short walk between city blocks. Tickets can be purchased at the entrance, but availability is subject to capacity limits. Prices vary by date and booking channel, so there is no fixed upper limit for your budget.
## Nearby food
You can enjoy lunch at the park’s dining or rest areas; bringing your own water and portable snacks is highly recommended. Please note that food, animal encounters, and general admission are all charged separately.
en.tips: Be careful not to accidentally navigate to Taronga Zoo or WILD LIFE Sydney Zoo. The park is very open, so remember to take sun protection measures. Children must not climb over any fences. Animal exhibits are subject to the animals' condition on the day of your visit.

items.title: 鲍尔斯岬角保护地
items.summary: 穿过砂岩林地，到开放观景点看海港，再回树下休息。
items.guide:
## 简介
Balls Head是位于海港大桥西侧的林地岬角，Berrys Bay与Balls Head Bay分布在两侧。和城市广场式的港湾公园不同，这里的主角是砂岩地形、原生树木与林下步道，港景常从树丛之间出现。离开附近街道不久就能进入相对完整的林地，适合想看水又想多一点自然环境的短途。

岬角名称来自第一舰队HMS Supply指挥官Henry Lidgbird Ball，周边也保留原住民长期使用海湾地景的历史。今天保护地通过公共步道、纪念牌与休息点，让城市居民继续接近这片林地。观察时可以留意光滑树皮的Angophora、砂岩与海湾之间的关系；岩棚、潜在文化遗存和未标明的小径不需要自行探索，走公开线路就能看见它的空间特色。
## 这样逛
1. 从Balls Head Drive公共入口看步道图，先选一条通往开放港景点的短线，并记住返回入口。跟随正式路径穿过林地，树根、落叶和砂岩台阶处放慢，不沿悬崖边找更短的路线。
2. 在有稳定路面或明确观景设施的位置看海港、桥和对岸城市，之后退回林内比较树皮、岩层与林下植被。文化或纪念标识可以读一两处，岩棚与未开放遗址只从规定位置观察，不攀爬或刻画。
3. 返回入口附近的开放休息点吃简便食物，仍有体力再按步道图加一个短分支。第一次到访选择清楚的折返线即可，不为了把每条小径都走完而在林中反复找路。
## 时间怎么用
45至60分钟适合一条短线与观景；90分钟可慢看树木、纪念牌和野餐。林地路面比城市人行道不平，雨后或体力少时选较短路线，夜间只走入口附近看得清的公共路径，不深入无照明林地。 夜间以岸边散步、听海和休息为主，沿入口附近能看清路面的公共路径往返；不下水、不走礁石、崖边或无照明的延伸山径。救生巡逻、浴场设施和停车场有各自时间，不能把可到岸边等同于有人巡逻或可夜泳。
## 怎么去与花费
地图搜索Balls Head Reserve, Balls Head Drive, Waverton。从Waverton站可沿公共街道步行接入，开车使用开放车场和合法街边位。普通散步无需专门场地预约，交通、食物和停车另计；专用活动或拍摄按市政规定安排。
## 附近餐饮
自带水和冷食适合树下休息，需咖啡或正餐可在Waverton站周边先买或返回后用餐。公园里的公共烧烤和野餐位先到先用，有空位再使用，不以点火烧烤作为这次短途的前提。
items.tips: 树根和砂岩雨后较滑，穿包脚防滑鞋。保持在正式步道，不进入洞穴、边坡或围挡区域，不触碰可能的文化遗存。夏天留意高温和火险提示，所有垃圾带到合适回收点，不喂鸟。

en.title: Balls Head Reserve
en.summary: Wander through the sandstone woodlands, reach an open vantage point to take in views of the harbor, and then head back to rest under the shade of the trees.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Balls Head is a wooded headland located west of the Harbour Bridge, flanked by Berrys Bay and Balls Head Bay. Unlike the manicured, urban-style parks found around the harbour, this area features sandstone terrain, native trees, and walking trails through the bush, with glimpses of the harbour appearing between the trees. Just a short distance from the nearby streets, you enter a relatively intact woodland—a perfect destination for a short excursion if you want to enjoy both water views and a more natural environment. The headland takes its name from Henry Lidgbird Ball, commander of HMS Supply in the First Fleet. The area also preserves a history of long-standing use of this coastal landscape by Indigenous peoples. Today, the reserve remains accessible to city residents through a network of public walking trails, commemorative plaques, and rest areas. As you explore, take note of the Angophora trees with their smooth bark and their relationship with the sandstone terrain and the harbor. You can appreciate the site’s unique spatial character—including rock shelters, potential cultural heritage sites, and unmarked paths—simply by following the designated public trails; there is no need to venture off-path.
## How to explore
1. Consult the trail map at the public entrance on Balls Head Drive. Choose a short route leading to a harbor viewpoint, and make a mental note of the path back to the entrance. Follow the official trails through the woodland; take extra care when navigating tree roots, leaf litter, or sandstone steps, and do not attempt to find "shortcuts" along the cliff edges.
2. Enjoy views of the harbor, the bridge, and the city skyline from stable, designated viewing areas. Then, head back into the woodland to observe the tree bark, rock formations, and undergrowth. Feel free to read the cultural or commemorative signage, but please view rock shelters and heritage sites only from designated vantage points—do not climb on them or carve into the rock.
3. You may enjoy a light snack at one of the rest areas near the entrance. If you still have energy, you can add a short side-loop as shown on the map. For a first visit, it is best to stick to a clear, out-and-back route rather than wandering through the woods trying to cover every single trail.
## Timing
A short walk combined with sightseeing typically takes 45 to 60 minutes. A 90-minute visit allows for a more leisurely pace to appreciate the trees, read the commemorative plaques, and enjoy a picnic. The terrain in the reserve is less even than city sidewalks; if it has recently rained or you are feeling fatigued, opt for a shorter route and after dark, stay on visible public paths near the entrance rather than entering unlit bush tracks. After dark this is a shore-side walk and a chance to sit and listen to the water. Stay on visible public paths close to the approach; do not swim, enter rock platforms or continue onto unlit cliffs or bush tracks. Lifeguard patrols, bathing facilities, toilets and car parks have separate hours; public shore access does not imply a patrolled swim or an open car park.
## Getting there and costs
Search for "Balls Head Reserve, Balls Head Drive, Waverton" on a map. If arriving by train, you can reach the reserve by walking from Waverton Station. If driving, please use the available parking lots or legal on-street parking spaces. Casual visits do not require a booking; however, please note that transport, food, and parking are your own responsibility. Organized events or professional filming/photography are subject to local council regulations.
## Nearby food
Bring your own water and cold snacks if you’d like to relax under the trees. If you’re looking for coffee or a full meal, it’s best to pick something up near Waverton Station beforehand or plan to dine after your return. Public barbecue facilities and picnic spots in the park operate on a first-come, first-served basis; please use them only if they are available. Do not make a barbecue the primary objective of this excursion.
en.tips: Tree roots and sandstone surfaces can become slippery after rain, so please wear enclosed, non-slip footwear. Stay on the designated trails; do not enter caves, venture onto steep slopes or fenced-off areas, and avoid touching any potential cultural artifacts. In summer, be mindful of high temperatures and fire danger warnings. Please carry all your trash out to an appropriate disposal or recycling point, and do not feed the birds.

items.title: 库内尔银沙滩
items.summary: 沿Botany Bay南岸走一段，看海湾、丁坝与水边生活，轻松野餐。
items.guide:
## 简介
Silver Beach沿Kurnell半岛北岸展开，面向的是Botany Bay而非Cronulla的外海冲浪面。岸线被一系列石质丁坝分成小段，远处可见港口和海湾交通，近处则是低层住宅、公共道路和沙滩。这种自然岸线与工作港湾同框的景象，是这里很鲜明的性格。

Kurnell拥有重要的原住民与殖民接触历史，附近Kamay国家公园的文化与纪念地景提供了进一步理解的背景。不过Silver Beach本身可以作为独立的公共海岸短途：看沙滩、潮间带边缘和湾内船只，再沿同一段岸线折返，不需要额外进入收费车场或把国家公园全部走完。西端Bonna Point与中段潮汐泳区也各有功能，步行时注意海滩和船用设施的区别。
## 这样逛
1. 从Prince Charles Parade沿线的公共海滩入口进入，先认清自己所在丁坝与返回出口。选一段干沙向海湾方向慢走，保持在开放岸线，住宅院落和私用通道不进入。
2. 在丁坝附近从稳固沙地观察海湾与石堤，看看不同小湾的沙面和风浪方向。不要爬到堤端或追着退潮走到湿滑石块上；靠近船道与下水坡道时让开船艇和拖车。
3. 找适合的公共岸边位置坐下吃自带简餐，再沿原段返回。想看更长岸线可多走一个丁坝间距，但不必为了从Bonna Point走到最东端而把短途变成长线。
## 时间怎么用
45至60分钟适合一段沙滩与休息；90分钟可加野餐和较长折返。晴天带遮阳用品，风大时把停留移到较有遮挡的位置；沙地比地图上同长度人行道更费力。 夜间以岸边散步、听海和休息为主，沿入口附近能看清路面的公共路径往返；不下水、不走礁石、崖边或无照明的延伸山径。救生巡逻、浴场设施和停车场有各自时间，不能把可到岸边等同于有人巡逻或可夜泳。
## 怎么去与花费
地图搜索Silver Beach, Prince Charles Parade, Kurnell。公共交通可从Cronulla方向接驳到Kurnell周边站点后步行，自驾使用合法车位并留意居民出入口。普通海滩入场免费，交通、餐饮及另去国家公园的车辆费用分别计算。
## 附近餐饮
自带三明治、水果和饮用水最省事，Kurnell街区的咖啡或外带店可作补充。先吃完再走沙滩，轻便餐盒方便回收，不把港边石堤当野餐桌。
items.tips: 本路线只在岸上，船道、下水坡道和石堤边缘留出距离。狗活动只限西端指定丁坝之间的区域，不能把整片Silver Beach当作遛狗沙滩。风浪或水质不适合时仍留在公共道路和岸上看景。

en.title: Silver Beach — Kurnell
en.summary: Take a stroll along the southern shore of Botany Bay to enjoy views of the bay, the groynes, and the local coastal atmosphere—a perfect setting for a relaxed picnic.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Silver Beach stretches along the northern shore of the Kurnell Peninsula, facing Botany Bay rather than the open-ocean surf found at Cronulla. The coastline is segmented by a series of stone groynes, with views of harbor and bay traffic in the distance, and low-rise residences, public roads, and the beach itself nearby. This juxtaposition—a natural shoreline set against an active working harbor—is a defining characteristic of the area.

Kurnell holds significant history regarding the first contact between Indigenous Australians and European colonists; the nearby Kamay Botany Bay National Park offers further context through its cultural and commemorative landscapes. However, Silver Beach can also be enjoyed as a standalone coastal outing—take in the beach, the intertidal zone, and the boats in the bay, then simply retrace your steps along the shoreline. There is no need to enter paid parking areas or attempt to explore the entire national park. Bonna Point at the western end and the tidal swimming area in the middle serve different purposes; as you walk, please be mindful of the distinction between the public beach areas and the maritime/boating facilities.
## How to explore
1. Enter via one of the public beach access points along Prince Charles Parade, and take note of which groyne section you are in so you can easily find your way back to the exit. Stroll along the dry sand toward the bay, keeping to the open shoreline—please do not enter private residential yards or restricted access paths. 2. From the stable sandy areas near the groynes (stone breakwaters), observe the bay and the stone structures; take note of the sand formations and wave patterns in the various small coves. Do not climb onto the ends of the groynes, and avoid venturing onto slippery, wave-washed rocks during low tide. Keep clear of boats and trailers when near navigation channels or boat ramps.
3. Find a suitable spot along the public shoreline to enjoy a packed snack or light meal, then retrace your steps. If you wish to explore further, you may continue to the next groyne, but there is no need to turn a short, leisurely outing into a long trek—for instance, by attempting to walk all the way from Bonna Point to the easternmost tip.
## Timing
Allow 45 to 60 minutes for a walk along the beach with time for a short rest; 90 minutes allows for a picnic and a more extended return trip. Bring sun protection for sunny days, and seek more sheltered areas if it is windy. Walking on sand requires more physical effort than walking the same distance on a paved path. After dark this is a shore-side walk and a chance to sit and listen to the water. Stay on visible public paths close to the approach; do not swim, enter rock platforms or continue onto unlit cliffs or bush tracks. Lifeguard patrols, bathing facilities, toilets and car parks have separate hours; public shore access does not imply a patrolled swim or an open car park.
## Getting there and costs
Search for "Silver Beach, Prince Charles Parade, Kurnell" on your map. If arriving by public transport, you can travel from the direction of Cronulla to a stop near Kurnell and walk the rest of the way. If driving, please use designated legal parking spaces and be mindful of residential driveways. Access to the beach itself is free; however, costs for transport, food, and entry to the nearby national park are separate.
## Nearby food
Bringing your own sandwiches, fruit, and water is the most convenient option, though you can also pick up supplies at cafes or takeaway shops in the Kurnell neighborhood. Please finish your food before heading onto the beach; use lightweight, recyclable containers, and do not use the stone breakwaters as picnic tables.
en.tips: This route is strictly for the shoreline; please maintain a safe distance from boat channels, ramps, and the edges of the stone breakwaters. Dogs are only permitted in the designated area between the groynes at the western end; the entire stretch of Silver Beach is not an off-leash dog beach. If conditions—such as strong waves or poor water quality—are unfavorable, please remain on the public paths or the shoreline to enjoy the scenery.

items.title: 悉尼公园
items.summary: 探索公园山坡、湿地周边与步行空间。
items.guide:
## 简介
Sydney Park的地形与工业历史密切相关。19世纪这里利用黏土制砖，后来旧采土坑又被用作垃圾填埋场，直到填埋结束后覆盖、整理和绿化，逐渐成为公园。保留的砖窑与烟囱，使过去的生产活动没有完全从景观中消失。

今天的山丘、湿地、公共艺术、步道和运动空间，把工业遗址与生态修复放在一起。湿地并非单纯装饰水池，也与城市雨水处理和环境改善有关；从砖窑看向水面与植物，再走到较高位置看城市轮廓，可以同时理解人工地形、工业记忆与当代公共绿地的关系。
## 这样逛
1. 先选最方便的入口：想看湿地可接近Campbell Street一侧，想看砖窑外观或游乐区可接近Barwon Park Road一侧。进园看指示图，只选这次有体力完成的一段。
2. 沿湿地公共路径观察水鸟、芦苇与雨水回收景观，找到Water Falls环境艺术附近的开放视角；保持在步道上，不靠近巢穴或进入水体。
3. 再沿开放路径上到一处缓坡看城市与绿地的层次，或回到历史砖窑外围看建筑外观；最后找树荫休息。砖窑、运动场和自行车中心有边界，不进封闭内部。
## 时间怎么用
60分钟选湿地或山坡其中一段；120分钟可连接两段、观察鸟类并休息。44公顷场地较大，走到半程就核对回程，不把所有设施都排进一次短逛。 夜间也可沿可通行的公共步道或建筑外侧散步，挑能看清台阶与路面的路线往返；室内、泳池、活动区域和园内设施按各自开放安排。
## 怎么去与花费
地址参考Sydney Park Road, Alexandria；St Peters站一带适合部分入口，其他公交可接近Euston/Campbell路侧，按具体入口导航。停车、课程和餐饮独立安排。
## 附近餐饮
园内咖啡点按当天营业选择，离园后可向St Peters或Newtown方向用餐。场地较大，带水比临时找售卖点实用；在中途安排短休息，再决定是否连接下一段步道。
items.tips: 广泛区域允许狗脱绳，但湿地、运动场、游乐、烧烤与骑行中心等有禁入规则。共享路径注意骑行者，砖窑和湿地区域按围挡走；带水、防晒，不喂鸟、不涉水。

en.title: Sydney Park
en.summary: Explore the park’s hillsides, the areas surrounding the wetlands, and the various walking paths.
en.guide:
## Introduction
The topography of Sydney Park is deeply intertwined with its industrial history. In the 19th century, the site was used for brickmaking, with the clay pits later serving as a landfill. Following the closure of the landfill, the area was capped, landscaped, and revegetated, gradually evolving into a park. The preserved brick kilns and chimneys ensure that the site’s former industrial activities have not vanished entirely from the landscape.

Today, the park’s hills, wetlands, public art, walking trails, and sports facilities integrate industrial heritage with ecological restoration. The wetlands are more than just decorative ponds; they play a functional role in urban stormwater management and environmental improvement. By taking in the view of the water and vegetation from the brick kilns, and then moving to higher ground to observe the city skyline, visitors can gain a nuanced understanding of the interplay between the man-made terrain, industrial legacy, and contemporary public green space.
## How to explore
1. Choose the most convenient entrance: Access the park from the Campbell Street side to visit the wetlands, or from the Barwon Park Road side to view the brick kilns or the playground. Once inside, consult the park map and select a route that suits your current energy level.
2. Follow the public paths around the wetlands to observe waterbirds, reeds, and the stormwater harvesting landscape. Seek out open vantage points near the "Water Falls" environmental art installation. Please remain on the designated paths; do not approach nesting areas or enter the water.
3. Continue along the open paths to a gentle slope for a view of the city skyline layered against the greenery, or explore the exterior of the historic brick kilns. Finally, find a spot in the shade to rest. Please note that the brick kilns, sports fields, and cycling center have defined boundaries—do not enter the enclosed interior spaces.
## Timing
A 60-minute visit allows for exploring either the wetlands or the hillside; a 120-minute visit provides enough time to cover both areas, observe birdlife, and take a break. Spanning 44 hectares, the park is quite large—check your return route halfway through your visit, and avoid trying to cover every single facility in a single short trip. Evening visits use public paths and building exteriors where you can see the surface and steps clearly. Interiors, pools, event zones and other facilities retain their own access arrangements.
## Getting there and costs
Location reference: Sydney Park Road, Alexandria. The area near St Peters Station offers convenient access to several entrances, while other entry points can be reached via bus routes along Euston Road or Campbell Street; please navigate to your specific chosen entrance. Parking, organized classes, and dining options should be planned independently.
## Nearby food
Check the daily operating hours for the café within the park; alternatively, you can head toward St Peters or Newtown for a meal after leaving. As the park is quite expansive, it is more practical to bring your own water than to rely on finding a vendor on the spot. Consider taking a short break along the way before deciding whether to continue onto the next section of the walking trail.
en.tips: Dogs are permitted off-leash in many parts of the park, though they are restricted from areas such as the wetlands, sports fields, playgrounds, barbecue zones, and cycling facilities. On shared paths, please be mindful of cyclists. Follow the designated fencing around the brick kilns and wetland areas. Remember to bring water and sun protection; please do not feed the birds or enter the water.

items.title: 格里布集市
items.summary: 周六在学校场地逛独立摊位，包含服饰、手作和餐饮选择。
items.guide:
## 简介
Glebe Markets设在Glebe Public School的校园场地，逢周六把日常学校空间转为临时市集。它的内容不是固定商场式柜台，而是由复古衣物、独立时装、首饰、手作、旧物、现场音乐与食品摊位共同组成；到访的趣味来自当日摊主与货品的组合。

这里与Glebe的街区气质相连：离开摊位便是Glebe Point Road上的商店与餐饮，而市集内部又有更慢的翻找和交流节奏。旧衣和二手物件适合仔细看材质与使用痕迹，手作品则可以听摊主解释做法；不一定购买，也能把它当作一次观察本地创作与周末生活的散步。
## 这样逛
1. 周六到 Glebe Public School 的集市入口，先不急着买，顺主要摊位通道走一圈，比较复古衣物、独立设计与手作摊的选择。
2. 找到感兴趣的摊位后问清尺寸、材质、退换和支付方式；二手商品逐件看状态，别把所有摊位当成统一经营的商店。
3. 到餐食区域看当日摊牌，按食量选一份现售食物；若当天有现场音乐且草地开放，可坐下听一会儿，再回最喜欢的一两个摊位。
## 时间怎么用
60分钟逛一圈加一次小吃；120分钟可慢试衣物、听音乐并休息。当前运营方公布周六10:00–16:00；非集市时间是学校场地，不作为日常自由参观地点。
## 怎么去与花费
46–56 Glebe Point Road，可乘沿 Glebe Point Road 的公交，或按地图由轻轨步行。逛摊、购物和吃饭分开安排，购物与餐饮另计。
## 参观要点
看旧衣先确认尺寸、缝线、拉链和明显污损，再询问退换方式；看手作可问材料与保养。支付方式由摊主决定，备好常用付款方式与一个可重复使用的袋子，会比看到东西后再临时找包装方便。
## 附近餐饮
市集里的食品摊适合边逛边看，先问清份量、计价和过敏原，再挑一份现做的小吃。想坐下来吃正餐，可离场后沿Glebe Point Road找店；用餐后收好包装，在场地允许的位置停留。
items.tips: 带可重复使用的袋子、水与防晒。先问支付方式，不假定每摊只收现金或都能刷卡。人多时注意背包，给通道留空间；下雨或活动变更时以运营方当天通知为准。旧平台“永久关闭”的历史条目不是当前运营场次的依据。

en.title: Glebe Markets
en.summary: On Saturdays, the school grounds host a variety of independent stalls, featuring clothing, handmade goods, and food options.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Glebe Markets are held on the grounds of Glebe Public School, transforming the school space into a temporary market every Saturday. Unlike a conventional shopping mall with fixed storefronts, this market features a diverse mix of vintage clothing, independent fashion, jewelry, handmade goods, second-hand items, live music, and food stalls. Part of the charm lies in the unique combination of vendors and products present on any given day.

The market’s atmosphere is deeply connected to the character of the surrounding Glebe neighborhood—step outside, and you’ll find yourself among the shops and eateries of Glebe Point Road, while inside the market, the pace slows down, inviting you to browse and engage. Take your time examining the materials and signs of wear on vintage or second-hand pieces, or chat with makers about their craft. You don’t have to buy anything; simply enjoy a stroll while observing local creative work and weekend life.
## How to explore
1. Upon arriving at the market entrance at Glebe Public School on a Saturday, take a full lap along the main aisles before making any purchases. Compare the offerings across vintage clothing, independent designs, and handmade goods.
2. Once you find a stall that interests you, clarify details such as sizing, materials, return/exchange policies, and payment methods. When looking at second-hand items, inspect each piece individually—remember that the market is a collection of independent vendors, not a single, unified retail store. 3. Head to the food area to check the day’s offerings and choose a snack or meal based on your appetite. If there’s live music and the lawn is open, feel free to sit and enjoy the performance before circling back to your favorite stalls.
## Timing
A quick browse and a snack will take about 60 minutes; a more leisurely visit—including trying on clothes, listening to music, and taking a break—could take 120 minutes. The current organizers host the market on Saturdays from 10:00 to 16:00. Outside of market hours, the site functions as school grounds and is not open for general public access.
## Getting there and costs
Located at 46–56 Glebe Point Road. You can reach it by bus (along Glebe Point Road) or by walking from the light rail station (refer to a map). It’s best to plan your browsing, shopping, and dining as separate activities, keeping in mind that shopping and food expenses are handled individually.
## Highlights
When looking at vintage clothing, check the size, seams, zippers, and for any visible stains or damage; also, ask about the return or exchange policy. For handmade items, feel free to inquire about the materials used and how to care for them. Payment methods are determined by individual stallholders, so it’s wise to have a few payment options ready. Bringing your own reusable bag is also much more convenient than scrambling for packaging after making a purchase.
## Nearby food
The food stalls are perfect for grabbing a bite while you explore. Be sure to ask about portion sizes, pricing, and potential allergens before selecting a freshly prepared snack. If you’d prefer a sit-down meal, you can head out to Glebe Point Road, where there are plenty of restaurants. Afterward, please dispose of your packaging properly and relax in any designated areas on-site.
en.tips: Bring a reusable bag, water, and sun protection. Always check the accepted payment methods—don’t assume every stall is cash-only or that all accept cards. When it’s crowded, keep an eye on your belongings and be mindful of leaving space in the walkways. In the event of rain or changes to the schedule, follow the latest updates provided by the organizers. Please note that any online listings stating the market is "permanently closed" are outdated and do not reflect the current event schedule.

items.title: 巴尔莫勒尔海滩
items.summary: 沿The Esplanade看沙滩、1920年代海滨建筑与Rocky Point，在港湾边慢慢停留。
items.guide:
## 简介
Balmoral位于Mosman面向Middle Harbour的一侧，海滩沿The Esplanade展开，Rocky Point把相连岸线分出不同的空间尺度。后方的公共绿地、步道与餐饮紧贴水边，既可以走一小段，也可以在树下坐着看港湾。它是一处海港海滩，和外海冲浪面在风浪、船只活动与周边街景上都有不同特点。

建于1920年代末的Bathers’ Pavilion是这里最醒目的历史建筑之一，浅色外墙、拱券和屋顶轮廓保留了海滨公共浴场时代的气质。如今建筑加入餐饮用途，普通游客从公共岸线就能看它的外观；附近圆形亭、Rocky Point连接桥与后方绿地，又把建筑、步行和观海结合起来。到访可以围绕这些公开空间完成，不必预订高档餐厅或参加水上活动，仍能看见悉尼海滨休闲文化的层次。
## 这样逛
1. 从The Esplanade靠Mandalong Road一带公共空间开始，先看Bathers’ Pavilion外立面与海滩方向。沿人行道比较建筑拱窗、色彩和海湾背景，不进入餐厅专用席位或服务区拍照。
2. 沿开放海滨步道向Rocky Point附近走，桥与台阶开放且条件合适时可上公共观景点看两侧岸线。精力少就留在海滩后方步道，碰到湿滑岩面不继续往外走。
3. 回公共绿地吃一份简餐或买咖啡，再沿同一段岸线慢慢返回。想多看一点可往南端浴场外侧步道走，但不需要同时覆盖Edwards Beach和整个Mosman海港长线。
## 时间怎么用
60分钟可看Pavilion、步道与Rocky Point附近；120分钟适合慢看建筑、吃饭并在绿地休息。午间餐饮较忙，先走一段再决定坐席或外带；傍晚回程公交和上坡步行另留时间。 夜间以岸边散步、听海和休息为主，沿入口附近能看清路面的公共路径往返；不下水、不走礁石、崖边或无照明的延伸山径。救生巡逻、浴场设施和停车场有各自时间，不能把可到岸边等同于有人巡逻或可夜泳。
## 怎么去与花费
导航Balmoral Beach, The Esplanade, Mosman，公共到访可从Mandalong Road周边接入。公交到海滩附近或从Mosman商业区转乘后步行，自驾沿The Esplanade及指定车场按表付费。普通公共岸线和小规模野餐无需预约，餐厅订位、停车、餐饮及活动费用另计。
## 附近餐饮
想轻松一点可买鱼薯、三明治或咖啡在允许休息的公共位置用餐；Bathers’ Pavilion等坐席餐厅是额外选择，不是看建筑所必需。外带先找好座位，食物收好防海鸥，避免在桥上边吃边走。
items.tips: Rocky Point有台阶，行动不便者可只走公开海滨步道；与船艇、潮位和湿滑边缘保持距离，不进海军设施或围挡区域。宠物和活动按现场市政标识安排。

en.title: Balmoral Beach
en.summary: Stroll along The Esplanade to take in the beach, the 1920s seaside architecture, and Rocky Point—take your time to linger by the harbor.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Balmoral is situated on the Middle Harbour side of Mosman. The beach stretches along The Esplanade, with Rocky Point punctuating the coastline and creating distinct spatial zones. Behind the beach, public green spaces, walking paths, and dining venues hug the water’s edge—perfect for a short stroll or simply sitting under the trees to gaze out over the harbour. As a harbour beach, it differs from the ocean-facing surf beaches in terms of wave conditions, boat traffic, and the character of the surrounding streetscape.

The Bathers’ Pavilion, built in the late 1920s, stands out as one of the area’s most prominent historic structures. Its light-coloured exterior, arched features, and roofline evoke the spirit of the era when public seaside bathhouses were in their prime. Today, the building houses dining establishments; visitors can admire its exterior from the public shoreline. Nearby features—such as the rotunda, the footbridge connecting to Rocky Point, and the adjacent green spaces—seamlessly integrate architecture, pedestrian pathways, and harbour views. You can fully experience this location by exploring these public areas; there is no need to book a table at an upscale restaurant or engage in water sports to appreciate the multi-layered nature of Sydney’s seaside leisure culture.
## How to explore
1. Begin in the public space along The Esplanade, near Mandalong Road, to take in the facade of the Bathers’ Pavilion and its orientation toward the beach. As you walk along the path, observe the building’s arched windows and colour palette against the backdrop of the harbour—please be mindful not to enter areas reserved for restaurant patrons or staff.
2. Follow the open waterfront path toward Rocky Point. If the bridge and steps are accessible and conditions are safe, you can head up to the public vantage point for views along the coastline. If you prefer a less strenuous route, stay on the path behind the beach; avoid venturing further if you encounter slippery rock surfaces.
3. Return to the public green space to enjoy a casual bite or a coffee, then take a leisurely walk back along the same stretch of the shore. If you wish to explore a bit more, you can follow the path beyond the baths at the southern end—though there is no need to cover the entire stretch toward Edwards Beach or the full length of the Mosman harbourfront.
## Timing
A 60-minute visit allows time to see the Pavilion, the walking paths, and the area around Rocky Point; a 120-minute visit is ideal for a more leisurely exploration of the architecture, a meal, and some relaxation in the green spaces. Lunchtime can be busy, so consider walking a bit before deciding whether to dine in or grab takeaway. Also, remember to factor in extra time for your return bus journey or the uphill walk back. After dark this is a shore-side walk and a chance to sit and listen to the water. Stay on visible public paths close to the approach; do not swim, enter rock platforms or continue onto unlit cliffs or bush tracks. Lifeguard patrols, bathing facilities, toilets and car parks have separate hours; public shore access does not imply a patrolled swim or an open car park.
## Getting there and costs
Navigate to "Balmoral Beach, The Esplanade, Mosman." If arriving by public transport, you can access the area via Mandalong Road. Buses run near the beach, or you can take a bus from the Mosman commercial hub and walk the rest of the way. If driving, you can park along The Esplanade or in designated parking lots (paid parking applies). No reservations are required for general public access to the shoreline or for casual picnics; however, restaurant bookings, parking, food, and specific activities may incur additional costs.
## Nearby food
For a more relaxed experience, pick up some fish and chips, a sandwich, or a coffee and enjoy it in one of the designated public seating areas. Sit-down restaurants like the Bathers’ Pavilion are optional and not strictly necessary for appreciating the architecture. If you opt for takeaway, secure a seat first, keep your food covered to deter seagulls, and avoid eating while walking on the footbridge.
en.tips: Rocky Point features stairs; those with limited mobility may prefer to stick to the accessible coastal walking path. Please keep a safe distance from boats, the water’s edge (be mindful of tides and slippery surfaces), and avoid entering naval facilities or fenced-off areas. Follow local council signage regarding pets and permitted activities.

items.title: 萨里山图书馆
items.summary: 在Crown Street的公共图书馆阅读，观察建筑与街区。
items.guide:
## 简介
Surry Hills Library与社区中心位于Crown Street，建筑由FJMT设计。它把图书馆与社区活动空间组合在同一街区场所中，外部立面、内部采光和公共阅读区之间的关系，是除了书本之外值得观察的内容。

这里的多语言馆藏包括俄语资料与中文报纸，反映了公共图书馆对不同居民需求的回应。与大型研究图书馆相比，本馆更贴近日常：可以从一份报纸、一册小说或一个感兴趣的主题开始，坐下读一段，再透过建筑看街区生活如何继续在Crown Street展开。
## 这样逛
1. 到405 Crown Street先看图书馆与社区中心的建筑外观，再进公共阅读层，按现场导览确认可参观范围，不走入活动室或办公区。
2. 在书架选一本感兴趣的书或报纸，想看多语言资料可留意本馆的俄语馆藏与中文报纸，找到一个值得慢读的主题。
3. 在空闲阅览座位读一段，休息时再观察室内采光与Crown Street街景。离开后若想吃饭再看周边当日菜单，餐饮不作为图书馆推荐的一部分。
## 时间怎么用
30分钟看建筑并短读；90分钟可完成一段专注阅读。平日、周末和公共假日开放不同，不能按社区中心的其他活动时间推断图书馆开放。
## 怎么去与花费
地址405 Crown Street, Surry Hills，可由附近公交或Surry Hills轻轨后步行接近；实际路线按当前位置与地图确认。
## 附近餐饮
Crown Street沿线有咖啡和餐饮，离馆后可以就近选择简餐。若计划继续逛Surry Hills，先沿一个方向走，再在折返点用餐，避免在同一段路上反复往返。
items.tips: 馆内桌位和电脑需看现场余位，打印复制及房间使用按单独规则。拍照避免打扰读者，公共阅读不等于可随便进入会议空间；需要电梯或辅助设备时先问工作人员。

en.title: Surry Hills Library
en.summary: Read at the public library on Crown Street while observing the building and the surrounding neighborhood.
en.guide:
## Introduction
The Surry Hills Library and Community Centre, located on Crown Street, was designed by the architectural firm FJMT. It integrates a library with community activity spaces within a single urban block. Beyond the books themselves, the building’s exterior façade, the way natural light filters into the interior, and the design of the public reading areas are all well worth observing.

The library’s multilingual collection—which includes materials in Russian and Chinese-language newspapers—reflects how the public library caters to the diverse needs of its local residents. Unlike large research libraries, this branch offers a more everyday experience: you might start with a newspaper, a novel, or a topic that piques your interest—settle in for a bit of reading, and look out through the building’s architecture to watch life unfold along Crown Street.
## How to explore
1. Begin at 405 Crown Street by observing the exterior of the library and community center. Then, head to the public reading level; check the on-site signage to confirm which areas are open to the public, and please avoid entering activity rooms or staff offices.
2. Browse the shelves for a book or newspaper that catches your eye—if you’re looking for multilingual materials, keep an eye out for the Russian-language collection or Chinese-language newspapers—and find a subject worth lingering over.
3. Settle into an available seat to read, and take a moment to observe the natural light filtering into the space and the streetscape of Crown Street outside. If you’re looking for a meal afterward, feel free to check out the local dining options—though please note that these are not official recommendations from the library.
## Timing
Allow 30 minutes to take in the architecture and enjoy a brief read, or 90 minutes if you’d like to settle in for a focused reading session. Please note that opening hours vary between weekdays, weekends, and public holidays; do not assume the library’s hours based on the schedules of other activities held at the community center.
## Getting there and costs
Located at 405 Crown Street, Surry Hills, the library is accessible via nearby bus stops or the Surry Hills light rail, followed by a short walk. Please check your current location on a map to determine the best route.
## Nearby food
There are plenty of cafés and eateries along Crown Street, making it easy to grab a quick bite after your visit. If you plan to continue exploring Surry Hills, consider heading in one direction and stopping for a meal on your way back—this helps you avoid retracing your steps along the same stretch of road.
en.tips: Access to tables, computers, and other facilities depends on current availability; specific rules apply to printing, photocopying, and the use of designated rooms. Please ensure that taking photographs does not disturb other readers. Note that access to public reading areas does not grant entry to private meeting spaces. If you require the use of an elevator or other assistive equipment, please ask a member of the library staff.

items.title: 月亮公园与米尔森角海滨
items.summary: 从笑脸入口外走到桥下海滨，免费路线也能看见北岸的游乐与港口历史。
items.guide:
## 简介
Luna Park于1935年在海港大桥北端开放，标志性的笑脸入口和彩色游乐设施，成了悉尼面向海港的一张独特名片。场地此前与海港大桥施工设施有关，桥建成后转向游乐用途；它的装饰艺术风格、Coney Island等历史建筑和海岸位置，让这里不仅吸引坐游乐设施的人，也适合看建筑与城市风景。海港大桥南北两岸的公共空间因此形成有趣对照：一边是繁忙的Circular Quay，另一边是铁路、游乐园和可慢走的岸线。

游乐园不是每天以完全相同的内容运行。当前Luna Lite日提供较少项目，常见于非学校假期的周初，开放时间也较短；普通日、特别活动和游乐设施各有安排。本条的零预约体验放在Olympic Drive和Milsons Point公共海滨，从外部看笑脸及大桥，再沿海边走一段，不要求买游乐通票或进入园内。想坐项目的人可以在现场确认当日运营内容后加购，这样即使到访时园内项目减少，散步本身仍是一趟完整行程。
## 这样逛
1. 从Milsons Point站沿Alfred Street下到海边，先在公共区域看Luna Park笑脸与塔楼，拍照时让出园门和道路，不把排队通道当拍摄区。
2. 沿Olympic Drive与公共海滨步道走到大桥桥墩附近，比较桥的钢结构、北岸岸线与对岸歌剧院；留在开放公共区域，泳池、园内与施工围挡按各自入口管理。
3. 在海边找座位休息后沿同一路线回车站，或按码头当天船班离开。想进园加玩先看营业牌、Luna Lite范围与票价，不用旧攻略假定所有项目全天运行。
## 时间怎么用
60分钟完成笑脸外观与桥下海滨；90分钟可加坐下休息和Kirribilli一小段。游乐设施排队和园内体验另留时间，免费岸边散步不代表游乐园和设施开放。 夜间也可沿可通行的公共步道或建筑外侧散步，挑能看清台阶与路面的路线往返；室内、泳池、活动区域和园内设施按各自开放安排。
## 怎么去与花费
以Luna Park主入口外Olympic Drive为导航点。Milsons Point火车站步行下坡可达，码头有渡轮衔接。公共海滨免费，园内游乐、演出、餐饮与停车分别付费。
## 附近餐饮
Kirribilli村落和Milsons Point周边有咖啡简餐，先在站旁或村落用餐再下坡也方便；园内餐厅营业不作为免费步行的必要条件。
items.tips: 近水和车行路照看儿童，返站有上坡；园内项目可能有身高、健康和年龄条件，只有外观散步不需要满足游乐设施条件。

en.title: Luna Park and Milsons Point foreshore
en.summary: A walk from the area outside the "smiling face" entrance to the waterfront beneath the bridge offers a free way to experience the history of the northern shore’s amusement park and harbor.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Opened in 1935 at the northern end of the Harbour Bridge, Luna Park—with its iconic smiling-face entrance and colourful amusement rides—has become a distinctive landmark along Sydney’s harbourfront. The site was originally used for construction facilities for the Harbour Bridge before being repurposed for recreation. Its Art Deco style, historic structures (such as the Coney Island building), and prime waterfront location make it a destination that appeals not only to thrill-seekers but also to those who appreciate architecture and urban vistas. This creates an intriguing contrast between the public spaces on the northern and southern shores of the Harbour Bridge: on one side lies the bustling Circular Quay, while the other features a railway line, an amusement park, and a scenic, walkable shoreline.

The amusement park’s offerings vary from day to day. On "Luna Lite" days—typically early in the week outside of school holidays—fewer rides are operational, and the park’s opening hours are shorter. Regular days and special events feature different ride schedules. For a visit that requires no advance booking, you can head to Olympic Drive and the public waterfront at Milsons Point. From here, you can view the iconic smiling face and the Harbour Bridge, then take a stroll along the shore—all without needing to purchase a ride pass or enter the park itself. If you decide you’d like to go on some rides, you can check the day’s specific offerings on-site and purchase tickets accordingly. This ensures that even if the number of available rides is limited during your visit, the walk itself remains a rewarding and complete experience.
## How to explore
1. From Milsons Point Station, head down Alfred Street toward the waterfront. You can view the iconic smiling face and towers of Luna Park from the public area; please ensure you do not block park entrances, pathways, or queueing lines while taking photos.
2. Follow Olympic Drive and the public waterfront promenade toward the bridge pylons, where you can take in the steel structure of the bridge, the northern shoreline, and the Sydney Opera House across the water. Please remain within the designated public areas; the swimming pool, the park itself, and areas behind construction hoardings are subject to their own separate access rules.
3. After relaxing by the water, you can return to the station via the same route or depart by ferry from the nearby wharf. If you wish to enter the park for the rides, please check the current operating hours, the "Luna Lite" zone, and ticket prices—do not rely on outdated guides that may incorrectly assume all attractions are open all day.
## Timing
Allow 60 minutes to view the smiling face and the waterfront area beneath the bridge; 90 minutes will provide enough time to also sit and rest, or to explore a short stretch of the Kirribilli neighborhood. Time for rides and other in-park experiences should be planned separately; the availability of the free public walking area does not necessarily correspond to the park’s operating hours for attractions. Evening visits use public paths and building exteriors where you can see the surface and steps clearly. Interiors, pools, event zones and other facilities retain their own access arrangements.
## Getting there and costs
Use Olympic Drive—located just outside the main entrance of Luna Park—as your navigation waypoint. The area is accessible via a downhill walk from Milsons Point train station or by ferry. While the public waterfront is free to access, rides, shows, dining, and parking within the park require separate payment.
## Nearby food
There are various cafés and casual dining options in the Kirribilli village and around Milsons Point; it is often convenient to grab a bite near the station or in the village before heading down the hill. Please note that the operating status of restaurants inside the park is independent of access to the free public walking areas.
en.tips: Please keep a close eye on children near the water and roadways. Note that the return journey to the station involves an uphill walk. Certain rides within the park may have specific height, health, or age requirements; however, these restrictions do not apply if you are simply walking around the exterior of the park.

items.title: 尼尔森公园与鲨鱼海滩
items.summary: 在树荫、历史海滨建筑和小沙湾之间慢慢走，适合野餐看港景。
items.guide:
## 简介
Nielsen Park位于Vaucluse的悉尼海港岸边，公园草地、成熟树木和Shark Beach紧邻，是把野餐与海边散步放在一处的好选择。它原属于Greycliffe地产，1911年转为公共所有，后来成为Sydney Harbour National Park的一部分；海湾从私人地产边界转为公众休闲空间，是理解这里的重要背景。

沿岸可见历史海滨设施与1914年的售卖亭传统，公园内部还有Greycliffe House相关遗产空间。近年Shark Beach的海堤进行了重建，并于2024年12月重新开放。普通到访可看海堤、沙岸和树荫下的公共区域，历史宅邸内部、导览与餐饮则各有独立安排。
## 这样逛
1. 从Greycliffe Avenue或公园正式公共入口进入，先在草地看海湾与沙滩的位置。想野餐可先选允许停留的公共区域作为基地，轻装去海边；不必带着所有食物沿海堤来回走。
2. 沿开放海滨路径慢走，观察新海堤、沙滩与两侧岬角。到干燥沙岸换一个角度看港湾，海水较高或浪花碰到通道时就留在陆侧，不为拍照走到边缘岩石。
3. 回树荫下休息，再在公园公共路径看历史设施与建筑外观，随后从原入口结束。有余力可沿Hermitage Foreshore的正式开放段走到第一个观景处后折返；不用把整条海滨步道与Milk Beach都纳入这次野餐。
## 时间怎么用
60分钟适合海堤、沙岸和公园；120分钟可安排野餐、建筑外观与一小段公共步道。周末人多时给找座位和返回停车点留余量，日落前结束公园行程。
## 怎么去与花费
导航Nielsen Park, Greycliffe Avenue, Vaucluse，公交后沿公共人行连接进入。自驾使用周边合法车位，留意限时和出入口。个人公共区域到访无需预约，餐饮、停车及有组织导览另计，历史建筑内部不包含在普通散步范围。
## 附近餐饮
可自带野餐，也可看海滨售卖亭或餐饮场所当天营业菜单。只想看海时一份简单轻食足够，正式餐厅另留等位与用餐时间。草地上吃完先收好包装，再去沙滩，避免让海风把物品吹散。
items.tips: 国家公园遵守禁烟与宠物限制，不踩踏植被或采集海洋生物。树荫与沙岸条件不同，仍需带防晒和水。围网或海堤并不替代现场海况与巡逻安排，本次以岸上到访为主。

en.title: Nielsen Park & Shark Beach
en.summary: Stroll leisurely among the shaded trees, historic seaside structures, and small sandy coves—an ideal setting for a picnic while taking in views of the harbor.
en.guide:
## Introduction
Located on the shores of Sydney Harbour in Vaucluse, Nielsen Park features a combination of grassy lawns, mature trees, and Shark Beach—an ideal setting for a picnic paired with a seaside stroll. Originally part of the Greycliffe estate, the site transitioned to public ownership in 1911 and later became part of Sydney Harbour National Park. Understanding this evolution—from private estate to a public recreational space—is key to appreciating the area.

The coastline retains historic seaside infrastructure, including a traditional kiosk dating back to 1914, while the park grounds house heritage sites associated with Greycliffe House. The seawall at Shark Beach was recently reconstructed and reopened in December 2024. Visitors can explore the seawall, the sandy beach, and the shaded public areas; note that access to the interior of the historic residence, guided tours, and dining services are managed separately.
## How to explore
1. Enter via Greycliffe Avenue or the park’s main public entrance, and take in the view of the bay and beach from the lawns. If you plan to picnic, set up your base in a designated public area before heading to the water—there’s no need to carry all your food and belongings along the seawall.
2. Take a leisurely walk along the accessible coastal path to observe the new seawall, the beach, and the headlands on either side. You can also view the harbour from the dry sand; however, if the tide is high or waves are washing over the path, please stay on the landward side—do not venture onto the rocks at the water’s edge for the sake of a photo.
3. Return to the shade to relax, explore the historic facilities and the exterior of the heritage buildings, and then depart via your original entry point. If you have extra time, you might walk a short section of the Hermitage Foreshore track to the first lookout point before turning back—there is no need to attempt the entire coastal trail or continue all the way to Milk Beach during this visit.
## Timing
A 60-minute visit is sufficient to take in the seawall, the beach, and the park grounds; a 120-minute visit allows time for a picnic, viewing the historic architecture, and walking a short portion of the public coastal path. On weekends, when the park is busy, be sure to allow extra time for finding a spot and returning to your parking area. It is best to conclude your visit before sunset.
## Getting there and costs
Navigate to Nielsen Park, Greycliffe Avenue, Vaucluse; if arriving by public transport, follow the pedestrian pathways to enter. If driving, please use legal parking spaces in the vicinity, and be mindful of time limits and entry/exit points. No reservation is required for general public access to the grounds; however, dining, parking, and organized tours are separate services. Please note that the interiors of the historic buildings are not included in the general walking area.
## Nearby food
You are welcome to bring your own picnic, or check the daily menus at the seaside kiosks and dining venues. A light snack is perfect if you simply wish to enjoy the ocean view, while formal restaurants may require time for waiting and dining. If picnicking on the lawn, please pack up your trash before heading to the beach to prevent items from being scattered by the sea breeze.
en.tips: As this is a national park, smoking and pets are prohibited; please do not trample vegetation or collect marine life. Conditions vary between the shaded areas and the sandy shore, so be sure to bring sun protection and water. Fences or seawalls are not a substitute for awareness of current sea conditions or lifeguard/patrol arrangements; this visit is intended for the shoreline area only.

items.title: 澳洲遗产酒馆
items.summary: 在岩石区街角老酒馆看建筑、挑披萨，再慢慢坐一会儿。
items.guide:
## 简介
Australian Heritage Hotel坐落在Cumberland Street与Gloucester Street形成的街角，现建筑属于1914年前后的岩石区重建。此前使用Australian Hotel名称的酒馆曾在附近不同位置经营，因此店名、酒牌传统与眼前建筑的年代应分开理解。两条街道的地势差，让外部立面、入口和酒吧空间有不同高度；绕街角观察，比只在招牌下拍一张照更能看清这座建筑怎样适应不规则地块。

内部保留的装饰与传统酒馆尺度，是了解悉尼城市日常建筑的一部分；压花金属天花等细节值得抬头看。今天这里仍以澳洲啤酒、披萨及酒馆菜经营，不是一间需要逐件打卡的博物馆。坐下吃一顿，观察街角人流和老建筑的使用方式，就是完整的到访内容，不需要为了“体验澳洲”强迫自己喝酒或点某种特别肉类。
## 这样逛
1. 到100 Cumberland Street先绕公共街角看两个立面和地面高差，再由正常营业入口入内；台阶和转角人多时不要停在门口拍照。
2. 找到允许使用的座位后看天花、吧台与街窗等细节。想上屋顶先问工作人员；屋顶人数有限，普通到访不以一定坐到屋顶为前提。
3. 两人可先选一款披萨或一份主菜分享，再决定是否加小食；特殊肉类、奶酪、面团和酱料都先按个人饮食需要确认。吃完沿Cumberland Street原路返回，或走公共街道下到George Street。
## 时间怎么用
45分钟适合饮品与建筑短停；90–120分钟可慢慢吃饭。酒馆每日11时至午夜，厨房每日11–22时，22时以后不依赖点到完整正餐。普通walk-in受欢迎，想确保餐桌或屋顶位置可预订；楼上住宿和私人活动不在这段到访范围内。
## 怎么去与花费
地址100 Cumberland Street, The Rocks。Circular Quay可经George Street、Argyle Street和Argyle Stairs上来；Wynyard方向也能经York Street抵达。它与Glenmore位置很近，但本次只需选一家，不用连续点两轮餐食。餐饮按所点菜品、饮料和附加费分别计算，没有统一每人套餐上限；酒吧继续营业不等于所有厨房和空间仍开放。
## 附近餐饮
本店以披萨和澳洲啤酒选择出名，也可不喝酒，只吃正餐或选无酒精饮品。饮食限制向服务员说明；不把某款特色肉类或一整杯烈酒当作必点。若只想免费散步，可看外部街景再沿公共道路离开，坐进店内则遵循正常消费与座位安排。
items.tips: 晚间酒吧活动按成人场景安排，携带有效证件；未成年人随行先遵循店方许可与监护要求。老街有台阶和高差，穿好走的鞋，不进入客房、厨房或私人活动区。

en.title: The Australian Heritage Hotel
en.summary: A corner pub in The Rocks for historic interiors, pizza and a relaxed evening.
en.guide:
## Introduction
The Australian Heritage Hotel occupies the junction of Cumberland and Gloucester Streets. The present building belongs to the rebuilding of The Rocks around 1914; earlier pubs using the Australian Hotel name operated at other nearby sites. The age of a trading name or licence is therefore different from the age of the building in front of you. Its relationship to two streets at different levels is one of the most useful details to notice from outside.

Inside, traditional pub proportions and surviving decorative elements, including pressed-metal ceilings, make the building part of the everyday architectural history of Sydney. It remains a working pub rather than a museum. Pizza, Australian beer and conversation are its present-day activities. You do not need to try an unfamiliar meat or order alcohol to make the visit worthwhile; spending an unhurried hour in the room is already a complete experience.
## How to explore
1. Start at 100 Cumberland Street and look at both public street frontages before entering. Notice the change in level around the corner, while leaving doorways and steps clear for other visitors.
2. Ask for an available table and look up at the ceilings and across the bar and street windows. If you want the small rooftop area, ask staff about availability rather than assuming it is included in every walk-in visit.
3. Begin with one pizza or a main to share, then decide whether you need more. Check meat choices, cheese, dough and sauces against your dietary needs. Return along Cumberland Street, or use public streets down to George Street, when you are ready to leave.
## Timing
Allow 45 minutes for a drink and a look around, or 90–120 minutes for dinner. The bar trades 11:00–midnight daily; the kitchen is open 11:00–22:00. A late drink does not imply a late full meal. Walk-ins are welcome, while a booking is useful for a preferred table or rooftop position. Accommodation and private functions are outside this visit.
## Getting there and costs
The address is 100 Cumberland Street, The Rocks. From Circular Quay use George Street, Argyle Street and the Argyle Stairs; Wynyard offers an approach via York Street. There are gradients and steps in the area. Glenmore is nearby, but choose one venue rather than ordering two dinners. Food, drinks and applicable surcharges are paid separately; the menu does not create a fixed maximum cost for every visitor.
## Nearby food
Pizza and Australian beer are the best-known parts of the offering. A meal with a non-alcoholic drink is an equally practical choice. Tell staff about dietary restrictions before ordering, and do not treat a novelty topping as obligatory. A free exterior walk can end at the street; using indoor tables follows the venue’s normal service arrangements.
en.tips: For a late bar outing carry accepted ID. Follow the venue’s rules for any accompanied minors. Wear comfortable shoes for the old streets and keep out of guest rooms, kitchens and private event spaces.

items.title: 悉尼鱼市场（新址）
items.summary: 逛海鲜零售与现制餐饮，看看新市场的滨水建筑与公共空间。
items.guide:
## 简介
Sydney Fish Market长期连接新南威尔士州的海鲜贸易与市民餐桌。旧市场自1966年起在Pyrmont的Blackwattle Bay岸边运营，2026年迁入Glebe的1 Bridge Road新址，并于1月19日开放。今天这里同时承担批发、零售、餐饮和食品教育功能，并非只有面向游客的美食广场。

新建筑由3XN/GXN与BVN合作设计，ASPECT Studios参与景观与公共空间。波浪般起伏的大屋顶是最醒目的特征，同时承担遮阳、采光、太阳能与雨水收集等功能；室内交易空间与外部港湾步行空间相连，让看建筑、了解市场运作和吃一顿饭能在一次到访中完成。
## 这样逛
1. 到新址1 Bridge Road, Glebe，先看公共零售区的楼层与商户导览。这里是2026年的新市场，不要按旧 Bank Street 场地图寻找摊位。
2. 先比较两三家商户的展示与现售菜单，辨清生鲜称重、可即食熟食和需要自行烹饪的产品；问清单价单位、份量、加工与附加费，再点一份适合自己的餐食。
3. 如公共滨水座位开放，带餐食去允许用餐的位置慢慢吃，再沿公共滨水空间走一小段看新建筑。批发拍卖区、后台与烹饪课程不属于自由参观范围，需另查预约。
## 时间怎么用
60分钟看零售区、点一份餐食；120分钟可慢慢比较商户、用餐并看滨水空间。场地官方开放07:00–22:00，商户各自营业；以零售与用餐为主时，白天到访更方便。
## 怎么去与花费
新地址1 Bridge Road, Glebe NSW 2037。官方参考为L1 Wentworth Park站约400米、Glebe站约450米；按新地址导航，部分旧地图短链仍残留旧坐标。停车入口在 Bridge Road，收费与空位另查。餐食和停车另计。
## 参观要点
看建筑时先看屋顶轮廓，再到公共空间观察光线、柱网与水面的关系。想看市场运作，只去允许公众停留的观察位置；购物前先决定这次是现场吃一餐还是买原料，后者还要安排保冷和尽快返程。
## 附近餐饮
先在新市场零售区比较两三家当前菜单，分清熟食、可即食海鲜与需要带回家处理的生鲜。鱼薯、烤制海鲜或一份现做主食更适合轻装短停留；称重商品先问单价、重量与加工费，食物在允许用餐的座位区吃。
items.tips: 新市场地址为1 Bridge Road，按现场指引进场。吃海鲜先核对过敏原与熟食状态，不把冰台生鲜当作可直接食用；带走垃圾、不喂鸟。周末可能排队，先看菜单再排，课程与导览另行预约。

en.title: Sydney Fish Market
en.summary: Explore the seafood retail and prepared-food offerings, and take in the waterfront architecture and public spaces of this new market.
en.guide:
## Introduction
The Sydney Fish Market has long served as a vital link between the seafood trade in New South Wales and the tables of local residents. The original market, which operated on the shores of Blackwattle Bay in Pyrmont since 1966, relocated to a new site at 1 Bridge Road, Glebe, opening on January 19, 2026. Today, the facility serves multiple functions—including wholesale, retail, dining, and food education—extending well beyond a typical tourist-focused food court.

The new structure was designed by 3XN/GXN in collaboration with BVN, with ASPECT Studios overseeing the landscape and public spaces. Its most striking feature is the undulating, wave-like roof, which serves several purposes: providing shade, allowing for natural light, and facilitating solar energy and rainwater harvesting. The interior trading spaces are seamlessly connected to the harbor-side pedestrian walkways, allowing visitors to admire the architecture, gain insight into market operations, and enjoy a meal—all in a single visit.
## How to explore
1. Upon arriving at the new location—1 Bridge Road, Glebe—consult the floor plan and merchant directory for the public retail area. This is the new market (as of 2026); do not use maps from the old Bank Street site to locate stalls.
2. Compare the displays and current menus of two or three merchants. Distinguish between raw produce (sold by weight), ready-to-eat prepared foods, and items that require home preparation. Clarify unit pricing, portion sizes, and any additional charges for processing or extras before placing your order.
3. If the public waterfront seating area is open, take your meal there to enjoy at a leisurely pace, then stroll along the waterfront to view the new architecture. Please note that the wholesale auction area, back-of-house facilities, and cooking class spaces are not open to the general public; access to these areas requires a separate booking.
## Timing
Allow 60 minutes to explore the retail area and enjoy a meal, or 120 minutes if you wish to take your time comparing merchants, dining, and walking along the waterfront. The site is officially open from 07:00 to 22:00, though individual merchant operating hours may vary. A daytime visit is recommended if your primary goal is shopping or dining.
## Getting there and costs
The new address is 1 Bridge Road, Glebe, NSW 2037. It is located approximately 400 meters from the L1 Wentworth Park light rail stop and 450 meters from the Glebe stop. Please use the new address for navigation; be aware that some older online maps or links may still point to the former location. The vehicle entrance is on Bridge Road—please check separately for parking fees and availability. Meals and parking are not included in any market entry arrangements.
## Highlights
When viewing the architecture, start by observing the roofline, then explore the public spaces to see how light, the structural grid, and the waterfront interact. If you are interested in the market’s operations, please remain only in areas designated for public access. Before shopping, decide whether you intend to dine on-site or purchase raw ingredients—the latter will require you to bring a cooler and plan for a prompt return home.
## Nearby food
In the new market’s retail area, compare the current menus of two or three merchants, and be sure to distinguish between ready-to-eat prepared foods, ready-to-consume seafood, and raw ingredients that require preparation at home. For a quick, light visit, opt for fish and chips, grilled seafood, or a freshly prepared meal. If purchasing items by weight, be sure to clarify the unit price, total weight, and any preparation fees; please consume your food only in designated dining areas.
en.tips: The new market is located at 1 Bridge Road; please follow the on-site signage to enter. Before eating any seafood, check for potential allergens and ensure the food is fully cooked—do not assume that raw items displayed on ice are ready for immediate consumption. Please take your trash with you and do not feed the birds. Expect potential queues on weekends; it is a good idea to review the menu before joining a line. Workshops and guided tours require separate bookings.

items.summary: 看港湾、逛旧渔村街道，再按食量选择一份海滨简餐。
items.guide:
## 简介
Watsons Bay位于South Head半岛末端，西侧是港湾、码头和小沙岸，东侧则很快转为面向外海的高岸。它从旧渔村发展为悉尼人乘渡轮看海与吃海鲜的目的地，仍保留紧凑街道、低层房屋与公共公园相接的尺度。一下船就能接触村落生活，适合不想长途徒步的人。

Robertson Park把码头、Military Road和街区串在一起，海滨餐饮、公共浴场与航海历史又给这里增加了层次。Doyles等海鲜场所让鱼薯与港景成为常见的到访组合，但看海并不需要订一顿正式餐厅。本页安排港边、街道和一顿可自由选择的简餐，不把Camp Cove、The Gap与灯塔全部打包成必须完成的清单。
## 这样逛
1. 从Watsons Bay Wharf下船，先在码头旁公共路径看港湾与Robertson Park，认清回程登船的位置。离开前顺手看看下一段返程班次，之后先走公园而非立刻加入餐饮队伍。
2. 沿Robertson Park到Military Road附近公共街道慢走，观察低层房屋、街道和港湾之间的连接。若想看公共浴场，可走正式海滨公共路线到Watsons Bay Baths一带，从陆侧看围网、步道和船只，随后返回公园。
3. 回码头周边比较餐饮选择，想轻松可选外带鱼薯，想坐下再看餐厅菜单与等位。吃完在公共海滨休息后乘船或公交返回；如果还想加看其他景点，只选一个独立加项，不把返程时间全用在继续走路上。
## 时间怎么用
60分钟看港边、公园与一段街道；120分钟可加公共浴场观景和用餐。鱼薯排队、堂食与返程登船都需留时间。晚点回程也要先确认实际班次，夜间只走公共海滨与街道，渡轮和公交按各自班次。 夜间也可沿可通行的公共步道或建筑外侧散步，挑能看清台阶与路面的路线往返；室内、泳池、活动区域和园内设施按各自开放安排。
## 怎么去与花费
导航Watsons Bay或Robertson Park, Military Road。渡轮从Circular Quay到Watsons Bay后可直接进入海滨，公交也可抵达半岛；自驾车位有限，按限时与计费规则停车。公共街道与公园个人散步无需预约，海鲜、饮品、停车与交通自行安排。
## 附近餐饮
点鱼薯先分清外带窗口与正式堂食：前者适合短停，后者需要更多时间与预算。看清鱼类选择、配菜份量和套餐内容后再点，同行可按食量分食，不把“海边吃鱼薯”理解成必须买最大份。想清淡一点，也可挑三明治或咖啡。
items.tips: 餐饮多在海鸟活动范围内，吃东西时看好纸袋和食物，不投喂。过街走正式位置，码头排队给上下船乘客留路；海风大时在公园较稳妥的位置整理随身物品，不把手机靠在栏杆上。
